IcyDB Code Review
Code review · 29 September 2026

IcyDB Code Review

Byte-level durability is excellent. Query semantics, schema evolution and upgrade liveness are not ready for 1.0: five critical defects, all reproduced with failing tests.
Commit 994715134 · v0.261.167 crates · ~465k lines of Rust41 review areas · 150 agents28 findings retested with failing tests

Verdict

IcyDB is carefully engineered at the byte and protocol level. Every persisted and wire format is exactly version 1 with no legacy decoders. Decoders bound counts before allocating, carry depth limits, reject trailing bytes and re-encode to check canonical form. Journal fingerprints and cursor HMACs are checked before any semantic decode. Commit publication is compare-and-swap style, recovery is staged and idempotent, and production code has almost no unwrap, expect or panic. No reviewer found a decoder that accepts malformed bytes, and the commit protocol holds up for the states the engine produces itself. Caller-facing authorization (endpoint exposure, guards, lane separation) also holds up.

The serious defects sit where two parts of the engine have to agree on meaning. There are five critical issues, and each was reproduced with a failing test against commit 994715134. First, the planner strips the predicate from `pk >= a AND pk < b` while the executor treats the key range end as inclusive, so `DELETE ... WHERE id >= 2 AND id < 5` also deletes id 5. Second, migration staging and abort fold the live index overlay into the canonical index outside the journal protocol: rows disappear from indexed reads, and the next fold fails as store corruption and leaves startup permanently failed. Third, the unique re-check for a filtered unique index ignores the index predicate, so a committed batch can never be folded or replayed. Fourth, renaming a record member is published as metadata-only, but stored records are keyed by member name, so every existing row holding that record becomes unreadable. Fifth, moving or renaming a journaled store's Rust type is reported as store corruption and permanently bricks the database; reverting the code does not recover it.

After merging duplicates there are 35 distinct high-severity issues, and they follow a few patterns. Optimizations drop a predicate because an access path supposedly proves it, or the two-valued predicate lane and the three-valued expression lane disagree on NOT, NULL, ILIKE, CASE and missing nested paths. One authority is kept in two representations that drift apart: filtered-index predicates as name-based SQL text, record members by name, the Identity allocator by dense field id. Deterministic failures are persisted or retried forever with no escape hatch. Index key bytes do not follow value order for negative timestamps and some principals. Decimal arithmetic panics, saturates or overflows on ordinary inputs. The generic grouped path and index-ordered continuation have fallen behind the specialized paths.

The evidence base is weaker than the repository suggests. Every reproduced bug passes current CI. The Tier A SQLite and mutation oracle lanes match zero tests, the PocketIC durability, upgrade, migration and guard suites do not run on pull requests, and the MSRV job actually builds on the pinned 1.98.1 toolchain. Several fixes change persisted bytes (timestamp and principal key order, the primary-key suffix bound, Account canonicalization, typed filtered-index predicates, record members keyed by id). The pre-1.0 hard-cut policy allows that, so they should ship together in one format cut with an explicit index rebuild.

Reproduced with tests

Static findings were re-tested by writing focused tests in isolated worktrees and running them against the current code. A test was written to assert the correct behaviour, so a failing test confirms the bug.

FindingOutcomeEvidence
Decimal::checked_div panics on i128::MIN / -1 (integer division overflow), which callers can trigger through SQL arithmetic
reproduced
crates/icydb-schema/src/decimal/tests.rs::repro_checked_div_min_by_neg_one_does_not_panic
The test uses catch_unwind to run Decimal::checked_div and the `/` operator on (i128::MIN mantissa, -1). It also confirms that Decimal::from_str("-170141183460469231731.687303715884105728") yields mantissa i128::MIN at scale 18, so text/SQL input can produce that value. All three cases panic at arithmetic.rs:355 (`numerator / denominator`) with 'attempt to divide with overflow'. The test profile is [optimized], and i128 division overflow panics regardless of overflow-checks. The bug is wider than the finding says. The retry loop lowers target_scale from 18 toward 0; when lhs.scale - rhs.scale is between 0 and 18 it reaches exponent 0, where numerator=i128::MIN and denominator=-1. So plain Decimal::from(i128::MIN) / Decimal::from(-1), both at scale 0, also traps. That value is the text "-170141183460469231731687303715884105728". The checked_div entry point that core SQL Div uses (crates/icydb-core/src/db/numeric/mod.rs:82, confirmed by grep) panics instead of returning None. That violates QUERY_PRACTICE.md:325, 'Evaluation must never panic'. The SQL end-to-end path through core was not executed; the Decimal-level panic was.
Decimal multiplication does not normalize its operands, so fixed-scale (e.g. e18) decimal fields overflow on tiny products like 20 × 20
reproduced
crates/icydb-schema/src/decimal/tests.rs::repro_checked_mul_padded_fixed_scale_operands
The test builds 20 as Decimal::from_i128_with_scale(20*10^18, 18), the padded form an e18 field holds after admission. It compares equal to Decimal::new(20,0). Multiplying the normalized operands gives Some(400). The padded operands give checked_mul = None, because checked_mul_impl (arithmetic.rs:51-55) multiplies the raw mantissas, 2e19*2e19=4e38 > i128::MAX, before stripping trailing zeros. Core SQL Mul maps that None to NumericEvalError::Overflow (numeric/mod.rs:76, confirmed by grep). The test also shows more than the finding states: the `*` operator on the same operands returns 17014118346.04... (i128::MAX at scale 28), not 400, so typed newtype arithmetic silently produces a wrong value. The claims that admission pads values and that persisted decode keeps the padding were not exercised here; they are core-side.
Decimal `Mul`/`MulAssign`/`Product`/`powu` return ~±1.7e10 when the exact product needs >28 fractional digits
reproduced
crates/icydb-schema/src/decimal/tests.rs::repro_mul_scale_overflow_rounds_instead_of_saturating
Every predicted case fails as described. Mul, and powu which is built on it, returns saturating_extreme(28, false), i.e. i128::MAX at scale 28 ≈ 1.7e10, whenever the exact product scale exceeds 28 and the mantissa cannot be reduced by stripping zeros. checked_mul and checked_powu return None for the same small results, including POWER(1.1, 30) ≈ 17.449, where SQL would report Overflow. Cause: checked_from_mantissa_scale (mod.rs) returns None when scale > 28 and the mantissa has non-zero low digits, and the Mul impl (arithmetic.rs:403-410) falls back to saturating_mul. The newtype derive path (E18s and similar) was not exercised directly; the literal 1.123456789012345678 stands in for E18s.
Decimal Add/Sub/Div saturate at the wrong scale when scale alignment overflows, returning values smaller than the dominant operand
reproduced
crates/icydb-schema/src/decimal/tests.rs::repro_saturating_add_div_are_monotonic_on_alignment_overflow
All three predicted values match exactly. When scale alignment overflows, saturating_add (arithmetic.rs:208-227) saturates at the target scale, so 1e21+1e-18 gives about 1.7e20 and 1e30+1e-28 gives about 1.7e10, both smaller than the left operand. The Div impl (arithmetic.rs:435-447) saturates at DEFAULT_DIVISION_SCALE=18, so a true magnitude overflow such as 1e37/1e-28 gives about 1.7e20, smaller than the dividend. The existing proptest decimal_add_saturation_boundary_property only checks that the mantissa is MAX/MIN/0, so it does not catch this.
Decimal `Rem` returns ZERO on scale-alignment overflow, so the MultipleOf application validator accepts non-multiples
reproduced
crates/icydb-schema/src/decimal/tests.rs::repro_multiple_of_rejects_non_multiple_on_rem_alignment_overflow
Reproduced at two levels. (1) In icydb-schema, 5.0000000000000000000000000001 (scale 28) % 10_000_000_000_000 gives checked_rem=None and Rem=0. Aligning the divisor to scale 28 overflows i128 (1e41) in checked_rem_impl (arithmetic.rs:84-97), and the Rem impl (arithmetic.rs:456-462) turns None into ZERO. The exact remainder is the dividend itself, which is representable. (2) End to end in icydb-model, MultipleOf::new(10_000_000_000_000u64).validate(&that_value) records no issue, so it accepts a non-multiple (num.rs:123, `!(v % self.target).is_zero()`). Separately, core SQL Rem (numeric/mod.rs, checked_rem → Overflow) reports a spurious overflow for this representable result; that path was noted from grep, not run.
Filtered (partial) unique index: conflict re-check ignores the index predicate, so a committed batch cannot be folded or replayed (wedge risk)
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application/tests/storage_evolution_repro.rs::repro_filtered_unique_handoff_batch_folds_online_demote_first;
The fixture is a journaled store (ABORT_REGISTRY) whose entity is published through apply_schema. Entity Membership{id, account_id, is_primary: bool} has a unique index on account_id with predicate `is_primary = true`. A {acct 7, primary} is inserted and folded into canonical state. Then a single dynamic batch runs. (1) Batch order [demote A, insert B]: the write commits, but the online watchdog fold fails with code 210 RUNTIME_BOUNDARY_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION. Its facts are ConstraintKind(61)=5 (Unique) and ConstraintContext(62)=3. A retry fails the same way, so the oldest batch is wedged. (2) Same batch, recovered through forget_recovered_domain_for_tests plus startup recovery: the same unique violation, so recovery never completes. (3) Batch order [insert B, demote A]: falsely rejected at write time with the same unique violation. Control: [delete A, insert B], where the final row is absent, commits and folds fine. This isolates the cause to the predicate-blind rebuild of the conflicting row's key in UniqueKeyAuthority::build_index_key_from_row_slots (unique.rs:50-74), which never evaluates predicate_sql. It is reached through prepare_row_commit_batch_for_replay / CanonicalCommitReader during fold.
Scalar fast path reports corruption for rows filled by a non-null historical default (ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT)
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/write/identity_pre_key_tests/storage_evolution_repro_tests.rs::repro_historical_default_fill_is_visible_to_scalar_predicates;
Two rows are inserted into IdentityRow (identity_pre_key_tests heap fixture). Then `ALTER TABLE IdentityRow ... ADD COLUMN score nat64 NOT NULL DEFAULT 7` (or `note text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'abc'`) runs through session.execute_admin_sql_ddl, which publishes metadata-only and leaves the rows at the older layout. Works: materialized projection, which returns the fill. Fails: WHERE score = 7 and OCTET_LENGTH(note), both with RUNTIME_CORRUPTION (code 17). Control: after rewriting both rows with an UPDATE, which stamps the current layout, the same WHERE returns both rows. The failure is therefore specific to historically-absent slots whose fill is SlotPayload. This matches get_scalar / required_accepted_value_storage_scalar returning persisted_row_decode_corruption for any non-Null historical value (structural_slot_reader.rs ~494-503, 590). Direct projection of CatalogValue scalars was not tested separately.
Value-storage walker misreads canonical enum envelopes (tag 0x84), so nested record-path reads fail for records that contain an enum
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/data/structural_field/value_storage/canonical.rs::repro_value_storage_view_walks_canonical_record_map_with_enum_member;
Unit test: decode_canonical_value_storage_bytes accepts a canonical Map {score: Nat64, status: enum}, but ValueStorageView::from_raw_validated rejects the same bytes with FieldDecodeError. The walker treats 0x84 as a 'nested frame' tag and skips only one byte, so the 00 byte of type_id parses as TAG_NULL. End to end: Player{profile: Profile{score: nat64, status: Status enum}} is published through apply_schema on a journaled store. The whole-record projection works. WHERE profile.score, projection of profile.score and GROUP BY profile.score all fail with RUNTIME_CORRUPTION on every row. This matches skip.rs:52-54 and tags.rs:42-49.
Record-member rename is metadata-only, but stored record values use member names as keys, so every existing row with that record becomes undecodable
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application/tests/storage_evolution_repro.rs::repro_record_member_rename_keeps_existing_rows_readable_and_writable
Fixture: MIGRATION_EXECUTION_REGISTRY (journaled, migration feature). Item{id, profile: Profile{nickname: Text(64), owner_id: Nat64}} at v1, with two rows inserted and folded. The v2 proposal renames the record member via SchemaMigrationRename::RecordField{Profile, nickname -> label} with no transforms. migrate_schema Advance publishes it in a single step (phase Applied), i.e. metadata-only with no row validation or rewrite. Afterwards, reading the existing rows fails with RUNTIME_CORRUPTION (17), and UPDATE and DELETE of pre-rename rows fail with 17 as well. This confirms that stored record maps keyed by the old member name no longer admit against the renamed composite catalog.
Online background folding routes batches through the LIVE accepted catalog, so a metadata-only entity rename published with retained debt makes older batches permanently unfoldable
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application/tests/entity_rename.rs::repro_online_fold_routes_retained_batches_after_relation_free_entity_rename;
Rows are inserted into 'Item'; their RowPut batches stay in the journal tail as retained debt (verified by walking next_batch_after from the fold watermark). A metadata-only entity rename Item -> CatalogItem is then published via migrate_schema Advance (Applied). Online convergence (continue_recovery on a recovered domain with no marker) is then driven without forget_recovered_domain_for_tests. Relation-free entity: the fold fails with code 15 STORE_CORRUPTION (Corruption/Store), and a retry fails identically, i.e. the fold is wedged. This matches the predicted failure in journal_batch_store_handle -> recovery_accepted_runtime_entity_for_path resolving 'Item' against the live catalog (recovery.rs:2343-2352). Existing self-relation fixture: the fold fails earlier with code 22 RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED (Unsupported/Store). This is consistent with the finding's secondary concern that relation projection binding resolves the target path through the live catalog. The exact failing call was not instrumented. Control: the same retained debt folds fine through the startup path, which resets overlays first. The bug is therefore specific to the online (live-projection) fold. The downstream consequences (terminal classification or startup failure receipt, Gate 2 backlog rejection) were not exercised.
Two-sided PK range `pk >= a AND pk < b` has its predicate stripped although KeyRange end is inclusive: the row with pk == b is returned, counted, updated or deleted
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_sql_semantics.rs::repro_two_sided_primary_key_range_excludes_exclusive_upper_bound
PlannerRow fixture (Nat64 PK, ids 0..12). `id >= 2 AND id < 5` picks KeyRange{2,5}. EXPLAIN shows residual_filter=none: HalfOpenRange stripped the predicate, and the inclusive KeyRange end then returns id 5. This happens in the dynamic lane (paged to exhaustion), SQL SELECT and SQL COUNT(*) (4). SQL DELETE removed 4 rows, including id 5, which is silent data loss. Control `id > 1 AND id <= 4` keeps the residual predicate and returns [2,3,4]. I also tried a Text-PK variant, but the fixture could not insert rows into a hand-built Text-PK schema (error code 22 from both SQL and dynamic insert), so I dropped it. The strip logic compares Values and does not depend on the PK type.
The FALSE set of a SQL NOT is compiled as a two-valued predicate NOT, so rows where the inner comparison is UNKNOWN (NULL operand) pass
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_sql_semantics.rs::repro_not_compare_rejects_rows_with_null_operand
Custom schema: id Nat64 plus nullable Text status. Rows: 1 archived, 2 active, 3 NULL, 4 closed. `NOT (status='archived')` and `status NOT LIKE 'a%'` return NULL-status row 3 through the predicate lane. The same predicates with an uncompilable conjunct (`AND id + 0 = id`) go to the 3VL expression lane and exclude row 3, so the result depends on which lane is chosen. `status != 'archived'` (control) correctly excludes NULL. `DELETE ... WHERE NOT (status = 'active')` deleted 3 rows, including the NULL-status row. This matches wrap_truth_predicate building FALSE as Predicate::Not(when_true).
In expression-lane filters, a missing nested path aborts the whole row, so an OR with a true sibling still rejects it
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_sql_semantics.rs::repro_missing_nested_path_does_not_veto_true_or_sibling
End-to-end with an accepted composite catalog: a nullable `profile` Record{rank: Newtype(Nat64)} and nested leaf `rank`. Rows: 1 bob (profile NULL), 2 alice (rank 5), 3 carol (rank 7). The filter runs in the expression lane (residual_filter=expression). `name = 'bob' OR profile.rank = 5` drops bob although `name = 'bob'` alone returns [1]. `id = 1 OR profile.rank > 5` returns [3] instead of [1,3]. This matches evaluate_field_path returning Err(MissingFieldPathValue), which the filter wrapper turns into false for the whole row. Two sub-scenarios could not be tested. `profile IS NULL` on a composite root is rejected at planning (NonQueryableFieldType), so that example cannot be written. The absent-key case (profile present without rank) was not tested because the test composite's member is required. The core NULL-root veto is confirmed.
Rewriting a scalar-WHERE CASE into AND/OR drops CASE's lazy evaluation, so a CASE-guarded division errors on the rows it was meant to skip
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_sql_semantics.rs::repro_case_guarded_division_in_where_does_not_error
Custom schema: id plus Int64 qty and total. Rows: (1, qty 0, total 10), (2, 2, 20), (3, 5, 10). `WHERE CASE WHEN qty = 0 THEN FALSE ELSE total / qty > 5 END` fails with the same numeric-not-representable error code as an unguarded `total / qty`. The identical CASE works as a SELECT projection (lazy CASE). It also works in WHERE when there is no division, and when the qty=0 row is absent. So the error comes from dividing on the row the guard should skip. DELETE with the same WHERE fails the same way, and no rows were deleted.
ILIKE/LOWER text predicates mean different things in the expression and predicate lanes; resumable UPDATE uses the expression lane and silently updates the wrong set
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_sql_semantics.rs::repro_ilike_prefix_agrees_across_lanes_and_resumable_update
Journaled store with a custom schema: id, name Text, flagged Bool. Rows: alice, Alan, bob. `name ILIKE 'Al%'` returns [1,2] through the casefold predicate lane. Adding an OR branch that forces the expression lane returns []. Exact UPDATE flags rows [1,2]. After resetting, start_trusted_sql_mutation_job with the same UPDATE reaches Completed after a Forward and a Verify pass that each scanned 3 keys, with rows_updated_total=0 and no rows flagged. The job reports success after updating none of the rows the exact UPDATE matched.
SortRequiresMaterialization can never fire: the admission summary always reports materialized_sort=false, so public reads admit materialized ORDER BY
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_sql_semantics.rs::repro_public_read_rejects_materialized_sort_over_index_prefix
PlannerRow fixture. execute_public_live_page runs `rare = 'group-a' ORDER BY wide_branch LIMIT 5`; wide_branch is not the leading key of any index. The route reports load_order_route_reason=requires_materialized_sort, but the admission block shows materialized_sort=false. PublicRead admits the query and returns a page, so SortRequiresMaterialization never fires. This matches summary_from_plan always using QueryMaterializationSummary::none() and contradicts READ_ADMISSION.md ('Materialized ordering normally rejects').
PublicRead counts every secondary-index route as bounded, including the planner's unbounded whole-index fallback, so public pages can full-scan the table
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_sql_semantics.rs::repro_public_read_rejects_order_only_whole_index_scan
PlannerRow fixture, 64 rows, filter wide_branch='y' (not indexed as a leading key). With no ORDER BY, PublicRead rejects the query as UnboundedFullScanRejected. Adding ORDER BY common (a_common_idx) makes the planner pick a whole-index IndexRange with a residual predicate, and PublicRead admits it, both with LIMIT 1 and envelope-paged. Each resumed page visited all 64 rows, which fits the finding that later pages restart at the first index entry and scan to the end. The final page came back empty after 64 visits, and the sequence visited 1038 rows in total for 64 rows. One detail of the scenario did not hold: its example field wide_fixed (leading key of the composite b_wide_branch_idx) stays a FullScan and is rejected, because the (wide_fixed, wide_branch, pk) index order does not satisfy ORDER BY wide_fixed, id. The mechanism reproduces with the single-field index a_common_idx.
Generic hash GROUP BY 'DirectOwned' probe path never looks up existing groups: one group per row for enum/unit/collection/composite keys
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_exec_index.rs::repro_generic_grouped_owned_probe_merges_equal_keys
End-to-end through DbSession::execute_trusted_dynamic_grouped_query on a published accepted schema with no index, so hash grouping is used. Group key List(Nat64) with 3 rows = [7] and 1 row = [9]. COUNT(*) alone takes the dedicated count fold and returns the correct 2 groups (count 3 and 1). COUNT(*)+SUM(amount) takes the generic fold, whose DirectOwned probe (bundle.rs resolve_owned_group_index calls insert_new_group with no bucket lookup) returns 4 groups: every row is its own group. A Unit-typed key (3 identical rows) also gives 3 groups instead of 1. Enum keys were not tested because they need an enum catalog in the fixture. They go through the same DirectOwned path (dispatch.rs test borrowed_group_probe_requires_accepted_scalar_authority shows Enum is not borrowed-probe capable).
Unbounded generic grouped finalization ignores DESC: groups always come back in ascending key order
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_exec_index.rs::repro_generic_unbounded_grouped_desc_order
No-index schema with id/dept/salary. group_by(dept).aggregate(sum(salary)).order_by(desc(dept)).grouped_limits(8,16K) with no LIMIT uses finalize_unbounded, which goes through into_sorted_groups (always canonical ascending, bundle.rs:775-780). reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_exec_index.rs::repro_mixed_direction_group_key_order
GROUP BY region, year ORDER BY region ASC, year DESC LIMIT 10 (grouped_limits 16/16K, no index) is accepted by validation. Resumed secondary-order IN-list pages cap each branch at limit+1 with no resume anchor, silently dropping rows
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/repro_exec_index.rs::repro_in_list_secondary_order_resume_keeps_all_branch_rows
Default cardinality_tiebreak fixture with non-unique index z_rare_idx. Rows: rare='a' id 0, rare='b' ids 1..=8, rare='c' id 9. The test drains execute_trusted_live_page with continuations (the test build page size is 2, so fetch hint = 2+1 = 3). WHERE rare IN ('a','b','c') ORDER BY rare runs as IndexMultiLookup/secondary_order. Page 3 restarts branch 'b' from its beginning, capped at 3 keys, and all of those keys fall at or before the cursor boundary. Only 'c' remains, so has_more=false and ids 4..8 are silently dropped. The control, a contiguous range rare >= 'a' AND rare <= 'c' over the same data, returns all 10 rows.
Timestamp index components use unbiased two's-complement bytes, so negative timestamps sort after positive ones
partially reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/index/key/tests/ordered_semantics.rs::repro_timestamp_ordered_encoding_preserves_mixed_sign_order;
The core bug is real. Timestamp index components encode as raw two's-complement bytes, so 18 of 30 mixed-sign pairs have byte order opposite to value order. The lowered raw envelope for [-1000, 1000) is empty (envelope_is_empty=true), which matches the claimed mechanism. End to end (Timestamp field with a secondary index, rows at -1000 ms and +500 ms), ORDER BY born_at through IndexRange(born_at_idx) returns 500 before -1000. Across continuation pages it also emits row 2 twice ([2,1,2]), which breaks canonical order and cursor pagination. The finding's specific consequence 'the range query returns zero rows' and 'born_at < 0 misses every negative row' did NOT show at session level. Dynamic range queries, the SQL query with bound Timestamp params, and born_at < 0 all returned the correct row sets, only in wrong order, even though the planner chose IndexRange with bounds Included(-1000)..Excluded(1000). I did not trace why execution does not honor the empty lowered envelope, so the zero-row sub-claim is unconfirmed; the ordering and pagination consequences are confirmed.
Index keys cap the primary-key suffix at 63 bytes but composite PKs can encode up to 254 bytes, so inserts fail on indexed entities
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/index/key/codec/tests.rs::repro_index_key_accepts_full_width_composite_principal_primary_key;
Unit test: a (Principal[29], Principal[29]) composite PK encodes to 64 bytes through key taxonomy, and IndexKey::to_raw rejects it with SegmentTooLarge because MAX_PK_SIZE = 1 + Account::STORED_SIZE = 63. End to end: an accepted schema with PK [owner, spender] (both Principal) and a secondary index on label. The insert with 10-byte principals succeeds, but the insert with 29-byte principals fails with InvariantViolation/Index 'index diagnostic' (InternalError::index_invariant from commit preparation). The failure depends on the data, as the finding predicted.
Dense field-ID renumbering orphans the Identity allocator: removing a field that sorts before the PK restarts Identity::next at 1 (reuse on empty entities; permanent insert failure and integrity corruption after a physical migration)
partially reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application/tests/repro_r2.rs::repro_identity_online_field_removal_never_reissues_committed_values
The online path is reproduced as described. Entity JournalEntry {archived: Bool, id: Nat64 Generated}: `archived` sorts first, so `id` is FieldId 2. The test inserted 3 rows (ids 1..3), deleted them all, brought cardinality to Ready, and called apply_schema with SchemaRemoval::Field{archived}. Dense removal renumbered `id` to FieldId 1. prepare_identity_state_transition (identity_state.rs:609-633) retired (tag,2) with high_water 3 and created a new Active (tag,1) at high_water 0. The next insert then got id 1 again, which breaks IDENTITY_CONTRACT's rule that committed values are never reused. It also leaves an extra Retired record that counts against the cap. The physical-migration scenario (a populated entity, then permanent insert failure and HighWaterExceeded) could not be reached. The migration fails first, at the Validating page: validate_migration_page returns STORE_INVARIANT_VIOLATION (16@12). This is not caused by Identity. The same error appears with a caller-supplied PK, and when only a non-PK retained field is renumbered. It does not appear when the dense removal renumbers only the newly appended transform target (control-after, which also shows the high-water is kept when the FieldId does not move). So the documented CheckedCast+SchemaRemoval pattern cannot currently remove a field that sorts before any retained pre-existing field. That is a separate defect. A likely cause (not confirmed): compile_entity_program matches preserved slots by FieldId equality between the before and candidate snapshots (migration_transform.rs ~430-440), which breaks after dense renumbering. The Identity root cause (a transition keyed only by (entity_tag, field_id)) is confirmed, and the physical path would hit it once that validation defect is fixed. Verdict: partially_reproduced, because the critical 'permanent insert failure after physical migration' consequence is unreachable today, while online reissue of committed values is proven.
Migration staging/abort folds the live overlay into canonical outside the journal protocol: durable prefix counts drift (rows vanish from indexed reads) and later folds wedge on count underflow
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application/tests/repro_r2.rs::repro_abort_from_prepared_keeps_index_prefix_counts_exact
Setup: a journaled store (MIGRATION_EXECUTION_REGISTRY) and entity Ticket {id, status, w_old} with a non-unique index on status. v1 is published, one row is seeded and folded, and cardinality is driven to Ready. Advance moves a physical migration (CheckedCast w_old->w_value, remove w_old) to Prepared. Ticket 2 (status 'fresh') is then inserted through ordinary session admission, which Prepared allows, and stays in the journal tail. Before Abort, the index query returns the row. After Abort-from-Prepared runs cleanup_migration_staging_page, index/store.rs fold_journaled_materialized_view moves the live entry into canonical and resets the prefix delta. The query now returns [] even though the row exists, because the exact prefix count is 0 and the scan is skipped. Folding the retained insert succeeds, but the row stays invisible (count never includes it). Deleting ticket 2 and folding that batch fails with STORE_CORRUPTION, matching the predicted checked_sub underflow. The generated watchdog (drive_generated_startup_recovery_page) then publishes a terminal JournalRecovery receipt, and observe_generated_startup_state returns Err, so the database is wedged. Every predicted step was observed.
Migration staging and abort fold the live index overlay into the canonical index without folding rows; retained batches then fail to fold with a corruption error and the database is wedged
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application/tests/repro_r2.rs::repro_abort_from_prepared_keeps_retained_update_foldable;
This is the same root cause as r2-cardinality-freshness-1, and these tests settle the dispute. A committed update of ticket 1 (status 'open' -> 'closed') is retained in the tail. Then a migration page calls fold_journaled_materialized_view, which moves the live overlay (tombstone for 'open', entry for 'closed') into the canonical index without folding the row. When the watchdog later folds the batch, it derives the old key ('open',1) from the canonical row, and the key is missing from the canonical index. validate_existing_old_index_membership then returns RUNTIME_CORRUPTION (17@4). The generated watchdog publishes a terminal JournalRecovery receipt, and observe returns Err, so the database is wedged. It fails in all three variants: (a) the update is written while the migration is Prepared, then Abort; (b) the update is written BEFORE any migration record exists (an ordinary write while startup is healthy), then Advance->Prepared and Abort. advance_metadata_schema_migration drains only when a prior record exists (application.rs ~1105-1116), so the batch is still retained. This removes the 'generated endpoints cannot write during Prepared' objection: all it needs is a controller Advance/Abort running before the next watchdog fold; (c) no abort at all: Advance through a Validating page that stages a candidate unique index (stage_migration_index_entries), then fold. Not tested: the claim that an upgrade/startup fold re-fails. The persisted receipt returned by observe() already shows the failure is durable.
Renaming or moving a journaled store's Rust type is treated as STORE_CORRUPTION and permanently bricks the canister; reverting does not clear it
reproduced
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application/tests/repro_r2.rs::repro_store_rust_path_rename_is_not_terminal_and_revert_recovers
This is a native approximation, not a PocketIC upgrade. Two StoreRegistry instances register the same journaled Data/Index/Schema/Journal stores with identical StoreAllocationIdentities (same memory ids and stable keys). They differ only in the Rust store path: 'app_schema::stores::TransferStore' versus 'app_schema::db::TransferStore'. Steps: publish the schema and write a row through the old registry, and drain. Simulate the upgrade by clearing recovery ownership (forget_recovered_domain_for_tests) and the volatile format-admission cache (I added a small #[cfg(test)] helper, forget_admitted_database_formats_for_tests, so convergence runs again). Run the generated watchdog through the new registry. Convergence accepts the moved registry because it matches allocation roles, not paths. Recovery then fails with STORE_CORRUPTION from the bundle.store_path() != registered path check (schema/store.rs:2269), and a terminal JournalRecovery receipt is persisted. After reverting to the original registry/path, observe() still returns the same Err and the driver stays Terminal, so the revert does not recover. The same-path control shows the reopen sequence itself is healthy, so the failure comes only from the path change. Limitation: the in-process heap store objects are reused instead of being rebuilt from stable memory after upgrade. The tail was drained first, so there was nothing to replay.
Hybrid covering fails valid SELECTs with an invariant error whenever a projected index component is anything other than Bool/Int/Nat(<=64)/Text/Ulid/Unit
reproduced

Both SQL SELECTs that project the Decimal index component together with a non-indexed column fail with a runtime invariant violation. This matches the predicted path: decode_covering_projection_component returns Ok(None) for the Decimal tag, and decode_hybrid_covering_components maps that to query_executor_invariant. The ORDER BY price variant fails the same way. The fluent DynamicQuery with the same projection and filter succeeds and returns both rows, so only the SQL projection facade, which reaches try_execute_prepared_covering_projection_rows_for_canister, is affected. 28 findings tested: 26 reproduced exactly, 2 partially (the core defect confirmed, one claimed consequence did not appear), none disproved. The test code is kept as patch files alongside this review and was never applied to the working tree.

What to fix first

  1. Stop the planner from mutating the wrong rows. Strip a primary-key range predicate only when both bounds are inclusive, or give KeyRange explicit bounds. Fix the Ne/NotIn coercion check in residual stripping, and never drop filter_expr without a coverage proof. Add a property test comparing eval(predicate, row) with access_contains(row) && eval(residual, row) across access shapes.
    Reproduced: `id >= 2 AND id < 5` returns, counts, updates and deletes id 5 through the typed, dynamic and SQL lanes. It is silent data loss on an ordinary range filter.
  2. Keep migration staging and abort inside the journal protocol. Never fold the live index overlay into the canonical index without folding the matching rows, and bound Validating and Abort pages instead of rewriting and snapshotting the whole index store per page.
    Reproduced: after an abort from Prepared, a retained insert disappears from indexed reads, and the next fold fails with STORE_CORRUPTION or RUNTIME_CORRUPTION, leaving startup terminally failed. A skeptic had disputed this; the test settled it.
  3. Give filtered-index predicates one typed authority. Persist the bound check expression (field ids and typed literals) instead of name-based SQL text, and compile it once for write membership, planner implication and the unique conflict re-check.
    Reproduced: a same-batch demote-then-insert commits, then every fold and every startup recovery fails with a unique violation. Text persistence also loses literal types and breaks on DDL renames.
  4. Classify record-member renames that stored rows can reach as physical, or reject them, in the migration planner. Then key canonical record storage by composite field id and resolve names only at the output boundary.
    Reproduced: after the rename is Applied, reads, updates and deletes of every pre-rename row fail with RUNTIME_CORRUPTION.
  5. Decouple durable store identity from Rust type paths and store topology. Match stores by their allocation identity (stable key and memory ids) during reconciliation, make topology changes non-destructive until the release's schema reconciliation succeeds, and keep source lineage valid across re-keying.
    Reproduced natively: the same stores registered under a moved Rust path go terminal with STORE_CORRUPTION, and reverting the code stays terminal. This contradicts the README's statement that Rust names do not own allocation identity.
  6. Add a recovery escape hatch and remove the startup wedges. Bind startup failure receipts to a build identity so a new wasm gets one fresh attempt. Write a receipt or stop the watchdog instead of trapping or replanning forever. Route fold-mode batches through the canonical catalog. Bound fold work per batch so it cannot exceed what the producer admitted.
    Several routine operations leave a canister permanently Recovering: a metadata-only entity rename with pending fold work (reproduced), migrations across multi-entity pages, and folds whose cost scales with records times schema size. A build-bound receipt turns every future wedge into 'ship a fix' instead of 'revert the code'.
  7. Key the Identity allocator by a stable owner rather than the dense field id, carry the high-water across renumbering, and fix physical-migration validation so dense field removal can renumber retained fields.
    Reproduced: removing a field that sorts before the primary key reissues id 1 after ids 1 to 3 were committed. The same test found that the documented CheckedCast plus field-removal migration fails at Validating.
  8. Seed the cursor HMAC key from IC raw_rand before the first cursor is issued, never from the ULID generator on wasm32, and rotate existing keys in the same format cut. Document or fix the predictability of generated ULID keys.
    On the production target the key can be derived from database creation time, so anyone holding one continuation can forge tokens and bypass an authored total LIMIT. Native tests use getrandom, so this path is never exercised.
  9. Restore CI evidence. Make the Tier A lanes fail when zero tests match and point them at real modules. Add a required, sharded PocketIC lane for durability, upgrade, migration, lifecycle and guard tests. Pin and assert the MSRV toolchain. Assert instruction samples against the 30B ceiling. Land the reproduction tests from this review as regression tests.
    Cheap, and it multiplies the value of every other fix. Every bug reproduced in this review passes current CI.
  10. Unify SQL three-valued semantics across the predicate and expression lanes: null-rejecting NOT, lazy CASE, missing nested paths as per-leaf UNKNOWN, casefolded ILIKE literals, explicit NULL handling for IS TRUE and IS FALSE. Add lane-parity tests.
    Reproduced: `DELETE ... WHERE NOT (status = 'active')` deletes NULL-status rows, a CASE-guarded division errors, an OR with a true sibling rejects rows, and a resumable UPDATE touches a different row set than the exact UPDATE.
  11. Correct index-key encodings in one persisted-format cut with a forced index rebuild: sign-biased Timestamp, length-first Principal, primary-key suffix bound of 254 bytes, canonical Account, pinned case-mapping tables.
    Reproduced: negative timestamps sort after positive ones and paging emits a row twice, and an entity keyed by two principals cannot insert once it has any index.
  12. Read rows written under older layouts correctly: resolve absent historical slots through their materialized default in the scalar fast path, patch checks and nested-path readers, and teach the value-storage walker the 0x84 enum envelope. Add older-layout fixtures.
    Reproduced: after `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT`, filters and OCTET_LENGTH fail on pre-ALTER rows, and any record path next to an enum member fails to filter or project.
  13. Bring the generic grouped path and index-ordered continuation up to the specialized paths: probe hash buckets for owned keys, honour DESC and per-term directions, fix IN-list resume anchors and physical repositioning, and decode every coverable index component kind in hybrid covering.
    Reproduced: GROUP BY on a list key yields one group per row, DESC and mixed-direction ORDER BY come back ascending, resumed IN-list pages drop rows, and SELECT of a Decimal index component with another column fails with an invariant error.
  14. Harden Decimal: checked division, normalization before multiplication, rounding to scale 28 instead of saturating, exact alignment for Add, Sub, Div and Rem. Remove the other caller-reachable traps (preallocation from LIMIT/OFFSET, ORDER BY parser depth, REPLACE with an empty needle).
    Reproduced: i128::MIN / -1 panics, 20 × 20 at scale 18 overflows, (1/3)² returns about 1.7e10, 1e21 + 1e-18 returns less than 1e21, and Rem returns zero so MultipleOf accepts non-multiples.
  15. Make public read admission match READ_ADMISSION: report materialized sorts, record index prefix and bound shape, reject empty-prefix whole-index fallbacks, and key the shared plan cache on full canonical literal bytes.
    Reproduced: a public page with a materialized ORDER BY is admitted, and an ORDER BY on an indexed column turns a rejected full scan into an admitted whole-index scan.
  16. Fix schema and job lifecycle liveness: activation abort cleans up candidate entries, unknown cardinality is not corruption, the deployed receipt is never evicted, lineage heads are re-stamped at every publication, catalog-lookup failures are not all terminal, and progress-store writes go through recovery admission.
    Each is reachable through routine schema evolution or long-running jobs and ends in a stuck job, a lost capacity slot or a blocked future migration that needs manual intervention.
  17. Make operator tooling safe: refuse `canister refresh` on non-local environments without an override, use a progress token in `migration run`, exit non-zero on failure or rejection, escape control characters in renderers, and page `icydb_schema`.
    The documented migration workflow stalls on tables over about 256 rows, a mistyped refresh can wipe a production canister, scripts continue after failed DDL, and stored text can inject terminal escapes.

Recurring themes

Predicate stripping and lane divergence return silently wrong rows, including for UPDATE/DELETE

Optimizations that drop a predicate because the access path supposedly already proves it are wrong in several places, and the two-valued predicate lane and the three-valued expression lane disagree on NOT/NULL, ILIKE/LOWER, lazy CASE and missing nested paths. Because the planner picks the lane, the same SQL can return, update or delete different rows depending on the plan. The fix: a property test checking that eval(pred,row) equals access_contains(row) && eval(residual,row), plus lane-parity tests.

Dual representations of one authority drift apart

Accepted-schema authority is supposed to be ID-based and typed, but some paths keep a second, name-based or text-based copy: filtered-index predicates are persisted as SQL text and re-parsed by a different grammar; record members are keyed by name; journal batches are routed through the live overlay catalog while rows are prepared against the canonical one; the value-storage walker still uses an old enum grammar; cardinality records share the schema map's namespace. Each mismatch surfaces later as corruption errors or wedges.

Deterministic failures are persisted or retried forever with no escape hatch (liveness wedges)

Several lifecycle paths turn a deterministic error into durable terminal state, or into a watchdog that retries forever: startup receipts bound only to database state, traps during recovery with no receipt, migration planning errors replanned every tick, non-abortable migration phases, orphaned candidate index entries, evicted readiness receipts, cardinality 'corruption' during upgrade, stale lineage heads, and resumable or pending jobs that can never finish or be aborted. The protocol is safe, but getting out of any of these usually needs a code revert or manual intervention.

Persisted key bytes do not match Value semantics

Index-component encodings must preserve Value ordering and identity. Timestamp (unbiased signed bytes) and Principal (content order instead of length-first) do not, the primary-key suffix cap (63 bytes) is smaller than real composite keys (up to 254), Account has two encodings for one ICRC account, and case-mapped expression keys depend on the toolchain's Unicode tables. Results are silently wrong range scans, failed inserts or duplicate unique rows. Fixing them changes persisted bytes, so they should be done together.

Rows written under older schema layouts are not tested

Several lazy and byte-level readers treat a legitimately absent historical slot as corruption. So after a routine ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT, filters, OCTET_LENGTH, resumable UPDATE and nested-path reads fail on rows written before the ALTER. The data-layer tests contain no rows stamped with an older layout version.

Decimal-centred numeric semantics

Decimal division panics on i128::MIN / -1, reachable from a SQL literal at plan time. Checked multiplication never normalizes or rounds, so ordinary scale-18 products overflow. The operator traits saturate to about 1.7e10 or 1.7e20 on scale overflow, and Rem returns zero, which lets MultipleOf validation pass. Numeric-widen comparisons send floats and large Nat128 values through a lossy Decimal conversion, so rows drop out of WHERE filters. The same path makes numeric comparisons slow.

The generic grouped path and index-stream continuation have fallen behind the specialized paths

The generic hash GROUP BY never probes existing groups for owned keys, ignores DESC when unbounded, executes mixed-direction ORDER BY with a single direction, builds cursors from projected rows, and fails on NULL in global DISTINCT. Continuation for streams that are not ordered by primary key never repositions: IN-list branches are capped without an anchor, which drops rows, and deep pages rescan from the start. The dedicated COUNT(*) path and the primary-key paths are correct, so parity tests would catch most of this.

Work scoped to the whole store, or to a single tracker, instead of the target

Several bounded operations scan or charge across the entire store instead of the target entity or relation domain, or measure instructions from each tracker's own start instead of per message. Index DDL, relation removal and migration abort therefore fail on large multi-entity stores, and instruction ceilings can turn typed exhaustion into IC traps. Related capacity problems: a 133 KiB stable B-tree node size, heap-resident prefix-cardinality metadata, an SQL command cache bounded only by entry count, and quadratic relation budget charging.

Caller-reachable traps that bypass typed budget errors

The resource model promises typed exhaustion errors, yet a few paths trap instead: Decimal division overflow, the ORDER BY arithmetic parser (no depth guard), Vec::with_capacity sized from a caller's LIMIT or OFFSET, REPLACE with an empty search string during constant folding, DESCRIBE on recursive composites, and unbudgeted nested-leaf expansion. The IC rolls traps back, so state stays intact, but these are cheap DoS paths.

Security: entropy and trust boundaries

Caller-facing authorization is solid, but secret material comes from an entropy-free generator on wasm32 (cursor HMAC key; predictable ULID keys). The shared plan cache identifies literals by a seeded XXH3 digest. Public read admission is looser than the contracts claim: materialized sort is never detected and whole-index fallbacks count as bounded. Operator tooling renders stored text raw, and `canister refresh` wipes any environment without a prompt.

CI and tests do not exercise what the repo claims

The Tier A oracle lanes match zero tests. PocketIC durability, upgrade, migration and guard tests are never compiled or run on PRs. The MSRV job builds on 1.98.1. Instruction-budget assertions cannot fail. cfg(test) forks replace production recovery and admission paths, and the native runtime stub hides instruction behaviour. These gaps explain how several high findings got through.

Operator tooling safety and exit codes

The documented `schema migration run` workflow treats legitimate identical status pages as a stall. One-shot `sql`, and migration run/abort, exit 0 on failure or rejection. Ctrl-D executes a half-typed statement. Canister text reaches terminals unescaped. `refresh` can reinstall a production canister.

Write-path and decode constant factors

The architecture is sound, but each written row is validated 4 to 6 times and re-canonicalized. Full-row reads decode slots 2 to 3 times. The row decode contract is rebuilt 4 to 5 times per batch item. Numeric comparisons expand to decimal digit strings. Top-K is O(N·K). Heap-store identity allocation rewrites the whole live checkpoint on every write.

Contract and documentation drift

The code matches the contracts on numeric limits and version policy, but some normative documents contradict each other or the code: placeholders, the resumable-update timestamp rule, the checksum policy, stale-index repair, NULL ordering, CLI INSERT/DELETE marked done, the default CLI environment, the crate README, TESTING.md layout, and the persisted-format inventory.

Migration and upgrade paths that bypass the journal or key durable state on unstable identities

The second-pass probes found the most severe liveness and integrity defects here. Migration staging and abort fold overlays outside the journal protocol, Validating and Abort pages rewrite the whole index store, a moved Rust store type is treated as corruption, a topology change re-keys source lineage, and the Identity allocator is keyed by a dense field id that renumbering changes. Four of these were reproduced with failing tests.

Fold cost is not bounded by what the producer admitted

Row commits are bounded end to end, but schema-publication producers bypass Gate 1, and several folds redo per record or per chunk what the producer did once per page: re-decoding the migration record, re-verifying the accepted bundle for each staged key, re-fingerprinting the entity snapshot for each 64-key chunk. The production fold has no instruction check, so an oversized batch can only appear as a trap that the watchdog repeats every second.

Targeted second-pass probes

A completeness critic named the areas that round one had covered least, and each got a dedicated probe. Probe findings went through the same adversarial verification as round one, and they appear in the explorer below with ids starting r2-.

Replay/fold cost versus the per-message instruction limit (liveness)

3 findings

I traced the whole replay pipeline in commit/recovery.rs. Replay of a retained marker runs as one message, each fold handles one complete retained batch per message, and Verify gets its own message. I compared each stage with every producer of retained batches: row commits via commit_window, SQL DDL user-index domain replacement, unique-validation pages, and migration rewrite/validation pages. I checked the admission gates, the convergence proof constants and the PocketIC coverage. Row commits hold up. Gate 1 (W = 4R + I + 4A + 4P <= 16,384) also counts reverse-relation ops, the replay preparation reuses the commit's relation budget, and the 240-row x 64-index maximum fold is still asserted under 30B through run_bounded_convergence_watchdog. The gap asked whether the write path rejects batches whose replay estimate exceeds the fold budget: it does not. Schema-publication producers bypass Gate 1. Gate 2 only counts batches, records and bytes, and one accepted-index record carries 64 keys. FOLD_CALLBACK_INSTRUCTION_LIMIT exists only in a #[cfg(test)] module (commit/mod.rs:20-21) as arithmetic and is not tied to any measured per-unit cost. The production fold has no instruction check at all. So an oversized batch can only show up as a trap. ic-timers keeps the committed 1 s cadence successor after a trap, so that trap repeats every second at up to 40B instructions per attempt, with no receipt. Online, retained debt then stops draining until E284 pressure blocks writes; after an upgrade the database stays Recovering. The new problems are cases where the fold redoes, once per journal record or per chunk, schema-metadata work that the producer does once per page. That cost scales with records x metadata size and no bound covers it. The worst case is migration rewrite pages, which reload and fully re-decode the durable migration record twice per record. Unique-validation pages re-verify the whole store bundle once per staged key. DDL index batches re-fingerprint the entity snapshot once per 64-key chunk, and DDL can admit up to 131,072 key effects per batch, twice the 65,536-effect maximum the convergence evidence proves and measured. For coverage: indexed_recovery.rs is #[ignore] and runs only 1-32 rows. convergence_candidate.rs adds a measured overhead to the frozen 22.07B baseline instead of measuring the shape itself. recovery_closeout.rs covers the 2,048x3, 240x64 and 64-batch-debt shapes. The largest measured callback, the 65,536-key accepted-index fold at 21.09B, now has no caller: publish_promotion_index_fixture and append_promotion_index_fixture_page are never invoked. The 4,096-zero-index and wide-row fixtures also have no callers.

Checked and sound
  • Stage separation holds. Replay of a retained marker runs in one message. Each fold handles exactly one complete retained batch and its watermark in one message, and the terminal fold yields before Verify (recovery.rs:319-350; ATOMICITY.md:73-81). The stage continuation is volatile and keyed by marker id (recovery.rs:108-124), so a trapped attempt rolls back and restarts idempotently.
  • A normal commit clears its marker in the same message (guard.rs:303-335). Marker-wide Replay and Verify therefore only run after an apply error was returned. Ordinary retained debt is always folded one batch per callback (recovery.rs:253-262, 843-852).
  • Row-commit batches are bounded by Gate 1: W = 4R + I (+4A + 4P) <= 16,384 (commit_window.rs:51-58, 217-261). Reverse-relation mutations are included in index_ops (prepare.rs:767-779), so relation fan-out is counted.
  • Row replay cannot fail a budget that the commit passed. prepare_row_commit_batch_for_replay uses the same RelationCommitBudget and does not re-run delete-restrict scans (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:393-426). Batches fold in global (database commit sequence, allocation, journal sequence) order (recovery.rs:854-934), so canonical before-images match what the commit saw.
  • The maximum row fan-out shape is measured against the design ceiling. The 240-row x 64-index fold is run through run_bounded_convergence_watchdog, which asserts every callback is under 30B and that the watchdog reaches quiescence (recovery_closeout.rs:136-226, 700-716).
  • Gate 2 is enforced before the marker is published. The cumulative retained debt limits are 64 batches, 16,384 records and 16 MiB (backlog_admission.rs:292-336; guard.rs:280-292), and pressure re-arms the watchdog.
  • Replay-stage overlay resets are heap clears that do not traverse canonical stores (data/store.rs:246-271, index/store.rs:510-530, schema/store.rs:1985-2002).
  • A trapped recovery or fold rolls back byte-for-byte (recovery_closeout.rs:1008-1034). ic-timers keeps the committed cadence successor after a trap (ic-timers-0.8.0 runtime/mod.rs:268-270), so a trap causes a retry and never data loss.
  • Positioned-overlay retirement in online mode is cheap: 293,529,644 instructions for 65,536 keys plus 38 head scans, per the 0.229 status evidence (0.229-status.md:506-513).
  • The Verify stage walks only marker-owned effects: one cached prepare context per entity and one point read per effect (recovery.rs:2529-2597). Its cost is comparable to the commit's own preparation.

Upgrade lifecycle: deferred registry reconciliation, silent store retirement, revert wedges, watchdog liveness

5 findings

I traced every check that runs after post_upgrade returns. post_upgrade itself only does the ic-memory bootstrap, a read-only observe() and watchdog registration. The first timer tick then runs format admission and registry reconciliation (convergence.rs), then recovery: live-checkpoint restore, mutation-revision init/validation, projection reset or replay/fold. After that comes the generated-schema handoff, and once Ready, root preparation and cardinality pages. I decided each cell of the scenario matrix: store key renamed with data, store removed then restored, upgrade with a retained marker, Rust-path rename, entity moved between stores, and heap-only migration. Sound: registry writes are preflight-then-apply; retirement refuses journal debt and any registry change while a marker exists; new quartets must be physically fresh; retired quartets are never reused. The watchdog does stop on SCHEMA_MIGRATION_IN_PROGRESS, and journaled migrations wake it again through retained journal debt. Not sound: (1) the runtime identifies a store by its Rust path. Renaming or moving a journaled store type is reported as STORE_CORRUPTION and publishes a JournalRecovery receipt that also matches after a revert, so only reinstall recovers. (2) Store retirement or addition is committed irreversibly before the same release's schema reconciliation. Generated reconciliation cannot bind new entities, so a store-key change, entity move or storage-mode switch always ends with both the new and the old wasm unusable. (3) Any store-topology change re-keys the lineage catalog, which breaks all later migrations. (4) Deterministic registry rejections are non-terminal, so the watchdog loops at 1 Hz forever while state shows Recovering. (5) A metadata migration confined to heap stores never wakes the stopped watchdog. The heap read-set ABA and receipt permanence are already reported (journal-jobs-4, xc-contracts-1, integrity-relations-1) and are not repeated here.

Checked and sound
  • post_upgrade performs no IcyDB durable mutation beyond the ic-memory bootstrap commit. __icydb_startup_post_upgrade only calls startup_state() (ensure_memory_bootstrap + read-only observe) and reconciles the watchdog (crates/icydb-model/src/build/actor/db/store.rs:148-166,237-256,806-817). A bootstrap failure is returned as StartupFailure, not a trap.
  • Registry reconciliation is preflight-then-apply. Tail-control initialization is preflighted and the control replacement is prepared before any apply step, and apply steps are infallible (crates/icydb-core/src/db/database_format/convergence.rs:185-206), so a rejected reconciliation leaves control bytes unchanged. logical_memory.rs asserts the unchanged control frame.
  • Retirement refuses journal debt: require_retirable_tail requires validate_current_tail_authority().is_empty() (convergence.rs:331-341). Any registry change is refused while a commit marker is present (convergence.rs:182-184), so a pending marker's batches cannot be orphaned by retirement.
  • Newly added quartets must be physically virgin (all four memories size 0, no tail batches or control) before adoption (convergence.rs:303-322). Retired quartets are never reused (156-157), and the registry is capped at 16 active-plus-retired entries (171-173).
  • Omitted stores' journals are re-included as historical allocations on every bootstrap, so retirement checks can read them (crates/icydb/src/db/memory_admission.rs:128-150).
  • Format admission is re-run per process and cached only on success (ADMITTED_DATABASE_FORMATS pushed after convergence succeeds, database_format/mod.rs:160-175).
  • The watchdog stops on SCHEMA_MIGRATION_IN_PROGRESS without persisting a receipt (build/actor/db/store.rs:342-347). Migration steps that publish to journaled stores create nonzero-sequence batches (schema_publication.rs:686-707), count as retained journal debt (backlog_admission.rs:104-109) and wake the watchdog (commit/guard.rs:334-336). Physical migrations and journaled metadata migrations therefore reach Ready after Applied.
  • Every retained-marker error exit wakes the watchdog. The wake-up function is captured before marker publication (guard.rs:269-273) and invoked on apply or clear failure (guard.rs:314-332).
  • Durable (resumable-job) read-set proofs reject non-journaled stores (crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/read_set.rs:108-125), so the known heap-revision ABA (journal-jobs-4/xc-contracts-1) is limited to exhaustive pages.

Identity (auto-increment) allocation: schema/identity_state.rs and db/identity

1 findings

I traced Identity::next from start to finish. The path runs from the statement-local cursor (session/write.rs) through the range preflight at the commit window, then the journal batch and marker (with durable proof in journal/codec.rs), live and heap-checkpoint materialization, marker replay, and the sequential canonical fold in recovery.rs. It ends at schema-publication state transitions (identity_state.rs prepare_identity_state_transition) and every schema path that can create, retire or renumber an owner. Cell by cell: (a) an explicit PK above high-water cannot happen, because authored and replace-on-missing values are rejected. (b) Rejected or rolled-back statements consume nothing. (c) Exhaustion is fallible Unsupported/Identity and statement-atomic. (d) Entity rename keeps the tag. Drop retires the owner, and re-add cannot happen because existing-head lowering cannot add entities. (e) The 65,536 cap is enforced but cannot be reached in practice. (f) Multi-row INSERT, INSERT...SELECT and DEFAULT VALUES allocate in input order in one Complete batch. Mutation jobs are update-only, so they never allocate across pages. Replay and fold idempotency, keyed by high-water plus exact advance ID, holds. One cell fails: FieldId reuse. A generated field removal, whether online or inside a physical migration, renumbers all retained fields densely. That includes the Identity PK, whose FieldId comes from name-sorted order. Identity state is keyed only by (entity_tag, field_id) and is never remapped. So publication retires the old owner and creates a fresh one at high-water 0. On an emptied entity this reissues committed IDs, which violates IDENTITY_CONTRACT. In a physical migration on a populated entity, every later generated insert collides with row 1 and fails as Identity corruption, and Deep integrity flags every existing row. Separately, fold routing of IdentityRangeAdvance through the live catalog is already covered by round-1 commit-1. An explicit entity removal while an older batch for that entity is still unfolded looks like a further trigger for the same root cause; I did not trace it to the end.

Checked and sound
  • (a) Explicit identity values cannot be authored: resolve_insert_active_slot and the insert-overlay path reject Authored intents on any insert_generation field (crates/icydb-core/src/db/data/persisted_row/patch.rs:432-440, 672-680); Insert with an Expected key on an Identity entity fails with mutation_database_owned_field_explicit (crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/write.rs:1350-1355); Replace on a missing key for an Identity entity is rejected (write.rs:1381-1388). Physical-migration transforms cannot target or source the PK (crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/migration_transform.rs:474-481, 564), and existing-head lowering rejects any write-policy drift (crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application_lowering.rs:1811-1818). No supported lane can create a row whose Identity key is above high-water.
  • (b) Allocation stays tentative: the cursor lives only in the statement's entity_states. into_range_advance runs only after precommit preparation (write.rs:1552-1586). preflight_identity_range_advance re-checks the expected high-water against effective state immediately before marker publication and returns Conflict when stale (crates/icydb-core/src/db/executor/mutation/commit_window.rs:589, 962-976; crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/identity_state.rs:314-330). Any error before the marker drops the cursor without consuming a value.
  • Durable range proof: one IdentityRangeAdvance per owner per batch is journaled next to its rows (commit_window.rs:810-857). validate_identity_range_row_sets requires generated puts to be contiguous, ascending, and to match count and new_high_water, and forbids deletes inside the new range (crates/icydb-core/src/db/journal/codec.rs:1705-1789). The scheduler keeps rows in input order (crates/icydb-core/src/db/executor/mutation/constraint_scheduler.rs:186-195), and narrow Nat PKs encode as PrimaryKeyComponent::Nat64, so the proof accepts them (crates/icydb-core/src/db/key_taxonomy.rs:131-143).
  • Idempotent materialization: range_commit_state treats a record as materialized only when both high-water and the exact IdentityAdvanceId match, and treats any other mismatch as corruption (identity_state.rs:354-383). Replay and canonical fold both go through it (crates/icydb-core/src/db/commit/recovery.rs:1592-1613, 1923-1956). Journal batches fold one at a time in database commit order (recovery.rs:843-852, 939-1012), and marker batches are appended to the tail before they fold (recovery.rs:600-669), so a lagging canonical state is always at the expected value when its range folds.
  • Heap / LiveRebuiltMetadata stores: an Identity range forces the store's row ops into the marker (commit_window.rs:835-849). The durable live checkpoint and the heap schema store are both advanced with the same advance ID (commit_window.rs:978-996), and marker replay for tail-less stores is admitted through journal_batch_is_direct_identity_commit (recovery.rs:2262-2294). The high-water survives the loss of heap rows on upgrade, so values are not reused.
  • (c) Exhaustion: allocation uses checked u128 arithmetic plus a per-kind maximum and returns identity_exhausted (Unsupported/Identity) without advancing (identity_state.rs:441-465, 513-532, 692-698). The statement is rejected atomically. There is no trap path, and the error class is typed and stable (crates/icydb-core/src/error/mod.rs:1718-1720).
  • (d) Entity identity: tags are allocated once, database-wide, at initial lowering (application_lowering.rs:2511-2531). Existing-head and generated lowering reject any entity without an existing source binding (application_lowering.rs:825-829, 1387-1400), so a tag can never be reissued to a new entity. Migration renames rekey source bindings but keep the tag. Entity removal retires the owner, and re-declaring a retired key is rejected as corruption (identity_state.rs:600-626; test crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/store/tests.rs:1568-1645).
  • (e) Capacity: the lifetime cap is enforced per store during transition (identity_state.rs:627-629) and per database at apply/migrate (crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application.rs:2223-2255). Owners are created only at initial lowering (at most the entity count) plus the bounded renumbering churn described in the finding, so ordinary churn cannot reach 65,536 and permanently block anything.
  • (f) Ordering: every SQL INSERT source (VALUES, DEFAULT VALUES, INSERT...SELECT with the source read first) is executed as one Complete-packed batch (crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/sql/execute/write/insert.rs:346-397). Ordinals increment only for Identity-generating inserts (write.rs:1286-1291, 1375-1378). BoundedPrefix packing, where a PageFull break could otherwise follow an allocation, is used only by resumable UPDATE jobs (write.rs:1074-1107; crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/sql/resumable_update.rs:669-684), and those never allocate Identity.

Cross-message concurrency: multi-message jobs and async endpoints interleaved with writes and schema changes

3 findings

I ran the gap-3 probe: every multi-message job crossed with the writes and schema events that can land between its pages. Jobs covered: constraint activation Forward/Verify, unique DDL index activation, cardinality builds, Deep integrity, SQL mutation jobs (ResumableForwardScanner plus the packer), application resumable jobs and exhaustive proofs, migration phases, and schema application. Events covered: an insert behind or ahead of the checkpoint, a key-moving update, deleting the checkpoint row, schema publication, upgrade, and entity rename. For async I traced DbSession, typed bindings, prepared cursors, cursors and caches across an .await, and checked ic-cdk-executor 2.0 polling. Most cells hold. Each job either fences on a revision (entity mutation revision, store data_mutation_revision, the Deep proof vector, the read-set root plus data and access revisions, or the cardinality source identity), blocks the conflicting write (the unique activation barrier), or enforces the constraint on new writes. Folds run under the canonical catalog at the batch's own journal position. Async sessions fail closed because DbSession holds no schema state and every typed binding, token and cache key is checked against the current accepted identity in the same message. The scanner does not move its checkpoint past a candidate the packer rejects. What does not hold: (1) IndexStore::fold_journaled_materialized_view, called on every migration Validating page and every abort-cleanup page, folds the live index overlay into the canonical index without folding rows or moving the watermark. Any retained batch that updates or deletes an indexed row in that store can then never be folded; recovery hits a corruption error and records a terminal startup failure. (2) The same call rewrites and snapshots the whole index store on every page, so on large stores both Advance and Abort trap while the database is gated. (3) A Building cardinality generation restarts on every fold, so on a large, busy store it never finishes, the watchdog runs forever, and stores later in the list starve. The assert! in RequestExecutionFuture::poll adds nothing new: the executor never nests polls, so only sharing a future across tasks triggers it, which is round 1's facade-4.

Checked and sound
  • A DbSession or Db held across .await keeps no stale schema: it holds only the store registry and the request scope (crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/mod.rs:57-59, crates/icydb-core/src/db/mod.rs:222-226). Every read and write looks up accepted authority again and commits in the same synchronous message.
  • Typed bindings fail closed when stale. Before every typed write, current_typed_entity_binding_catalog re-checks incarnation, accepted revision, fingerprint, layout generation and each field's id and slot (crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/write.rs:839-925). Mixed batches check every item (write.rs:1873-1905), and prepared output rows check again (crates/icydb/src/db/session/write.rs:1293).
  • Scalar continuation tokens bind database incarnation, accepted-root revision and fingerprint, and the entity fingerprint (crates/icydb-core/src/db/cursor/token/codec.rs:217-221). The SQL compiled-command cache key includes runtime-root identity and accepted revision (crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/sql/cache.rs:50-56).
  • Request counters stay consistent across .await. Instruction units come from performance_counter(1), the call-context counter, which keeps counting across callbacks (crates/icydb-core/src/runtime.rs:12-13). Execution and preparation trackers are created and finished synchronously (executor/budget.rs:489-498, query/preparation.rs:88-103).
  • ic-cdk-executor 2.0.0 polls woken tasks one after another from poll_all at the entrypoint's top level and never inside another task's poll (ic-cdk-executor-2.0.0/src/machinery.rs:222-270, 351-368). A spawned RequestExecutionFuture is therefore polled with no ambient root, and the assert at crates/icydb/src/db/session/request.rs:87 fires only when one future is shared across tasks, which is facade-4.
  • ResumableForwardScanner does not skip a rejected candidate. It moves pending_candidate_checkpoint into the checkpoint only on the next pull (session/sql/resumable_update.rs:986-988). On PageFull or CandidateExceedsPolicy the packer breaks without pulling again (session/write.rs:1240-1252). finish() therefore returns the last non-candidate key before the rejected row (resumable_update.rs:1087-1094), and the progress record is committed in the same marker as the rows (1210-1226).
  • Mutation-job Verify checks the target entity's durable mutation revision before and after each page. Residual rows or a revision change restart Forward (resumable_update.rs:743-792). The expected revision after the job's own commit is predicted (1142-1157). Any publication that changes revision or fingerprint ends the job as AcceptedSchemaChanged (1503-1514), and incarnation or allocation changes end it as TargetAllocationChanged (483-537).
  • Constraint activation stays sound while writes land between pages. New writes are checked against Check and NotNull activations (schema/check/compile.rs:713-779). The unique barrier blocks Insert, Replace and key-changing updates (compile.rs:475-499). Deletes remove the candidate key (commit/prepare.rs:654-699). Verify checks the store data_mutation_revision before each page and after the last (constraint_activation_runner.rs:630-635, 1041, 1278-1290). Only row-mutation batches raise that revision (journal/store.rs:805-818, journal/codec.rs:227-245), so the job's own candidate-index and job-record batches do not invalidate it.
  • Folds and replays of journaled stores use the canonical accepted selection (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:197-210). Batches committed before a DDL or activation are prepared under the schema in force at their journal position, so the activation write barrier is never applied to older batches.
  • A cardinality build cannot mix sources. It reads only canonical rows and index entries, and its source identity binds incarnation, allocation, accepted root, index set and fold watermark (schema/cardinality_generation.rs:338-356). The source is checked before and after every page, and any change restarts on the other slot (schema/cardinality_build.rs:353-382). Entries of candidate or migration-staged index generations are excluded from counts (cardinality_build.rs:652-668).
  • Deep integrity marks the job Invalidated if the proof vector changes before or after any page, or if plan or schema identity changes (integrity/deep.rs:359-414, 959-981).
  • Application resumable jobs re-check incarnation, accepted root and each store's data and access revisions both before and after the operation closure (session/resumable_job.rs:127-137, session/read_set.rs:74-105).
  • The migration gate blocks ordinary work from Validating through Rejected (schema/migration_record.rs:55-66), and the cached gate is refreshed on every applied migration-record op (schema/live_schema_checkpoint.rs:680-694).
  • A non-unique SQL CREATE INDEX stages its complete index domain in one message (schema/mutation/user_index_domain.rs module header, 'valid only for the current non-awaiting stage'), so it has no cross-message window. Unique index additions go through the fenced activation runner.

Executor covering-index projection (executor/covering.rs, executor/projection/covering/*)

2 findings

I probed gap #4 (covering projection) from start to finish. On the planner side I read query/plan/covering/mod.rs: field-source classification, order contract, pure vs hybrid admission and the ordered-DISTINCT group seek. On the executor side I read all of executor/covering.rs (lines 1-1302) and projection/covering/{mod,pure,hybrid,shared}.rs, plus the index-key encoders (ordered/mod.rs, segments.rs, normalize.rs, build.rs, expression.rs) that the decode must invert. I then built a matrix of field kind × source (IndexComponent, IndexExpressionComponent, PrimaryKey, prefix Constant) × lane (pure, hybrid, group seek). The decode handles only the Bool, Int64 (covers Int8-Int64), Nat64 (covers Nat8-Nat64), Text, Ulid and Unit tags, and for those it round-trips exactly to the Value a row read returns. Pure covering fails closed on every other tag. The hybrid lane does not: its decoder turns an unsupported tag into a query_executor_invariant error. The planner never checks component kinds, so an ordinary SQL SELECT fails whenever it projects an index component of any other kind (Decimal, Timestamp, Date, Duration, Float, Int128/Nat128/IntBig/NatBig/U256, Principal/Subaccount/Account, Enum) together with a column that is not in the index. The pure lane has a related cost problem: for those same kinds it scans and buffers the whole index range, finds out at the first decode that it cannot use the result, and then the scalar path does the same scan again, with both scans charged to the same hard budget. The gap's other hypotheses do not hold. Decimal scale on prefix constants cannot be observed, because Decimal equality, display and Candid output are normalized. Text case and expression keys use the same lower/upper/trim functions as runtime evaluation. NULL never appears as a component, and a completeness gate stops the planner from using an index that would drop NULL rows. Signed zero is normalized when a Float is built. Covering reads the same index ordinal and physical generation that scalar access uses. Mixed-direction ORDER BY and continuation or cursor pages never reach covering or reorder_covering_projection_pairs.

Checked and sound
  • Supported decode tags round-trip exactly to row-read Values. Int8-Int64 are stored with the Int64 tag and decoded as Value::Int64 through the XOR-bias inverse (covering.rs:1046-1049, ordered/mod.rs:181-195 vs semantics.rs:62-65). Nat8-Nat64 decode as Value::Nat64 from big-endian bytes. Text decoding (covering.rs:1198-1248) exactly inverts push_terminated_bytes (segments.rs:52-62), including the 0x00 0xFF escape and the 0x00 0x00 terminator. Bool, Ulid and Unit also round-trip. A Relation field decodes as its key kind in both the row and the index (structural_field/accepted.rs:53-55).
  • Pure covering fails closed. When decode_covering_projection_component returns Ok(None) for an unsupported tag, the pure lane returns Ok(None) and the facade falls back to the scalar path (pure.rs:196-205, 264-273, 368-370; facade.rs:269-291).
  • NULL is never a covering component. A NULL value, or an unsupported kind, makes the whole index key None, so the row has no index entry (build.rs:699-713, 597-600). index_stream_is_complete_for_query (index_select.rs:54-79) requires every omittable key field to be implied NOT NULL, so covering cannot silently drop NULL rows.
  • Expression components match runtime evaluation.
