LOWER, UPPER, TRIM and LOWER(TRIM) index keys are derived with the same lower_text, upper_text and str::trim functions that projection evaluation uses (scalar_expr.rs:85-115 vs function_semantics/evaluation.rs:25-33). Date/Year/Month/Day items are never coverable (covering/mod.rs:1048-1051). Expression items are never treated as sources for the raw field (covering/mod.rs:992-1003). The only divergence left is Unicode-table drift across toolchains, which round 1 already reported (value-types-error-6).
  • Prefix-bound Constant sources come only from field key items with Strict coercion (key_item_match.rs:31-33) and from leading prefix values (path.rs:426-440 for branch sets). The Constant for a Decimal field carries the literal's scale, not the declared scale (admission.rs:773-779), but Decimal equality, hashing, Display and Candid all normalize (decimal/compare.rs:68-74, text.rs:29-31, wire.rs:14-19), so the difference cannot be observed. Float -0.0 is normalized when the value is built (atom.rs:610-616).
  • Mixed-direction ORDER BY never reaches covering. DeterministicSecondaryOrderContract rejects non-uniform directions (order_contract.rs:152-156), primary_key_only_direction_fields requires a uniform direction (order_contract.rs:458-466), and covering_projection_order_contract returns None through `?` (covering/mod.rs:456).
  • Covering projection runs only when DISTINCT is off, there is no continuation progress, no cursor is being emitted and there is no scan budget (facade.rs:253). The group seek likewise requires no continuation, no cursor and no page envelope (facade.rs:227-233). So reorder and page windowing never interact with resume.
  • The PK-order reorder (covering.rs:80-93) sorts by PrimaryKeyValue::cmp. That order agrees with the compact key byte order: integers and timestamps are bias-encoded and Principal is length-prefixed (key_taxonomy.rs:1150-1160, 1328-1341). Merged streams use the same comparator, with a per-child monotonicity check (covering.rs:691-703).
  • Index generation cannot diverge between lanes. Pure, hybrid and group-seek scans all use the lowered scan contract, whose IndexId is (entity, ordinal, physical_generation) from the accepted contract (access/lowering.rs:349, 472, 680). The planner sees only accepted-schema indexes, and only while the store's IndexState is Ready (session/query/cache.rs:359-363).
  • LIMIT 0 becomes an empty ByKeys plan before covering is considered (plan/pipeline.rs:654-660), so the .max(1) in covering_scan_limit (shared.rs:360-364) can never produce a row.
  • Branch-set and multi-lookup IndexOrder covering requires a Full order match (order_contract.rs:191-198, covering/mod.rs:461-471). OrderedConcat sorts branches by raw lower key using the same comparator as the index store (key_taxonomy.rs:1083-1087, 1418-1434) and reverses them for DESC.
  • Index-only residual predicates are evaluated before an entry is pushed and counted against the limit (stream/access/scan.rs:1070-1095), so the scan-time LIMIT/OFFSET window counts only rows that pass the filter. Scan-time windows are applied only under ProvenByPlanner, where raw entries equal present rows (shared.rs:154-165).

Write-side versus decode-side bounds for persisted recursive data

5 findings

I probed gap #5 (recursive-bounds), comparing write-side and read-side limits for every persisted recursive payload: row value storage (canonical enum/composite wire and by-kind lists/maps), insert defaults, mutation-job intent (scope Expr and literals, fixed patch, engine continuation), accepted check trees, accepted field kinds and enum/composite catalogs in schema snapshots, nested-leaf and relation paths, journal records, constraint-validation finding paths, cursor tokens, and persisted partial-index predicate SQL. I checked each encoder/decoder pair for the same counting convention and traced where writes are admitted before persistence. Every durable pair that startup or recovery reads is symmetric: the canonical codec and value admission both use root=0 and reject at depth>=64. Admission charges extra levels for Relation and Newtype, so it is never looser than the encoder. Kind, catalog, check-tree and mutation-intent codecs reject at identical bounds. The intent and the rendered index-predicate SQL are both re-decoded/re-parsed before persistence. So I found no path where a write succeeds and startup/recovery then fails with Corruption. Schema type depth 64 limits only inline FieldType. Through named records, enums, newtypes and named collections, value nesting is unbounded by the schema, but admission rejects anything deeper than 64 levels before encoding. Option is a nullable flag, not a wrapper. SQL UPDATE predicates of depth 33-128 fail with IneligibleIntent before any progress-store write. Wasm stack use for decode during startup/recovery is bounded at roughly 64 levels × 2-3 frames per recursive stage, far below the 1 MiB default. What does not hold: (1) the non-canonical value-storage materializing decoder counts two depth units per level, so it rejects values the canonical write path accepts (query-side failure, reported as Corruption); (2) every recursive row decoder re-skips each subtree at every level, so decode cost is O(bytes × depth) while all budgets are byte-based; (3-5) three smaller bound mismatches around check/predicate trees.

Checked and sound
  • Canonical value-storage encoder and decoder use the same convention (root depth 0, +1 per list item, map key/value and enum payload, reject depth>=MAX_ACCEPTED_RECURSIVE_DEPTH_U16=64): crates/icydb-core/src/db/data/structural_field/value_storage/canonical.rs:57, :120, :197, :302-306.
  • Value admission rejects at depth>=64 (admission.rs:86-91, :412, :735) and charges >= the encoder's depth on every edge (List/Map/Enum/Record/Tuple +1 on both sides; Relation admission.rs:527-529 and Newtype :717-719 add +1 with no encoded nesting), so every admitted value encodes. Read-side admit_canonical/validate_kind (admission.rs:750-997) uses the same counting as write-side normalize, so a row written under a revision re-admits under that same revision.
  • Row-contract decode of canonical-wire fields uses the canonical decoder plus admission (persisted_row/contract.rs:50-65, persisted_row/canonical.rs:190-201). Index-key derivation reads values through required_value_by_contract_cow (index/key/build.rs:361-366), so index, relation and recovery replay paths share the write codec.
  • Schema type depth: proposal FieldType depth (icydb-schema fragment.rs:186-199, codec/value.rs:64-120) lowers 1:1 to AcceptedFieldKind List chains; named types become Enum/Composite references (application_lowering.rs:3171-3196). The accepted kind snapshot codec (schema/codec/field.rs:110-117 vs :199-206), local-shape check (accepted_field_kind.rs:86-89) and enum-catalog kind codec (enum_catalog/codec.rs:227-234 vs :316-323) all reject at depth>=64 on both sides.
  • Value nesting past schema depth 64 through named types (recursive records, enum payloads, map entries, newtype chains) is always rejected by admission with DepthExceeded before encoding, so no persisted value exceeds 64 levels. Nullable/Option is a flag, not a nesting wrapper (admission.rs:727-739).
  • Nested-leaf paths (application_lowering.rs:2831 depth>=64 plus a cycle guard), leaf path codec (codec/field.rs:86-107), index field paths (codec/index.rs:286-301) and relation path steps (MAX_RELATION_PATH_STEPS in both proposal and snapshot codec) use symmetric bounds.
  • Accepted check tree: the validator (schema/check/mod.rs:335-352, depth>=32 and nodes>256) and the snapshot codec (schema/codec/constraint.rs:290-300 encode, :336-345 decode) agree. The encoder omits the node check, but bind_check_expr_v1 (check/bind.rs:79-88) and snapshot integrity (integrity/constraint.rs:196) validate first.
  • Mutation-job intent: the scope Expr encoder and decoder both enforce depth<=32 and nodes<=256 (mutation_job/intent.rs:521-545). CanonicalMutationIntent::new runs validate(), which decodes the scope and patch (intent.rs:86-120, :296-327), and start_trusted_sql_mutation_job decodes again before insert_mutation (session/mutation_job.rs:46-68). So an SQL UPDATE predicate of depth 33-128 fails with IneligibleIntent before any progress-store write. The engine continuation codec is non-recursive (resumable_update.rs:250-357).
  • Targeted-rule traversal is iterative with depth limit 64 and path-component limit 64 (check/targeted.rs:804-818, :854-881). It charges <= admission depth, so every admitted value evaluates. Constraint-validation finding paths are bounded at 64 on encode and decode (constraint_validation.rs:580-583, :891).
  • Cursor token value codec enforces depth<=128 on write and read (cursor/token/value.rs:55, :101-103, :136-140). Row values (<=64 levels) always fit, and scope literals are round-tripped at job start.
  • Insert defaults are scalar literals only (icydb-schema FieldInsertPolicy::Default(ScalarLiteral)), validated on acceptance through the same canonical/admission path (persisted_row/canonical.rs:204-233).
  • Journal records are non-recursive at record level. Embedded schema snapshots and validation jobs use the symmetric codecs above (journal/codec.rs:1793-1968). Index keys encode only scalar and unit-enum components (index/key/build.rs:733-766, enum_catalog/equality_key.rs).
  • Persisted partial-index predicate SQL (DDL verbatim, sql/ddl/index.rs:536-548, or rendered for generated/proposal indexes, application_lowering.rs:2009-2023) is re-parsed by snapshot integrity before acceptance (integrity/nullable_unique.rs:51-61, integrity.rs:126-132). A predicate the parser rejects cannot be persisted.
  • By-kind structural lists/maps (accepted.rs) recurse by accepted kind (<=64) and re-skip each item from depth 0 (binary.rs:431-440), so writes accepted by kind depth are never rejected by MAX_STRUCTURAL_BINARY_SKIP_DEPTH=64.
  • Wasm stack headroom: decode recursion during startup/recovery is bounded by 64 levels × about 2-3 frames each for canonical decode (canonical.rs), admission validate_kind/validate_composite/validate_composite_element and Value drop. Snapshot kinds are <=64 and check trees <=32. Together that is well under the 1 MiB default wasm32 stack.

Persisted SQL text as a durable format (filtered-index predicate_sql)

3 findings

I ran the persisted-sql-text probe end to end. I traced PersistedIndexSnapshot.predicate_sql from its sources (the generated check-expr renderer, DDL token re-render) through DDL RENAME relabeling, migration-planner relabeling, generated-proposal reconciliation at startup, snapshot decode/acceptance, and every runtime consumer. (a) Reconciliation compares predicate text, never semantics: application_lowering.rs:1922 checks full struct equality at every generated schema apply, migration_planner.rs:1323 compares strings, and compatibility.rs:336 is used only for DDL publication. Building the renderer matrix cell by cell, the check-expr renderer (generated indexes) and the predicate-AST renderer (relabel) agree on every construct except field-to-field =/!=. There the predicate AST reorders the two field names into a canonical order and the check renderer keeps the authored order. This produces the lead sql-parser-5 could not demonstrate: a DDL RENAME of any DDL column rewrites generated-index text, and the next release with any generated schema change fails startup reconciliation. The planner also rejects metadata-only migrations for the same reason, and rejects enum-variant renames because relabeling only maps field names. (b) A parse failure is fail-closed everywhere: decode reports store_corruption, publish reports store_invariant, the write path reports store_corruption, DDL bind reports InvalidFilteredIndexPredicate, and a failed relabel rejects the rename. There are no panics. (c) The grammar has no inventory entry and no golden corpus. Keyword collisions and wide-literal round-trips are already covered by xc-architecture-1 and sql-parser-9. One new hazard: the index predicate's meaning depends on the current parser code, while the fingerprint and physical generation depend only on the text, so a parser fix leaves already-built index contents stale and the planner still trusts them. (d) Write-time membership, planner implication, inspection and DDL domain builds all use the same parse and normalize function, so the same text gives the same predicate tree.

Checked and sound
  • All runtime consumers use one parse path. normalized_accepted_index_predicate (predicate/mod.rs:65-76) is used for write-time membership (index/plan/mod.rs:55-61, 224-247), planner contracts (access/path.rs:160,186), inspection (index/plan/integrity.rs:322-334) and DDL domain builds (schema/mutation/user_index_domain.rs:564-568). Dependency slots use the same parse_sql_predicate+normalize (schema/check/compile.rs:1132-1137). The same text always yields the same Predicate.
  • Persisted predicate parse failures are fail-closed and never panic. Snapshot decode maps to store_corruption (schema/codec.rs:234-235, integrity.rs:52-56). Publish encode maps to store_invariant (codec.rs:72-73). Per-row writes map to store_corruption (predicate/mod.rs:70-72). Dependency compile maps to accepted_row_constraint_program_corrupt (check/compile.rs:1132-1133). DDL bind maps to InvalidFilteredIndexPredicate (sql/ddl/index.rs:233). references_field treats unparseable text as a dependency (snapshot.rs:1247-1249).
  • Relabel output is never persisted unchecked. The DDL rename derivation goes through AcceptedSchemaSnapshot::try_new_with_acceptance (mutation/field.rs:805-806), which re-parses the text and rebinds every predicate field name (integrity/nullable_unique.rs:51-60). A relabel failure rejects the rename (mutation/field.rs:842-843) or the migration (migration_planner.rs:1306).
  • The migration planner persists the check-renderer `target` and never the relabeled text (migration_planner.rs:1220-1224). Relabeling is used only for comparison, so a migration that succeeds reconciles cleanly at the next apply.
  • Planner mismatches never publish inconsistent state. Working and candidate bundles re-run acceptance (enum_catalog/publication.rs:247-249, migration_planner.rs:164-174). Stale predicate text, such as a DDL index naming a generated field that was renamed, is rejected as RekeyedCatalogInvalid or CandidateMismatch.
  • For the forms the generated macro grammar can produce, the check-expr and predicate-AST renderers agree textually on everything except symmetric field-field ordering. This covers And/Or child order (sorted by canonical key and preserved by the parser), parenthesization, NOT, IS [NOT] NULL, Bool, Text with '' escaping (lexer token_body.rs:37-72), ints, normalized Decimal Display (decimal/text.rs:29-69) and float Display, within the ranges sql-parser-9 excludes.
  • relabel_sql_predicate_field_root cannot return None on parser output. The render None arms (render.rs:86-91, 121, and the non-scalar values) are unreachable from parse_sql_predicate.
  • DDL predicate capture re-renders tokens with correct string escaping (sql_shared/types.rs token_kind_sql_fragment: `''`). The stored text therefore re-parses to the predicate that validated_create_index_predicate_sql checked (sql/ddl/index.rs:536-549).
  • Contextual words LOWER/UPPER/STARTS_WITH/LIKE/ILIKE/U256 are resolved by lookahead (operand/field.rs:73-86, cursor.rs:80-85, operand/text.rs:163-186). Fields or rename targets with those names survive relabeling.
  • Check-expr depth (MAX_CHECK_EXPR_V1_DEPTH=32) is far below parser depth (MAX_SQL_EXPR_DEPTH=128), so generated renders always re-parse.
  • Restarting with an unchanged generated fragment short-circuits on the exact receipt (application.rs:665, 291-311; icydb/src/db/session/catalog.rs:163-169), so text drift only surfaces when a new schema fragment is applied.

Freshness of derived cardinality and prefix metadata that the engine trusts as exact

3 findings

I read gap #7 and built a matrix of every DataStore and IndexStore mutation path against the metadata the engine treats as exact. The metadata: heap EntityCardinality, EntityCardinalityDelta, IndexPrefixCardinality (checked by data generation), IndexPrefixCardinalityDelta (bound to a watermark), and the durable Ready count generation in the schema store. The paths: live insert/remove, positioned publish, fold (visible and shadowed branches), exact retirement, recovery reset plus fold, durable maintenance, invalidating batch kinds, schema-publication domain replacement, migration rewrite, migration staging/abort, and heap vs journaled init. A grep shows only three code paths write canonical data/index state: the two journal fold functions and IndexStore::fold_journaled_materialized_view. Every cell holds except that last one. It is compiled with the `migration` feature and runs on every migration Validating page and every Abort page, including Abort from Prepared, a phase that still admits ordinary writes. It copies the whole live overlay, including index effects of not-yet-folded journal batches, into the canonical index. It does not move the fold watermark and does not touch the durable generation. Durable prefix counts then drift permanently: the later fold of those batches computes a net delta of zero against the already-rewritten canonical. Reads trust the drifted count. A Some(0) makes single-prefix scans and multi-lookup branches return no rows, and exact COUNT is wrong. A later delete or update of a drifted row underflows in maintenance, which returns STORE_CORRUPTION from the fold. The driver records that as a terminal JournalRecovery failure, so the database wedges. The same function also does O(whole index store) work on each page, which can permanently trap Validating and Abort while the database-wide migration gate is held. Separately, the fold path makes a count underflow or a delta-watermark mismatch fatal to the authoritative fold. The 0.230 design says such evidence should just become unavailable. The entity counts that authorise destructive DDL are not affected: the materialized fold never touches the data store. The exact SUM/AVG/COUNT DISTINCT folds match the row-based semantics.

Checked and sound
  • EntityCardinalityDelta (visible minus canonical) is correct in every journaled data path. insert/remove/publish apply presence transitions (data/store.rs:162-242, 308-346). The shadowed-fold branches correct the delta when canonical changes under a live entry (data/store.rs:489-497, 518-524). Exact retirement removes live only where live equals the folded canonical value (data/store.rs:430-454). reset clears live and delta together (data/store.rs:246-272).
  • IndexPrefixCardinalityDelta is updated by every IndexStore mutator (index/store.rs:432-508, 570-614). The shadowed fold branch passes (new canonical, old canonical) in reversed order, which correctly subtracts the canonical change (index/store.rs:773-775). Its base watermark is preflighted and advanced in the same message as the journal retirement (commit/recovery.rs:1006-1024) and reset to the journal watermark on recovery (commit/recovery.rs:681-706).
  • Durable Ready counts are maintained from canonical-predecessor values (commit/recovery.rs:1121-1175). They are applied in the same message as the fold, together with a header re-bound to the next watermark (schema/store.rs:1318-1403, commit/recovery.rs:1028-1049). Batches with AcceptedSchemaPublish, AcceptedSchemaIndexPut/Delete or SchemaMigration* records skip maintenance, and the header's stale watermark then makes all counts unavailable (commit/recovery.rs:1058-1064, 1103-1119).
  • Consumers read durable counts only when the header is Ready, no build cursor exists, the source validates (incarnation, allocations, accepted root, index set, watermark), and either the effective root equals the canonical root (Current) or the admitted root matches (registry/handle.rs:981-1066; schema/cardinality_build.rs:111-135). Base plus delta arithmetic is checked; underflow gives None (registry/handle.rs:1173-1179).
  • The builder scans canonical only (data/store.rs:669-692) and restarts into the alternate slot on any source change between pages (schema/cardinality_build.rs:347-404). Count records are generation-checked on read (schema/store.rs:1301-1315). The empty-generation shortcut requires both canonical maps to be physically empty (schema/cardinality_build.rs:365-372).
  • Heap IndexPrefixCardinality is trusted only while its stamp equals the current DataStore generation. Every count-changing mutation clears the stamp, and mark_synchronized cannot revive a map invalidated by decoding (index/cardinality.rs:128-132, 524-574). Journaled stores with a non-empty canonical map at init or reset start unavailable (index/store.rs:170-176, 532-538).
  • Heap stores: EntityCardinality and prefix counts start empty over an empty map and track every insert/remove. Commit rollback via Drop exists only under cfg(test) (commit/guard.rs:172-179), so no production path rewinds a store without updating counts.
  • ConstraintValidationIndexPut keys are validated to the candidate index generation, which is outside the accepted cardinality domain, so leaving them out of maintenance is sound (commit/recovery.rs:1888-1921; commit/schema_publication.rs:870-908). Reverse-relation keys are System kind and excluded from all counts (index/cardinality.rs:866-869).
  • Startup/marker recovery resets live projections and folds the entire tail before verify, and queries are refused until then (commit/recovery.rs:336-349, 405-409, 130-151).
  • Exact numeric fold semantics match the row path. Eligibility: non-nullable Int32 target, unfiltered field-path index whose first key is the target, all key fields non-null, no filter/HAVING/ORDER BY (sql/lowering/aggregate/command/binding.rs:53-58, 121-168; query/plan/pipeline.rs:511-536). SUM returns Decimal scale 0 or NULL on empty; AVG uses the same average_decimal_terms_checked (executor/aggregate/exact_terminal.rs:255-270 vs executor/aggregate/value_reducer.rs:290-304). i32 x u64 terms in i128 cannot overflow realistically.
  • Entity counts used for destructive DDL and row-local proofs (schema/sql_ddl.rs:350-362, schema/application.rs:2620-2664) are unaffected by migration staging, because the data store is never materialized-folded. Migration rewrite rows keep their keys, so presence is unchanged (schema/migration_execution.rs:586-598).

Heap caches under the IC query-call model (performance)

4 findings

I traced every heap cache that the query-call model touches: ACCEPTED_SCHEMA_RUNTIME_ROOTS (C1), the per-store SchemaStore accepted_bundle_cache (C2), the query-plan cache (C3), the SQL compiled-command cache (C4), and the persisted flags (migration gate, recovered keys, marker hint). For each I checked which lifecycle event fills it or invalidates it, and whether that happens in a replicated message. The gap's main premise is partly wrong. C1 is pre-warmed in a replicated context: driver.rs:52-58 does it on every watchdog convergence, it was added in C37 and is documented in startup-readiness.md:113-122. Query-mode cold costs are also measured: sql_perf_audit.rs compares cold query calls with warm update calls, and the 0.261 I1/C37/C48 docs record about 34.6M instructions cold versus about 2.0M warm for the ~80-entity SQL fixture. C3 and C4 cannot be pre-warmed generically and are always cold for query-only traffic; this is measured and does not affect correctness. At the measured ~0.4M instructions per minimal entity, a cold C1 stays under the 5B query limit even at 4,096 entities. Only schemas with hundreds of heavy entities or multi-MiB bundles get close, and there queries would trap rather than fail typed, because cold compile is charged to per-entity 30B maintenance budgets. The real residual gaps are these. (1) Schema publications on heap stores never wake the watchdog, so C1 stays cold for query traffic across the whole database until an unrelated update call. (2) Folding a schema batch after C1 was already rebuilt for the new root leaves C2 empty, and C1 hits never refill it. Every admitted-root cardinality consumer then silently falls back, and query calls re-decode the whole bundle, until the next write. (3) Adjacent to the gap: canonical accepted authority has no cache at all. Fold-mode journal validation re-decodes and re-verifies the whole canonical bundle for each ConstraintValidationIndexPut record (up to 256 per unique-validation page). This is O(records × bundle) unbudgeted watchdog work that can trap deterministically for large bundles.

Checked and sound
  • C1 is warmed in a replicated message before the watchdog goes quiescent, on every convergence (crates/icydb-core/src/db/startup/driver.rs:52-58). That warm also primes the migration gate (live_schema_checkpoint.rs:626-649 via Db::ensure_recovered_state, mod.rs:264-267) and fills C2 for every store, because AcceptedSchemaRuntimeRoot::compile walks every accepted entity (session/accepted_schema.rs:125-141, 50-61).
  • Journaled-store schema publications write journal batches with a nonzero sequence. So CommitGuard.retained_journal_debt is true (commit/guard.rs:290), finish_commit wakes the watchdog (guard.rs:334-335), and C1 is recompiled once folding completes (driver.rs:56).
  • C1 stays consistent: a hit requires every store root to be equal (accepted_schema.rs:436-445), compile re-checks incarnation and roots before publishing (accepted_schema.rs:460-469), and SQL DDL invalidates explicitly (session/sql/ddl.rs:248, 326, 362, 393, 424, 479, 535).
  • The shared plan-cache key binds runtime-root identity, schema revision and index visibility (session/query/cache.rs:368-386, 489-494). Plans built on unavailable cardinality evidence re-check the lifecycle stamp on every hit (cache.rs:182-201, 287-291). The cache is bounded to 1024 entries and 4 MiB retained (cache.rs:37-38) and only publishes after preparation succeeds (cache.rs:311-322).
  • The SQL compiled-command key binds surface, entity path, runtime-root identity, revision, version, fingerprint and SQL text (session/sql/cache.rs:49-58), and the per-command plan slot re-checks the fingerprint (session/sql/compiled/command.rs:125-135, 159-172).
  • Cache warmth never changes results. Every miss recompiles from current accepted authority, and query-call insertions are simply discarded; no correctness path depends on a cache filled by a query call.
  • Ordinary admission is a state-only read in query calls: recovered-domain flag plus marker probe (commit/recovery.rs:126-151). Those flags are set by the replicated watchdog, so query calls neither drive recovery nor need to persist anything.
  • The audit harness measures query-mode cold costs and update-mode warm costs separately (testing/integration/tests/sql_perf_audit.rs:73-92, 233-320; canisters/audit/sql_perf/src/lib.rs:1999, 2007). Runtime-root cold versus warm query costs are recorded in docs/design/0.261-entity-rename/i1-read-investigation.md:20-31 and c37-runtime-preparation.md:69-77.
  • Entity metrics deliberately skip query-mode recording (docs/contracts/RESOURCE_MODEL.md:381-383).

Candid interface stability of generated endpoints and decode quotas

4 findings

I probed gap #9 (Candid stability and decode quotas). I could not run cargo or candid-extractor, so instead I wrote a script that pulls the declared shape of every CandidType item (144 items at HEAD) from each release tag since v0.248.0 and diffs them. I also traced the generated endpoint wrappers (crates/icydb/src/lib.rs:655-1034) through the ic-cdk-macros 0.20.3 decode path and the candid 0.10.37 depth guard and opt-recovery code, and read the CLI's decode sites. HEAD is the v0.261.16 release, and no endpoint signature or DTO shape has changed since v0.257.4. Generated endpoints take only `text`, `()` or the two migration DTOs that the golden file already pins, so the argument side is stable and not recursive. IcyDB never decodes Candid in production code. The Error record carries only numeric codes, so it stays forward-compatible. Four gaps remain. First, `icydb_schema` puts every entity's full description into one reply with no size guard; with three entities shaped like the repo's own "reachable" test schema, every call traps. Second, only the migration ABI is gated, and past releases changed wire shapes in patch versions (0.249.4, 0.252.5, 0.257.3, 0.257.4). The CLI decodes strictly and never checks the canister's version. The "0.218" golden has itself been rewritten twice, so it detects changes but does not check compatibility. Third, recursive input DTOs have no depth bound while decoding on wasm, and FilterExpr's error wrapper grows quadratically. Fourth, the RETURNING size check measures a hand-written copy of the response type instead of the envelope that is actually sent.

Checked and sound
  • Argument ABI of generated endpoints is fixed and non-recursive: every SQL endpoint takes `sql: String`, snapshot/metrics/schema/fixtures take no args, and only icydb_schema_migrate/icydb_schema_migration take DTOs (crates/icydb/src/lib.rs:655-1034); those two are pinned byte-exactly by render_schema_migration_endpoint_abi vs contracts/0.218/schema-migration-endpoints.did (testing/integration/src/canister_artifact.rs:532-550, 800-806).
  • ic-cdk 0.20.3 default arg decoding applies DecoderConfig with skipping_quota=10000 and no decoding quota, and unwraps (traps) on decode failure before the handler runs (ic-cdk-macros-0.20.3/src/export.rs:255-261); no-arg endpoints perform no Candid decoding at all. A decode trap is per-message and rolls back.
  • IcyDB library crates never decode Candid in production: every candid::decode_one/Decode! site in icydb-core/icydb/icydb-schema is inside #[cfg(test)] modules; persisted formats use custom byte codecs, so no init/post_upgrade/timer/recovery path depends on Candid decoding. Lifecycle wrappers without user args use `init(hidden = true)` with no decoding (lib.rs:430-438).
  • Candid label hash collisions in derived types (including generated entity structs, icydb-model-macros entity.rs:703,1091) are rejected at compile time by candid_derive 0.10.37 (derive.rs:175-176, 440-441).
  • The public Error record uses only numeric code/class/origin/fact tags (crates/icydb/src/error.rs:101-108). Unknown classes fall back to the code's class (error.rs:227-232), and the CLI renders unknown codes through a registry fallback (crates/icydb-cli/src/diagnostic.rs:237-245, 593-600), so new diagnostics do not break older decoders.
  • FilterExpr closes Candid's opt-recovery hole: its custom Deserialize makes nested failures terminal, so an invalid supplied filter inside `opt` errors instead of becoming None (crates/icydb-core/src/db/query/expr/filter.rs:668-680, tests 1566-1622).
  • After decoding, query input admission bounds FilterExpr/FilterValue depth at 128 and nodes at 4096. It checks before each descent, so over-deep decoded filters get the typed InputDepthExceeded before any recursive lowering (crates/icydb-core/src/db/query/admission/input.rs:18-40, 64-116).
  • No public Candid drift since v0.257.4: a structural diff of all CandidType items across every tag v0.248.0..v0.261.16 shows the last shape changes at v0.257.3 (MetricsReport) and v0.257.4 (StorageReport). Manual CandidType impl files (u256, key, decimal/wire, atom, time_atoms, value/input, value/output, nat_big, int_big, unit) and the endpoints! signatures are unchanged since v0.259.0.
  • icydb_query's reply guard measures the exact delivered `Result<&SqlQueryResult, Error>` envelope and returns the typed E258 rather than trapping (crates/icydb/src/db/sql/types.rs:116-131, test 243-259). Integrity replies are bounded (MAX_QUICK_RETURNED_FINDINGS=64, crates/icydb-core/src/db/integrity.rs:314). Public RETURNING is capped at 1 MiB (write_policy/model.rs:11-12), well under the 2 MiB update reply limit.
  • The Candid/Wasm method manifests agree: inspect_canister_artifacts requires that the Candid service methods and modes match the raw Wasm exports (canister_artifact.rs:371-407).
  • The CLI decodes strict typed structs built from the same workspace version (Decode! at shell/mod.rs:110-113,129; observability/metrics.rs:73-84; snapshot.rs:46-50; schema.rs:69-73; migration.rs:199). On native targets candid's stacker-based recursion guard protects it from deeply nested replies.

All findings

Every finding with its location, failure scenario, recommendation and verification trail. Duplicates reported by more than one reviewer are merged into the first report; switch merging off to see each one.

307 shown
criticalreproducedindex-access-1 · correctness · medium confidence
Filtered (partial) unique index: conflict re-check ignores the index predicate, so a committed batch cannot be folded or replayed (wedge risk)
crates/icydb-core/src/db/index/plan/unique.rs:50

Failure scenario

Journaled store with `index(fields=["account_id"], unique, predicate="is_primary = true")`. The canonical state holds A {acct:7, is_primary:true}. One batch sets A.is_primary=false and inserts or updates B {acct:7, is_primary:true}. At write time, if A is processed first, A's index removal is staged, B's probe sees the entry overridden, and the batch commits and is journaled. If B is processed first, the write is falsely rejected with a unique violation. When fold_oldest_journal_batch or startup recovery replays the batch, preparing B probes canonical and finds (7, pkA). has_primary_row_override(A) is true and A's final row still builds key (7) because the predicate is ignored. Result: unique_violation. The oldest journal batch can never fold, so online convergence stalls. After the next upgrade, recovery never completes and ensure_recovery_admitted returns recovery_pending for all ordinary work until a code fix ships.

Evidence

UniqueKeyAuthority::build_index_key_from_row_slots calls IndexKey::new_from_slots_with_accepted_field_path_index_primary_key_value / ..._expression_... directly (unique.rs:50-74). Those builders (build.rs:61-71, 421-435) never evaluate accepted_index.predicate_sql(); only the *_with_membership_structural helpers in plan/mod.rs:62-106 do. In validate_unique_constraint_structural_impl the final row of the conflicting PK is rebuilt this way (unique.rs:222-239). If the components are unchanged, the batch-override release is skipped and unique_violation is returned. Replay/fold goes through prepare_row_commit_batch_for_replay (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:393-429) with CanonicalCommitReader. That reader serves batch final rows but reads index state from canonical only (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:83-107), so earlier ops in the same batch are never staged. The preflight overlay, by contrast, stages earlier rows (commit_window.rs:531-533). Filtered unique indexes are first-class: nullable unique indexes must carry a predicate guard, and the macro test shows `unique, predicate = "active = true"`.

Recommendation

Rebuild the conflicting row's membership using the same predicate-aware path as mutation planning: compile the accepted index predicate once, pass the PredicateProgram into UniqueKeyAuthority, and treat a predicate miss as released membership. Add replay and fold tests for filtered unique indexes where a row leaves the predicate and another row enters it in the same batch, in both op orders. Consider making preflight acceptance independent of batch order.

Verifier (confirmed): I traced this end to end. UniqueKeyAuthority::build_index_key_from_row_slots (plan/unique.rs:50-74) calls IndexKey::new_from_slots_with_accepted_*_primary_key_value directly. Those builders (key/build.rs:421-451) never evaluate the predicate. Only the *_with_membership_structural helpers do (plan/mod.rs:62-106), and plan_index_mutation passes them a compiled PredicateProgram (plan/mod.rs:219-222); validate_unique_* gets none. In validate_unique_constraint_structural_impl (unique.rs:208-239), a conflicting row whose final image left the predicate but kept the same key columns still rebuilds the same components, so the batch-override release is skipped and unique_violation is returned. Replay and fold path: fold_selected_journal_head -> prepare_recovered_row_transitions (recovery.rs:797) -> prepare_row_commit_batch_for_replay (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:393-429) with CanonicalCommitReader. That reader serves batch final rows but reads index ranges from canonical only (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:83-107). No mode flag skips unique validation. The write path is different: PreflightStoreOverlay stages earlier ops' index effects (commit_window.rs:302-318, 531-533) and hides the tombstoned entry during the merge (commit_window.rs:410-424). So a batch whose ops run in the right order (e.g. SQL UPDATE flipping is_primary for pkA<pkB) commits and is journaled, and then fails on fold. The reverse order is falsely rejected at write time. Filtered unique indexes with predicates on non-key columns pass acceptance: validate_index_semantic_contract returns Ok when all key sources never omit (integrity/nullable_unique.rs:63-77), and the macro supports `unique, predicate = "active = true"`. A failed fold leaves recovery stuck in the Fold stage (recovery.rs:333-341), and ensure_recovery_admitted then returns recovery_pending (recovery.rs:141-143). Nothing in-band recovers until a code fix ships, so critical fits the rubric's wedge criterion.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, critical): I could not refute the claim. I traced it end to end and it holds. The unique conflict re-check rebuilds the conflicting row's index key without evaluating the index predicate. It only releases the committed membership when the rebuilt components differ, the row is gone, or the builder returns None. A same-batch "flip the filter column" transition therefore still looks like a live collision. At write time the preflight overlay hides this whenever the flipping row comes earlier in the batch, because it stages earlier prepared index ops. Replay/fold uses CanonicalCommitReader, which reads the canonical index only and stages nothing. So a batch that committed and was journaled deterministically fails to prepare during fold. No guard blocks the path: - Unique validation is not gated by CommitPrepareMode::RecoveryReplay. - Batches keep input order, so the journal records match that order. - Filtered unique indexes are supported (the macro accepts `unique, predicate = ...`, and nullable-unique indexes require a predicate). The one sub-case that escapes is the nullable-unique `IS NOT NULL` guard: the key builder likely returns None for null components, which triggers the release. Consequence: online fold fails and the timer driver publishes a terminal JournalRecovery receipt. The journal backlog can no longer drain, so the backlog admission gate eventually blocks writes. After any upgrade, startup recovery is stuck in the Fold stage forever and ensure_recovery_admitted returns recovery_pending for all ordinary work until a code fix ships. The trigger is a realistic "swap the primary row" atomic batch through a public facade API. By the rubric this is a way to wedge a canister, so critical. The B-first ordering additionally causes a false unique violation at write time (high on its own).
Skeptic · intent (upheld, critical): I could not refute this claim. The code does what the claim says, and neither the docs nor the tests treat it as intended. 1) Predicate omitted. `UniqueKeyAuthority::build_index_key_from_row_slots` (crates/icydb-core/src/db/index/plan/unique.rs:50-74) calls `IndexKey::new_from_slots_with_accepted_{field_path,expression}_index_primary_key_value` directly. Those reach `build_accepted_*_index_key_from_slots` (crates/icydb-core/src/db/index/key/build.rs:421-451), and build.rs never references a predicate. Only the `*_with_membership_structural` helpers in plan/mod.rs:62-106 run the accepted predicate program. So in unique.rs:222-239, the batch-final row of the conflicting PK rebuilds the same components even when that row no longer matches the index predicate. Components match, so the code returns `unique_violation` and never releases the membership. 2) The contract says this should release. docs/contracts/TRANSACTION_SEMANTICS.md:115-119 says unique-index preparation observes the complete final overlay, and that "An updated or deleted old row releases its previous membership". The design intends batch-final release: CanonicalCommitReader keeps `batch_final_rows` "for same-batch uniqueness release proofs" (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:41-43). The existing tests cover only swaps and delete/reuse (session/write.rs:4381 and 8561; CHANGELOG 0.229 note). No test covers a row leaving a partial index. Filtered unique indexes are first-class: WRITE_ADMISSION.md:85, the SQL_SUBSET `partial_unique_index_v1` semantics, SQL DDL `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE`, and the macro `unique, predicate = ...`. Nothing documents that a row leaving the predicate in a batch is unsupported. The code is the side that is wrong. 3) The write path depends on op order. - The preflight overlay loads every final row up front (commit_window.rs:283-303), so `has_primary_row_override` is true for A. - It stages index ops only from earlier rows (commit_window.rs:530-533). - With order [A leaves the predicate, B enters under the same key], A's staged index removal hides (7,pkA) from B's probe, and the batch commits and is journaled. - With order [B, A], the batch is falsely rejected. That alone is a contract violation of high severity. 4) Replay fails every time. Fold goes `fold_selected_journal_head` -> `prepare_recovered_row_transitions` (recovery.rs:753-811) -> `prepare_row_commit_batch_for_replay` (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:393-429). That uses CanonicalCommitReader: - index reads are canonical only (lines 83-107), with no staging of earlier ops; - row reads return batch-final rows (lines 62-80). - Unique validation has no mode gate (prepare.rs:421-485; plan/mod.rs:342-352). B's probe finds (7,pkA) in canonical. The override is true, and A's final row {7, false} rebuilds key [7] because the predicate is ignored. Result: `unique_violation` on every attempt, whatever the op order. 5) Impact is not lower than claimed. - Fold errors propagate as `StartupRecoveryFailure` with no quarantine or skip (recovery.rs:843-852). Canonical state never changes, so the oldest batch never folds. - Online: convergence stalls. Retained debt grows until backlog pressure (MAX_RETAINED_JOURNAL_BATCHES = 64, backlog_admission.rs:329) rejects new writes. The claim did not mention this. - After an upgrade: recovery sits in the Fold stage forever, and `ensure_recovery_admitted` (recovery.rs:130-151) returns `recovery_pending` for all guarded reads and writes. DURABILITY.md says guarded reads and writes fail closed. - Schema escapes such as dropping the index require converged journals (DURABILITY.md:179-181). The owner cannot recover without a library fix. Journaled is the documented production mode. The trigger is a realistic pattern: "switch primary" or soft-delete-and-reinsert under `unique(...) WHERE is_primary = true` or `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`, done in one atomic batch or in one multi-row SQL UPDATE whose scan order puts the exiting row first. One nuance that softens but does not refute: the journal bytes are valid, so a corrected library would unwedge the canister on upgrade with no data loss. Pure `IS NOT NULL` guards are not affected, because a null component omits the key and takes the release path. The bug needs a predicate on a non-key field.

Two-sided PK range `pk >= a AND pk < b` has its predicate stripped although KeyRange end is inclusive: the row with pk == b is returned, counted, updated or deleted
crates/icydb-core/src/db/query/plan/primary_key_access_proof.rs:131

Failure scenario

Entity with a Nat64 PK and rows id 0..16. Typed/dynamic `filter(FieldRef::new("id").gte(nat64(2)) & FieldRef::new("id").lt(nat64(5)))` produces Strict compares (Nat literals compile to Strict), selects KeyRange{2,5}, and strips the predicate. It returns ids [2,3,4,5] instead of [2,3,4], and exact COUNT returns 4. SQL `DELETE FROM T WHERE id >= 'a' AND id < 'm'` on a Text/Ulid/Principal PK takes the same path through the mutation selector (session/sql/execute/write/delete.rs uses the same planner via into_load_selection). It deletes the row whose PK equals 'm': silent data loss from the most common windowing idiom. A covering PK-only projection over the same KeyRange also emits the extra key.

Evidence

primary_key_range_from_and (planner/range/extract.rs:80-81) maps `Gte`->start and `Lt|Lte`->end, then builds `AccessPlan::key_range_bounds(start, end)`. Its comment says 'The residual predicate owns exclusivity'. AccessPath::KeyRange is documented as 'Present endpoints are inclusive; the predicate retains any stricter comparison semantics' (access/path.rs:499), and PrimaryRangeKeyStream::new_bounds uses `Some(end) => Bound::Included(end.to_raw()?)` (executor/stream/access/physical.rs:894). But PrimaryKeyAccessProof::from_access maps any two-sided KeyRange to `HalfOpenRange{start,end}` (primary_key_access_proof.rs:47-48). matches_primary_key_half_open_range accepts exactly `[Gte start, Lt end]` (line 130-131). strip_redundant_primary_key_predicate_for_exact_access (pipeline.rs:834-849) then returns `stripped()`, and assemble_query_model_plan drops both the predicate and the filter expression (`logical_inputs.without_filter_expr()`, pipeline.rs:205-213). No residual survives, so execution scans [a, b] inclusive with no filter. Existing tests cover only one-sided PK ranges (session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak/scalar_page_limits.rs:261-316) and the planner-level shape (and_primary_range_copies_valid_interval_endpoints). No end-to-end test covers a two-sided `>= / <` range.

Recommendation

Remove the HalfOpenRange proof. Alternatively, make it match the inclusive semantics (strip only `[Gte start, Lte end]`), or change KeyRange to carry explicit `Bound`s so `Lt` lowers to `Excluded`. Add end-to-end load, count and delete tests for `pk >= a AND pk < b`, `pk > a AND pk <= b` and BETWEEN on Nat64 and Text PKs, and assert the executed row sets.

Migration staging/abort folds the live overlay into canonical outside the journal protocol: durable prefix counts drift (rows vanish from indexed reads) and later folds wedge on count underflow
crates/icydb-core/src/db/index/store.rs:816

Failure scenario

Journaled store with entity User and an accepted unique index on email; the cardinality generation is Ready; the canister is built with `migration`. 1) The controller starts a physical migration of User that changes an index generation (Advance → Prepared). Ordinary writes continue. 2) The app inserts user u1 {email:'a@x'}. Batch B1 stays in the tail as retained debt. 3) Before the watchdog folds B1, the controller aborts (or advances into Validating). cleanup_migration_staging_page rewrites canonical index = canonical ∪ live, so (email 'a@x', u1) is now canonical and the prefix delta is 0. 4) The watchdog folds B1: data +1, but the index prefix change is 0 because the key is already canonical. The durable count for 'a@x' is 0. 5) `SELECT * FROM User WHERE email = 'a@x'` sees exact count 0, skips the scan and returns no row. `COUNT(*) WHERE email='a@x'` returns 0. This holds for every row written in the window until the next schema publication for that store. 6) The user later deletes u1. Folding that batch computes 0 - 1: checked_sub fails, store_corruption. A terminal JournalRecovery receipt is published, the watchdog stops, and every db() call fails. Redeploying the same Wasm refolds the same batch and fails again. Only patched code recovers. The mirror case (a pulled-forward delete) leaves permanent over-counts, so COUNT results are wrong.

Evidence

fold_journaled_materialized_view snapshots the visible index (canonical minus tombstones plus ALL live entries, index/store.rs:930-960), runs canonical.clear_new(), re-inserts everything (831-834), clears live/tombstones and resets the prefix delta to zero at the SAME watermark (837-841). The journal watermark, positions and the schema-store cardinality header are untouched. Production callers under `feature = "migration"`: stage_migration_index_entries on every Validating page with staged keys (schema/migration_validation.rs:575-582, called from schema/application.rs:1313), and cleanup_migration_staging_page on every Abort page for every derived-domain store, even when nothing is removed (schema/migration_execution.rs:1073-1078, called from schema/application.rs:859). Abort is legal from Prepared (schema/migration_record.rs:75-79), and Prepared 'still admits ordinary row reads and writes' (schema/live_schema_checkpoint.rs:652-653). The journal is drained first only when a prior migration record exists (schema/application.rs:1105-1116). The migration record publish with no candidates writes only database control (commit/schema_publication.rs:240-245), so the Ready header stays valid. When the pulled-forward batch B later folds, maintenance takes 'previous' from the already-rewritten canonical index (commit/recovery.rs:1163-1169), so the prefix delta nets to 0 and the durable count never includes the entry. Reads compute base+delta (registry/handle.rs:628-654). Some(0) skips a single-prefix scan (executor/stream/access/physical.rs:316) and prunes multi-lookup branches (executor/stream/access/scan.rs:176-187). A later removal of the entry underflows at schema/store.rs:1358-1365, returning store_corruption from prepare_folded_cardinality_maintenance (commit/recovery.rs:998-1005). The watchdog records it via record_recovery_failure (startup/driver.rs:66, 210-236), and STORE_CORRUPTION is a persisted terminal code (startup/mod.rs:116-124). The fold's unique re-check also reads the canonical index (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:83-106; index/plan/unique.rs:187-217). A future entry pulled forward for another PK whose row is not yet in canonical data makes it return index_unique_validation_row_required, which is store corruption (error/mod.rs:1337-1339): a second wedge path.

Recommendation

Remove fold_journaled_materialized_view from production paths. Candidate keys use planner-invisible IndexIds: stage them through journaled SchemaMigrationIndexPut records with positions (as rewrite pages already do), or write/remove only those candidate keys directly in canonical over the candidate IndexId ranges, never the whole live overlay. Until then, require every journal tail to be drained, with writes blocked, before any staging or abort page. Restart the cardinality generation whenever canonical changes outside the fold. Add a test that aborts or validates a migration with unfolded ordinary writes in the tail, then checks the prefix counts and that a subsequent delete still folds.

Renaming or moving a journaled store's Rust type is treated as STORE_CORRUPTION and permanently bricks the canister; reverting does not clear it
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/store.rs:2269

Failure scenario

v1 declares `#[store(canister="App", storage(journaled(key="transfers")))] pub struct TransferStore;` in module app_schema::stores. v2 moves it to app_schema::db (or renames the struct or crate). Stable keys and the registry quartet are unchanged, so ic-memory and convergence accept the upgrade. Tick 1: the accepted bundle says 'app_schema::stores::TransferStore' but the registry says 'app_schema::db::TransferStore'. That is store_corruption, which writes a terminal JournalRecovery receipt, and every db() call returns StartupFailure. The operator reverts to v1: the journal allocation and proof are byte-identical, so the same receipt matches in post_upgrade, the watchdog is never scheduled, and the canister stays failed. No later wasm can clear it. The only escape is reinstall, which loses all data. The permanence mechanism is the one in integrity-relations-1. The new part is the trigger: a routine refactor that the docs present as identity-neutral is classified as persisted corruption.

Evidence

Store identity at runtime is the Rust path `module_path::Ident` (crates/icydb-model/src/node/def.rs:36-38; build/actor/mod.rs:126-132). That path is registered as the registry path (build/actor/db/store.rs register_journaled_store(#store_path,...)). Only the memory keys are rename-independent (node/store.rs:642-645; test at node/store.rs:967-990 'Rust names locate generated code; only the explicit key names memory'; docs/guides/schema-authoring.md:378 'Rust renames and declaration order do not change these keys'). Accepted bundles persist the store path at lowering, and current_accepted_runtime_entities returns store_corruption when bundle.store_path() != registered path (schema/store.rs:2269-2271; the same check appears at 2296, 2321, 2357, 2400). On the first timer tick after upgrade, recover_domain calls initialize_missing_entity_mutation_revisions (commit/recovery.rs:282, also 363/402). That function maps the error through StartupRecoveryFailure::journal_store (recovery.rs:441-455). STORE_CORRUPTION is terminal for every kind (startup/mod.rs:116-124). record_recovery_failure then publishes a JournalRecovery receipt bound to incarnation, journal allocation (key-derived, unchanged by the rename) and journal proof (driver.rs:219-268; journal/store.rs:891-900, counters only). observe() matches that receipt for any wasm whose journaled store has the same key and unchanged tail counters (startup/observe.rs:66-69,112-157,211-229). It returns Err, and the watchdog is set Inactive (build/actor/db/store.rs:148-166).

Recommendation

Make the durable store identity the allocation key, not the Rust path. Bind bundles, database/store identities, lineage keys and live checkpoints to the key, or re-path accepted bundles when the registry quartet matches. At minimum, classify a bundle/registry path mismatch as a non-terminal configuration error (Unsupported, no receipt) so reverting recovers. Add a PocketIC upgrade test that renames and moves a journaled store type.

criticalreproducedschema-catalogs-1 · durability · high confidence
Record-member rename is metadata-only, but stored record values use member names as keys, so every existing row with that record becomes undecodable
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/migration_planner.rs:659

Failure scenario

Entity Item { profile: Profile { nickname: Text, owner_id: Nat64 } } has 10k rows. The developer renames Profile.nickname to label with a generated `renames(record_field(..))` migration and no transforms. The plan is classified metadata-only, and the candidate passes validation and publishes, because only entity fields, nested leaves and defaults are re-checked, not rows. After publication, every read of an Item row decodes the profile slot, finds key "nickname" where the catalog expects "label", and fails with persisted_row_decode_corruption. Updates and deletes also decode the before-image and fail, and relation checks through profile members fail with a value mismatch. All existing rows become unreadable and undeletable until another migration renames the member back. The same applies to List<Profile>, enum payloads containing Profile, and every store holding a copy of the type.

Evidence

migration_planner.rs:659-697 handles `SchemaMigrationRename::RecordField` by rekeying the source binding and calling `store.composites.with_renamed_record_field(type_id, field, to, ..)` (composite_catalog.rs:114-144). That call renames the member and re-sorts members by name. `physical` is computed from transforms only (migration_planner.rs:313-316: `.any(|t| !t.transforms().is_empty())`), so a rename-only plan has requires_physical_validation()==false and is published as a metadata candidate (application.rs:1062-1092). Stored record values, however, are canonical maps keyed by member name: normalize_composite writes `(CanonicalValue::Text(name), ..)` (admission.rs:684). On read, decode_runtime_value_from_row_contract -> decode_admitted_value_from_accepted_field_contract -> admit_canonical -> validate_composite rejects `if name != field.name()` (admission.rs:945) and maps the error to `persisted_row_decode_corruption()` (data/persisted_row/canonical.rs:205). Nested relation extraction also looks members up by their current name (relation/reverse_index.rs:1807-1826). The planner test `complete_metadata_rename_set_preserves_every_accepted_identity_without_aliases` plans nickname->label with no transforms and never writes or reads rows. Contract: PERSISTED_FORMAT_INVENTORY.md:43 says 'Editable variant and member names are therefore never identity authority'; the 0.218 design (line 615) claims record-member layout is unchanged by the rename.

Recommendation

Either persist record members keyed by stable CompositeFieldId (and resolve names only at the output boundary), as the contract implies; or classify any RecordField rename reachable from stored rows as a physical rewrite that rewrites map keys (and rebuilds affected member-path indexes) before publication. Add an end-to-end test: insert rows, apply the rename migration, then read, update and delete those rows.

Verifier (confirmed): I traced the full path and could not refute it. The planner sets `physical` from transforms only (migration_planner.rs:313-316). The RecordField rename arm (659-697) rekeys the binding and calls with_renamed_record_field (composite_catalog.rs:114-144), which changes `field.name` and re-sorts members by name. RecordFieldFragment derives source_key from name (icydb-schema fragment.rs:992-998), so the rename really changes the member name. With no transforms, `programs` must be empty (migration_planner.rs:356). application.rs:1062-1150 then runs preflight_existing_application, which only does removal and row-local-constraint proofs (application.rs:2282-2291), and publishes the metadata candidate with no row scan. Stored record values keep member names as map keys: normalize_composite pushes `(CanonicalValue::Text(name), ..)` (enum_catalog/admission.rs:680-690), and encode_canonical_value_storage_bytes writes the Map keys verbatim (value_storage/canonical.rs:84-90). Composite fields always use the canonical wire (accepted_field_kind.rs:273). On read, decode_runtime_value_from_row_contract (persisted_row/contract.rs:48-65) calls decode_admitted_value_from_accepted_field_contract, whose admit_canonical -> validate_composite rejects `name != field.name()` (admission.rs:945), mapped to persisted_row_decode_corruption (canonical.rs:205). No CompositeFieldId-keyed row encoding exists anywhere in data/. No test exercises a record-field rename over existing rows; the only uses are the planner unit test and the macro UI test. The 0.218 design (line 613-615) claims record-member layout is unchanged, which contradicts the name-keyed value storage, so the code (or the design claim) is wrong. The rows can be recovered by renaming back, but after publication the accepted schema and the stored rows disagree, which is durable-state inconsistency. Critical stands.

The ordinary lowerer reconciles against the already-renamed working catalog, so it detects no residual difference. Caveats: trigger is controller-initiated (not attacker), and raw bytes remain intact, so immediate rename-back before new writes is recoverable. Contract PERSISTED_FORMAT_INVENTORY.md:43 ('member names never identity authority') is contradicted by the value encoding; code (or its encoding) is the side that looks wrong given the migration design's intent.
Skeptic · intent (upheld, critical): I could not refute this claim. The code does what the claim says, and neither the docs nor the tests show the behavior is intended. 1) Record values store member names as keys. normalize_composite (crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/enum_catalog/admission.rs:684) writes (CanonicalValue::Text(name), ..). encode_canonical_value_storage_bytes (crates/icydb-core/src/db/data/structural_field/value_storage/canonical.rs:81-86) writes map keys to disk as text. Enums are not affected because they use a store-local type/variant ID envelope. So of the two renames the 0.218 design treats as equivalent, only the record-member one is broken. 2) A rename-only plan is metadata-only and never rewrites rows. `physical` is decided by transforms alone (migration_planner.rs:313-316). That preflight (application.rs:2282-2290) checks entity, field, index and relation removals plus row-local constraints. It has no empty-domain check or row check for composite member names. The candidate is then published directly. 3) The project already knew about this. The 0.213 changelog (docs/changelog/0.213.md:2006-2007) rejected record-member renames because member names are embedded in canonical record values and need a row rewrite. 0.213.21 (CHANGELOG.md:935; docs/changelog/0.213.md:1499-1505) allowed them only when every affected physical domain was exactly empty. The 0.218 explicit-migration design (0.218-design.md:614-616) then wrongly states that record-member layout is unchanged. The guide (docs/guides/schema-migrations.md) says metadata-only transitions preserve stored rows and indexes. Inserts still succeed and write the new name, so the store ends up holding a mix of old-name and new-name rows. At that point no in-product fix works. Renaming back breaks the new rows. A physical migration would decode old rows against the before catalog and re-encode them against the candidate, which fails with a ValueContract finding because the Map keys no longer match. That is a durable inconsistency between accepted schema and stored rows, reached through a documented operator feature. That fits the rubric's critical level. Two mitigating points: the trigger is an operator-authored migration, not attacker input, and the old row bytes are not physically destroyed.

highreproducedcommit-1 · correctness · medium confidence
Online background folding routes batches through the LIVE accepted catalog, so a metadata-only entity rename published with retained debt makes older batches permanently unfoldable
crates/icydb-core/src/db/commit/recovery.rs:2343

Failure scenario

1) A journaled store has entity 'Item'. The app inserts rows; the batch B1 (RowPut entity_path='Item') stays in the tail as retained debt, as it does after every write until the watchdog folds it. 2) Before the watchdog runs, an operator calls migrate_schema Advance with a metadata-only rename to 'CatalogItem'. B2 (AcceptedSchemaPublish) is appended and the live schema projection now shows only 'CatalogItem'. 3) The watchdog calls continue_recovery_with_failure_authority, which takes the online path because recovered, not in progress and no marker. It selects B1 (lowest database commit sequence), and journal_batch_store_handle looks up 'Item' in the live catalog: not found, so store_corruption. The failure is classified terminal (StartupFailureKind::JournalRecovery + STORE_CORRUPTION) and a startup failure receipt is published. B1 can never fold online, and every later write adds debt behind it until Gate 2 rejects all writes with the 'retryable' backlog-pressure error (64 batches). Depending on how the receipt is bound, admission may fail sooner. Only an upgrade, which resets overlays so live == canonical again, clears it. The same inconsistency breaks Replay of a retained post-rename marker after an upgrade (apply_marker_live_schema_checkpoints/publish_marker_bound_journal_batches resolve 'CatalogItem' against canonical-only state).

Evidence

The online fold (fold_selected_journal_head, JournalFoldProjection::OnlinePositioned, lines 976-991) calls validate_journal_batch_records(.., Fold, ..) -> validate_journal_batch_envelope (1771) -> journal_batch_store_handle(db, batch) (2241). For RowPut/RowDelete that resolves via journal_row_record_store_handle -> recovery_accepted_runtime_entity_for_path -> `db.accepted_runtime_entity_for_path(entity_path).map_err(|_| InternalError::store_corruption())` (2343-2352). That lookup reads the live root (SchemaStore::current_accepted_schema_root -> accepted_root_slot_bytes -> get_raw_snapshot, overlay first), not the canonical one. IdentityRangeAdvance does the same through accepted_runtime_entity_for_tag (2312-2316). In contrast, prepare_row_commit_batch_for_replay is canonical-first (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:405-409), and validate_journal_batch_record's Fold branches use canonical lookups (1819-1823, 1928-1933). The metadata-only migration path publishes a journaled AcceptedSchemaPublish without draining retained debt (schema/application.rs:1145; only the physical path drains, 1106-1115). A rename changes snapshot.entity_path ('Item' -> 'CatalogItem', entity_rename.rs:74). The existing rename tests only recover through forget_recovered_domain_for_tests + startup recovery (entity_rename.rs:456-457). That path resets overlays first, so live == canonical, which hides the bug.

Recommendation

Make batch-to-store routing independent of the live projection in Fold mode. Resolve row entity paths and identity-owner tags against the canonical accepted catalog (canonical_runtime_entity_for_path/tag), with the same canonical-then-live fallback prepare_row_commit_batch_for_replay uses for non-journaled stores. Alternatively, route journaled batches by the tail they were selected from, since select_oldest_journal_head already knows the handle. Also check that relation projection binding in the fold (RelationConstraintProjection::bind -> accepted_relation_from_binding/relation_target_store_binding) does not resolve target paths through the live catalog. Add a test that inserts, applies a metadata rename, then drives continue_recovery WITHOUT forget_recovered_domain_for_tests. Separately, consider draining or refusing metadata migrations while journal debt is retained.

Verifier (confirmed): I traced this end to end and it holds. The online path is continue_recovery_with_failure_authority (recovery.rs:231-232/250) -> continue_online_convergence -> fold_oldest_journal_batch(OnlinePositioned). It selects the batch with the lowest database commit sequence (recovery.rs:854-934). Row transitions resolve against the canonical catalog first: prepare_recovered_row_transitions -> prepare_row_commit_batch_for_replay (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:405-409), and CanonicalCommitReader uses canonical_runtime_entity_for_tag (runtime_entity_catalog.rs:73). But validate_journal_batch_records (recovery.rs:1699) always calls validate_journal_batch_envelope -> journal_batch_store_handle (1771, 2241) -> journal_row_record_store_handle -> recovery_accepted_runtime_entity_for_path (2343-2352). That calls db.accepted_runtime_entity_for_path, which walks current_accepted_schema_bundle_ref / accepted_root_slot_bytes -> get_raw_snapshot, the overlay-first live root (schema/store.rs:2211-2217, 3408-3413). The canonical root is read separately via canonical_root_slot_bytes (3415). The Fold branches of validate_journal_batch_record do use canonical lookups (1819-1823, 1928-1933), so the envelope is the odd one out. Writes do leave retained tail debt that only the watchdog folds; the test session/write.rs:8232-8279 builds 64 retained batches and then drains them one page at a time. The metadata migration path (schema/application.rs:1130-1152) publishes via publish_candidates_atomically. For journaled stores that appends an AcceptedSchemaPublish batch and applies apply_journaled_accepted_schema_candidate to the live overlay only (commit/schema_publication.rs:758-763). There is no drain and no tail-empty gate; only the physical branch drains (application.rs:1106-1115), and ensure_recovery_admitted (recovery.rs:130-151) does not require empty tails. The rename test confirms the live entity_path becomes 'CatalogItem' while the entity tag is kept, and that the publication is schema-only (entity_rename.rs:414-418). That test recovers only through forget_recovered_domain_for_tests + startup recovery (456-457), which resets overlays, so it never exercises the online fold. Result: once a rename is published with retained debt, every watchdog tick fails with store_corruption on the retained 'Item' batch. Backlog then grows until Gate 2 rejects writes. An upgrade or restart resets overlays and clears it, so this is not a permanent brick. Rename requires the migration feature. Severity stays high: recovery fails under plausible conditions and writes are wedged until upgrade. One nuance: the IdentityRangeAdvance tag lookup at 2312-2316 is also live-based but is unaffected by a rename, because tags are preserved. It would only matter for entity removal.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could not refute this. There is a real path from public APIs to the failure, and no guard stops it. One limit on reachability: the intended generated migration flow cannot hit it. The bug needs the public facade DbSession::migrate_schema (crates/icydb/src/db/session/catalog.rs:196), which its doc comment describes as "used by generated and handwritten controller endpoints". It must be called with a metadata-only rename proposal while the database is Ready and still has unfolded row batches. Why the generated flow is safe: the rename is compiled into a new wasm, so it only arrives by upgrade. Startup recovery then folds every tail to empty before it marks the domain recovered (recovery.rs:319-349, 843-852). migrate_schema requires that recovered state (application.rs:800). Scalar fast path reports corruption for rows filled by a non-null historical default (ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT)
crates/icydb-core/src/db/data/persisted_row/reader/structural_slot_reader.rs:590

Failure scenario

Table SqlTestUser has rows. Run `ALTER TABLE SqlTestUser ADD COLUMN required_score nat64 NOT NULL DEFAULT 7` (the integration test at sql_canister.rs:3217 does exactly this), then `SELECT name FROM SqlTestUser WHERE required_score = 7`. For each pre-ALTER row, the slot is absent, historical_slot_value returns Nat64(7), and get_scalar returns a Serialize/Corruption error, so the query fails. `OCTET_LENGTH(text_col)` (row_decode/mod.rs:295, projection/eval/scalar.rs:358) and direct projection of CatalogValue scalars (take_direct_projection_value) fail the same way. Projections and SUM work because they use required_cached_value, which is why the existing U256 test passes: it rewrites every row before running WHERE.

Evidence

get_scalar(): `if self.field_bytes.field(slot).is_none() { return match self.contract.historical_slot_value(slot, ...)? { Value::Null => Ok(Some(ScalarSlotValueRef::Null)), _ => Err(InternalError::persisted_row_decode_corruption()) } }`. required_accepted_value_storage_scalar (line ~494-503) has the same `_ => Err(persisted_row_decode_corruption())`. SQL DDL `build_sql_ddl_field_addition_candidate` (schema/mutation/field_allocation.rs:58-62) sets historical_fill = SlotPayload(default), and `derive_sql_ddl_field_addition_accepted_after` (mutation/field.rs:490-499) keeps history_floor, so old rows keep their shorter layout. The predicate fast path (predicate/runtime/mod.rs:748-760, 771-772) calls `required_scalar` -> `get_scalar` for every Scalar-leaf field, and raw-row scan filters use StructuralSlotReader (terminal/page/row_runtime.rs:283-284). relation/reverse_index.rs:2023-2043 already works around exactly this limitation with a comment about 'misclassifying legitimate historical absence as scalar corruption'. The data layer has no tests for historical-layout rows.

Recommendation

When the slot is historically absent, get_scalar / required_accepted_value_storage_scalar should return the materialized historical value as a scalar view. For example, cache the historical Value in `materialized` and return a borrowed ScalarSlotValueRef from it, or return Ok(None) so callers fall back to required_value_by_contract. Add reader tests with rows stamped at an older layout for Null and SlotPayload fills, covering WHERE, OCTET_LENGTH and direct projection.

A non-null DEFAULT becomes SchemaHistoricalFill::SlotPayload (field_allocation.rs:57-61). Publication is metadata-only: execute_admin_sql_ddl_field_addition (schema/sql_ddl.rs:296-346) rewrites no rows, and history_floor is kept (mutation/field.rs:490-499), so pre-ALTER rows keep a layout where the new slot's span is None (structural_row.rs:407-411). In StructuralSlotReader::get_scalar (structural_slot_reader.rs:581-592) an absent slot calls historical_slot_value. The WHERE fast path hits this for every scalar-leaf compare: eval_compare_with_structural_slots -> scalar_compare_operands_supported_for_fast_path -> required_compare_scalar_slot -> slots.required_scalar (predicate/runtime/mod.rs:643-647, 747-760). Raw-row scans evaluate filters on a StructuralSlotReader (row_runtime.rs:283-284, row_decode/mod.rs:70-75). OCTET_LENGTH also goes through required_scalar (row_decode/mod.rs:295, eval/scalar.rs:358). No test covers WHERE on a DDL-added defaulted column over pre-ALTER rows. reverse_index.rs:2023-2043 already documents and works around this exact misclassification. Null fills are handled correctly; only non-null defaults fail. ADD COLUMN DEFAULT followed by filtering on that column is a standard flow, so high is right.

Value-storage walker misreads canonical enum envelopes (tag 0x84), so nested record-path reads fail for records that contain an enum
crates/icydb-core/src/db/data/structural_field/value_storage/skip.rs:52

Failure scenario

Record Profile { score: Nat64, status: Status(enum) } on entity Player. `SELECT profile.score FROM Player WHERE profile.score >= 10`, or `GROUP BY profile.score`. The walker reaches the status value 0x84 and skips only one byte after it, because type_id's high byte is 0x00 and parses as TAG_NULL. The map walk then ends 12 bytes early, from_raw_validated returns an error, and CanonicalSlotExprReader::read_field_path (eval/scalar.rs:266-279) or the grouped single-path decode (grouped.rs:443-457) fail with a field-path decode error on every row. A path that ends at the enum member itself (`profile.status`, which is a nested leaf per application_lowering.rs:2822-2845) can never decode.

Evidence

skip.rs:52-54: `other if is_nested_value_storage_tag(other) => skip_value_storage_binary_value_at_depth(raw_bytes, offset + 1, depth)`, and tags.rs:42-49 lists VALUE_BINARY_TAG_ENUM (0x84) as a 'nested frame' tag. The canonical encoder writes enums as `0x84 | type_id u32 BE | variant_id u32 BE | body_tag | payload_len u32 | payload` (enum_catalog/value_wire.rs:29-60, canonical.rs:65-71). Record composites are encoded as canonical Maps whose member values include these enums (admission.rs:659-694). resolve_path_segments (executor/projection/path.rs:55) calls ValueStorageView::from_raw_validated(root), which skip-validates the whole root with this walker. decode_value_storage_slice_at_depth (decode/value.rs:247-280) also has no ENUM arm. The canonical fixed_width test (value_storage/canonical/tests/fixed_width.rs:97-102) checks enums only through decode_canonical_value_storage_bytes and never through ValueStorageView.

Recommendation

Have the value-storage skip/view path recognise the current canonical enum envelope: at 0x84, read the 14-byte header, bound payload_len and skip it (reuse canonical::skip_canonical_enum). Alternatively, route nested-path traversal over canonical-wire roots through the canonical skipper. Add a test that runs ValueStorageView::from_raw_validated and map_text_key_bytes on a canonical Map that contains an enum, and an executor test that filters on a record path next to an enum member.

Verifier (confirmed): Composite and enum fields always use the canonical value wire (accepted_field_kind.rs:271-279, runtime.rs:222-225). Records are canonical Maps with Text member keys (enum_catalog/admission.rs:683-686). The canonical encoder writes enums as 0x84 + type_id u32 BE + variant_id u32 BE + body tag + payload_len u32 + payload (value_wire.rs:29-60, canonical.rs:65-71), and only the canonical skipper understands that 14-byte header (canonical.rs:204-233). The value-storage skipper treats 0x84 as a 'nested frame' tag (tags.rs:42-49) and recurses at offset+1 (skip.rs:52-54). For any type_id < 2^24 that byte is 0x00 = TAG_NULL (binary.rs:18), so the walker consumes 2 bytes instead of 14+payload. ValueStorageSlice::from_raw then fails its `skip != raw.len()` check (decode/mod.rs:47-48), or later map entries misparse. resolve_path_segments calls ValueStorageView::from_raw_validated on the whole root (executor/projection/path.rs:55). Both CanonicalSlotExprReader::read_field_path (eval/scalar.rs:266-279) and the grouped single-path decode (grouped.rs:443-457) use it, so a record path fails whenever any member of the record is an enum. In addition, decode_value_storage_slice_at_depth (decode/value.rs:247-280) has no ENUM arm, so a path ending at an enum leaf can never decode. The existing test (canonical/tests/fixed_width.rs:90-95) checks enums only through decode_canonical_value_storage_bytes, never through ValueStorageView.
