Generic hash GROUP BY 'DirectOwned' probe path never looks up existing groups: one group per row for enum/unit/collection/composite keys
crates/icydb-core/src/db/executor/aggregate/runtime/grouped_fold/bundle.rs:596

Failure scenario

Fluent public query on an entity with an enum field `status`: group_by("status").aggregate(count()).aggregate(sum("amount")).grouped_limits(100, 65536) with no index on status, so hash mode is used. Three rows with status=Paid produce three separate `Paid` groups, each with count=1, instead of one group with count=3. This violates GROUP-BY §2.1 canonical identity. With more than 100 rows the query fails with a max_groups limit error even if there are only 3 distinct statuses. Multi-field keys that include any such field are also affected.

Evidence

resolve_owned_group_index materializes the key and calls insert_new_group directly, with no bucket lookup:
  let group_key = materialize_group_key_from_row_view(row_view, group_fields, None)?;
  self.insert_new_group(group_key, execution_context)
insert_new_group (l.530) also does not check for duplicates. The path is selected in runner.rs:57-63 (GroupProbeKind::DirectOwned) whenever group_fields_support_borrowed_group_probe is false (dispatch.rs:84-90). That holds for Enum and Unit (field_kind_semantics.rs:213, test dispatch.rs:115) and for List/Set/Map/Composite. By contrast, the dedicated COUNT(*) owned path does a bucket lookup (count/ingest.rs:198-218). Reachability: direct group fields resolve through FieldSlot::resolve_with_schema with no groupability check (group_field.rs:88; validate/grouped/structure/mod.rs:74-81 only checks slot identity), and dynamic/typed group_by passes straight through (session/query/dynamic.rs:192). Only SQL lowering rejects enum/non-groupable keys (sql/lowering/select/mod.rs:538).

Recommendation

Make resolve_owned_group_index look up the owned key's hash bucket and compare with GroupKey equality before inserting, mirroring GroupedCountState::increment_owned_group_key. Add a generic-fold test with an enum group key. Separately, decide whether the fluent frontend should reject non-groupable direct keys (Enum without catalog proof, Unit, collections) the way SQL lowering does, instead of letting them reach execution.

Verifier (confirmed): bundle.rs:596-606: resolve_owned_group_index calls materialize_group_key_from_row_view and then insert_new_group directly. insert_new_group (bundle.rs:530-566) never checks for an existing equal key; it just pushes the new index into the hash bucket. runner.rs:57-62 selects DirectOwned whenever group_fields_support_borrowed_group_probe is false. That is the case for Enum and Unit (field_kind_semantics.rs:212-214 excludes them from identity form; capability.rs:54-63 only adds Decimal and Relation) and for collections and composites. The dispatch.rs:115 test asserts that enum takes the owned path. The COUNT(*) owned path does do a bucket lookup (count/ingest.rs:198-217). The fluent group_by path, resolve_group_fields_with_schema (validate/symbols.rs:24-47) followed by FieldSlot::resolve_with_schema, does not check groupability, and validate_group_spec_structure (structure/mod.rs:74-97) only checks identity and duplicates. So enum keys reach hash execution. One correction to the scenario: the public lane rejects full scans and requires secondary-index access (admission/policy.rs:230-241). The bug still triggers when hash mode is chosen through an index on a different field (for example WHERE on an indexed created_at), or on the trusted lane. In that case every row opens its own group.

I found no guard in planning, validation, routing or finalization that blocks this for the typed or dynamic APIs. Only SQL lowering rejects these keys. One correction to the claim's scenario: the public lane rejects an unindexed full scan (UnboundedFullScanRejected / PublicQueryRequiresIndex at admission/policy.rs:230-241). So the literal "public query, no index anywhere" case fails at admission. The bug is still reachable in two ways: 1. The public facade `execute_trusted_dynamic_grouped_query`, which allows full scans. 2. The public typed or dynamic lane, when a filter uses a secondary index on some other field, so admission passes and grouping still runs in hash mode. A query with more rows than max_groups fails with a limit error even when there are only a few distinct keys. Resumed secondary-order IN-list pages cap each branch at limit+1 with no resume anchor, silently dropping rows
crates/icydb-core/src/db/executor/pipeline/entrypoints/scalar/hints.rs:163

Failure scenario

Setup: entity with a non-unique index on `a`. Query via execute_public/trusted_live_page: `WHERE a IN (1,2,3) ORDER BY a` (id tie-break appended). a=1 has 50 rows, a=2 has 500, a=3 has 10; public page size is 100. Page 1 (initial route, top-N) correctly returns 50 a=1 rows and the first 50 a=2 rows, boundary (2, 50th id). Page 2: the fetch hint is 101, so branch a=2 emits only its first 101 keys from the start of the branch. The cursor filter keeps a=2 positions 51..101 (51 rows) plus the 10 a=3 rows, giving 61 rows. Since 61 < 100, has_more is false and the continuation is null. The 399 a=2 rows at positions 102..500 are never returned. Any branch larger than limit+1 whose boundary falls inside it is truncated the same way. This breaks QUERY_CONTRACT §3/§5 (no omission).

Evidence

apply_index_set_page_fetch_hint runs for every MaterializedPage terminal. It has no continuation guard and sets `route_plan.scan_hints.physical_fetch_hint = Some(continuation.keep_count_for_limit_window(plan, limit) + 1)` for IndexMultiLookup/IndexBranchSet routes whose order is satisfied (hints.rs:177-205). For a secondary ORDER BY the leaf policy is PreservePrefixBranch, so physical.rs:428-437 calls resolve_branch_ordered_index_prefix_streams with `PrefixMergeResumePolicy::None`. There is no anchor, and each branch is built as `IndexRangeKeyStream::from_prefix(..., resume_anchor=None, limit=request.index_fetch_hint, ...)` (physical.rs:595-611). The branches are then concatenated (577). ScalarContinuationContext::access_scan_input always passes an index anchor of None and supplies no primary-key boundary for non-PK orders (continuation/scalar.rs:114-137). streaming_page_scan_keep_cap returns None on resumed non-PK pages (plan.rs:109), so only the post-access cursor filter trims rows (post_access.rs:75-82).

Recommendation

Do not apply the index-set page fetch hint when `continuation.has_progress()` and the leaf policy preserves prefix-branch order, because those streams cannot resume. Alternatively, derive per-branch resume state from the logical cursor boundary: skip branches before the boundary prefix, anchor the boundary branch at (prefix, boundary suffix, pk), and start later branches from their beginning. Add a multi-page test with an IN list, ORDER BY the indexed field, and a branch larger than the test page size.

For `a IN (...) ORDER BY a`, the secondary contract classifies as Full, so secondary_fast_path_eligible() is true and index_leaf_order_policy() returns PreservePrefixBranch (route plan.rs:225-238). crates/icydb-core/src/db/index/key/ordered/semantics.rs:50

Failure scenario

Timestamp column `born_at` with a secondary index, containing rows at -1000 ms and +500 ms. Query `born_at >= -1000 AND born_at < 1000`: the planner accepts the interval as semantically valid. The raw lower bound starts 0xFF.. and the raw upper bound starts 0x00.., so envelope_is_empty() is true and the query returns zero rows instead of two. `born_at < 0` misses every negative row. `ORDER BY born_at` through the index returns 1970+ rows before pre-1970 rows, which violates the QUERY_CONTRACT canonical-order guarantee and breaks cursor pagination. COUNT answers from first-component cardinality ranges are wrong in the same way.

`impl OrderedEncode for Timestamp { out.extend_from_slice(&self.repr().to_be_bytes()) }` while `Timestamp` is `pub struct Timestamp(i64)` with MIN=i64::MIN (icydb-schema/src/time_atoms.rs:299-307; Repr::Inner = i64 in types/timestamp.rs:25). Value ordering uses Timestamp::cmp on the i64 (value/compare.rs:53,83). The PK encoder biases correctly (key_taxonomy.rs encode_ordered_i64 for Timestamp), and the index encoder for Int64 biases (ordered_i64_bytes), but Timestamp does not. Tests only cover positive timestamps (ordered_semantics.rs:562-563, 622-630).

Recommendation

Encode Timestamp index components with the sign-bias transform (ordered_i64_bytes(self.repr())), matching the PK encoder. Add negative and mixed-sign cases to the pairwise ordering tests and a golden vector. The persisted index format changes, so existing Timestamp indexes must be rebuilt (pre-1.0 policy allows a hard cut).

Timestamp wraps i64, MIN=i64::MIN, and from_millis/parse_flexible accept negatives (icydb-schema/src/time_atoms.rs:299-340). The PK encoder biases Timestamp through encode_ordered_i64 (key_taxonomy.rs:1155-1157, 1366-1368), and Int64 index components use ordered_i64_bytes (ordered/mod.rs:289-291), so Timestamp is the odd one out. The planner validates intervals with Value ordering (planner/range/bounds.rs:107-161, strict_order_cmp using Timestamp::cmp at value/compare.rs:53). envelope_is_empty compares raw bytes (index/envelope/mod.rs:108-125), so a mixed-sign interval collapses to empty, and negative values sort after positive ones. The tests only use positive timestamps (tests/ordered_semantics.rs:562-563, 622-623). Nothing warns: results are silently wrong for a legal, schema-accepted value domain, so I keep high. It could be argued down to medium because pre-1970 Timestamp values are uncommon.

crates/icydb-core/src/db/index/key/codec/bounds.rs:21

Failure scenario

Entity with `pk(fields=["owner","spender"])`, both Principal, plus any secondary index or relation reverse index. The encoded PK for two 29-byte user principals is 2+31+31 = 64 bytes, so every insert fails in commit preparation with an InvariantViolation. Short (canister-id) principals succeed, which makes the failure data-dependent. (Principal, Subaccount), (Subaccount, Subaccount), any Account component, and four Ulid/Nat128 components all exceed the cap too. Adding an index to an existing table of such rows fails the index build.

`MAX_PK_SIZE: usize = 1 + Account::STORED_SIZE` (=63). to_raw_with_primary_key rejects `primary_key.len() > Self::MAX_PK_SIZE` with SegmentTooLarge (codec/mod.rs:91-93), and decode reads the PK segment with max IndexKey::MAX_PK_SIZE (codec/mod.rs:618). key_taxonomy allows COMPOSITE_PRIMARY_KEY_MAX_SIZE = 2 + 4*63 = 254 and uses it as INDEX_PRIMARY_KEY_MAX_SIZE in its own comparator (key_taxonomy.rs:49-51,1463). Composite PKs with indexes are a supported feature (schema/demo/rpg/src/schema/grid.rs), but tests use only small components (codec/tests.rs:1259 uses a 3-byte principal). commit/prepare.rs:868/878 call insert_delta.key.to_raw()? and map the failure to InternalError::index_invariant.

Set IndexKey::MAX_PK_SIZE and the high PK wildcard to the taxonomy's INDEX_PRIMARY_KEY_MAX_SIZE (254), and derive the Storable BOUND from it (single authority). Add tests with maximum-width composite PKs through insert, unique probe and range scan, or reject such schemas at acceptance time.

The suffix is the full EncodedPrimaryKey (codec/mod.rs:463). Composite encoding is tag + count + per-component (tag + payload) (key_taxonomy.rs:1133-1144), and Principal components are len-prefixed (key_taxonomy.rs:1328-1341). So (Principal29, Principal29) = 2+31+31 = 64 bytes, over the cap. Four Ulid or Nat128 components come to 70, and any Account component pushes past it. key_taxonomy itself allows COMPOSITE_PRIMARY_KEY_MAX_SIZE = 254 (key_taxonomy.rs:45-51, 1463). I found no acceptance-time check on PK width. Composite PKs with secondary indexes are accepted (schema/demo/rpg/src/schema/grid.rs). commit/prepare.rs:868/878 propagates the to_raw error, so such writes fail, and whether they fail depends on principal lengths. This is a returned error, not corruption; high is appropriate.

crates/icydb-schema/src/decimal/arithmetic.rs:403

`let t = Decimal::from(1) / Decimal::from(3);` gives 0.333333333333333333 (scale 18). `t * t` has an exact scale of 36; its mantissa ends in 9, so it cannot be reduced, and the result is 17014118346.0469231731687303715884105727 instead of about 0.1111. Likewise `E18s("1.123456789012345678") * E18s("1.123456789012345678")` gives about 1.7e10, and `Decimal::new(5,1).powu(30)` gives about 1.7e10 instead of about 9.3e-10. User code that computes a price×rate or an interest factor and writes the result persists a value off by 10+ orders of magnitude. In SQL, the same checked_mul/checked_powu returns None, so `POWER(1.1, 30)` or a product of two scale-18 columns fails with NumericEvalError::Overflow (core numeric/mod.rs:76, 255) even though the result is small.

checked_mul_impl (l.51-55) adds the operand scales and calls checked_from_mantissa_scale, which returns None when scale > 28 and the mantissa has no trailing zeros to strip. `impl Mul` (l.403-410) then does `.unwrap_or_else(|| self.saturating_mul(rhs))`, and saturating_mul (l.312-323) returns `saturating_extreme(min(scale,28), neg)` = {i128::MAX, 28}. A scale overflow (value too *precise*) is treated as a magnitude overflow. powu (l.260-282) and Product (l.429-433) use the same operator. Every primitive Decimal newtype (built-in Usd/E8s/E18s and user newtypes) derives Mul/Product by default and delegates to this operator (icydb-model-macros newtype.rs PRIMITIVE_NEWTYPE_TRAITS, helper_ops.rs derive_mul). No test covers scale-overflowing products.

When scale > MAX_SUPPORTED_SCALE, round the exact product half-away-from-zero down to scale 28 (using a wider intermediate, or by dividing the mantissa by 10^(scale-28) with rounding, as division already does). Saturate only on real magnitude overflow. Apply the same rule in checked_mul/checked_powu, or add rounding variants for SQL. Add tests for (1/3)*(1/3), E18s×E18s and powu of fractional bases.

The FALSE set of a SQL NOT is compiled as a two-valued predicate NOT, so rows where the inner comparison is UNKNOWN (NULL operand) pass
crates/icydb-core/src/db/query/plan/expr/predicate/compile.rs:238

Failure scenario

Table with nullable `status`. `SELECT id FROM T WHERE NOT (status = 'archived')` returns the NULL-status rows. `WHERE status NOT LIKE 'a%'` (lowered to NOT STARTS_WITH, sql/lowering/expr.rs:211-219) does the same. `DELETE FROM T WHERE NOT (status = 'active')` deletes rows whose status is NULL. Adding a conjunct that cannot compile to a predicate (e.g. `AND id + 0 = id`) sends the query to the expression lane, and the NULL rows disappear. The result set depends on which lane the planner picks, which violates 'Access paths must not change results' (QUERY_PRACTICE.md) and SQL three-valued logic.

Evidence

The compile_bool_truth_predicate doc (lines 251-255) says 'SQL UNKNOWN is represented by neither set ... NOT requests FALSE from its child'. However wrap_truth_predicate (238-248) builds the FALSE set as `Predicate::Not(Box::new(when_true))`. It is used for compare leaves (354-366), STARTS_WITH/ENDS_WITH (587), CONTAINS (617) and others. The predicate runtime evaluates NOT two-valued (predicate/runtime/mod.rs:377 `ExecutablePredicate::Not(inner) => !eval(...)`), and a compare with a NULL operand yields false (compare/value.rs:17-21; semantics.rs compare_eq returns None -> false). So NOT(x = 5) with x NULL evaluates to !false = true. The expression lane (evaluate.rs:493-506, 581-609) returns NULL for the same row, and filter admission rejects it. Coverage is Full whenever the subset compiles (intent/state.rs:87-95), so the predicate program becomes the only runtime filter (semantics/logical.rs:612-619).

Recommendation

For BoolTruth::False, emit null-rejecting forms instead of Not(when_true): invert the compare operator (Eq<->Ne, Lt<->Gte, ...), which already yields false on a NULL/None operand, and for text/contains leaves emit And(IsNotNull(field), Not(leaf)). Otherwise, refuse to derive a predicate subset under NOT so the 3VL expression lane stays authoritative. Add differential tests with NULL rows for NOT(=), NOT LIKE, NOT(a AND b) and DELETE.

Verifier (confirmed): normalize_bool_expr_impl keeps NOT(compare) as-is (canonicalize/normalize.rs:26-43), and RuntimePredicateAdmission admits NOT over a compare (compile.rs:886-903). Asking for BoolTruth::False ends in wrap_truth_predicate, which builds Predicate::Not(when_true) (compile.rs:238-248). Neither predicate normalize (predicate/normalize.rs:560-569) nor schema canonicalization (sql/lowering/select/binding.rs:34) rewrites that Not. Every runtime evaluator computes Not as `!` (predicate/runtime/mod.rs:377, 442, 616). For a NULL field, compare_eq under Strict gives None, and eval_equality_compare_result then gives false (semantics.rs:30-67), so NOT yields true. The expression lane gives NULL for the same row (compiled_expr/evaluate.rs:490-503, 581-587) and the filter rejects it. SQL lowering passes the derived subset (select/mod.rs:171-176), and compile_effective_runtime_filter_program prefers the residual predicate (semantics/logical.rs:606-619). So `WHERE NOT (status='x')`, `NOT LIKE` (lowered to NOT STARTS_WITH, sql/lowering/expr.rs:211-219), and DELETE all admit NULL rows. That contradicts the 3VL intent documented at compile.rs:251-254. The NOT IN membership path is fine (NotIn of NULL gives false). No test establishes the current behavior.

For a single compare leaf and for text or contains leaves, compiling the FALSE set under SQL NOT just wraps the TRUE set in a two-valued Predicate::Not. The runtime predicate engine is two-valued by contract (QUERY_PRACTICE.md: 'Predicates always evaluate to true or false'). A compare against a NULL slot evaluates to false. So NOT(x = 'a') matches rows where x is NULL, which breaks the function's own doc comment ('SQL UNKNOWN is represented by neither set', compile.rs:251-254). The same compiler handles its sibling shapes correctly: NOT over an OR of equalities on one field collapses to NOT IN, which excludes NULL. A bare bool field under NOT compiles to `field = false`, which excludes NULL. NOT over a membership list containing NULL compiles to False. So `NOT (x='a')` and `NOT (x='a' OR x='b')` disagree about NULL rows, and so do `NOT (x='a')` and `x != 'a'`. Nothing upstream blocks this. Normalization does not push NOT into compares, since it only removes double negation and folds literals (canonicalize/normalize.rs:26-43). TruthAdmission accepts NOT (truth_admission.rs:50-53). RuntimePredicateAdmission accepts NOT over a compare (compile.rs:885-895). Nothing checks nullability, and schema canonicalization (binding.rs:34) keeps the Not. Coverage is set to Full, so the predicate program becomes the only runtime filter. The expression lane evaluates the same row to NULL and rejects it, so results depend on which lane the planner picks. Severity is high: this gives wrong read results and wrong DELETE/UPDATE target sets (NULL rows get deleted or updated) with ordinary nullable columns and ordinary SQL. It is not a durable-state inconsistency or a wedge, so it is not critical.

In expression-lane filters, a missing nested path aborts the whole row, so an OR with a true sibling still rejects it
crates/icydb-core/src/db/query/plan/expr/compiled_expr/evaluate.rs:259

Failure scenario

Entity with a nullable composite `profile { rank }`. `SELECT id FROM Player WHERE name = 'bob' OR profile.rank = 5` drops bob whenever profile is NULL or lacks `rank`, even though `name = 'bob'` is TRUE. `WHERE profile IS NULL OR profile.rank > 5` never returns rows where profile is NULL. `WHERE COALESCE(profile.rank, 0) = 0` and `NOT (profile.rank = 5)` also reject those rows outright. The predicate lane scores a missing field as false per leaf (QUERY_PRACTICE.md 'if the field is Missing, return false'), so the two lanes also disagree.

Evidence

evaluate_field_path (252-262) turns a reader `None` into `Err(ProjectionEvalError::missing_field_path_value(..))`, and the `?` in Binary, FunctionCall and CASE evaluation carries it past AND/OR/IS NULL/COALESCE. Filter readers set field_path_missing_is_null=false (executor/projection/eval/scalar.rs:376-386, 399-407), and the filter wrappers map `Err(MissingFieldPathValue)` to `Ok(false)` for the entire row. resolve_value_field_path returns None both for an absent key and for a NULL root (executor/projection/path.rs:25-27, 38-43). The nested-path filters that hit this are always routed to the expression lane (semantics/logical.rs:679-681, 701-711). The reader comment says the intent is only that 'IS NULL cannot admit absent subfields', not that sibling disjuncts get vetoed.

Recommendation

Represent 'missing' as a per-leaf value instead of a whole-row error. For example, materialize a distinct sentinel or NULL inside comparisons, and treat only the specific null tests (IS NULL / IS MISSING) specially, so that TRUE OR <missing> = TRUE. At minimum, catch MissingFieldPathValue at the comparison/function leaf in filter context and turn it into UNKNOWN or false for that leaf only. Add tests covering OR/NOT/COALESCE over absent and NULL-root paths.

Verifier (confirmed): The filter readers use field_path_missing_is_null=false (executor/projection/eval/scalar.rs:381, 402). materialize_missing_field_path returns None for both a missing member and a NULL ancestor (scalar.rs:66-75; executor/projection/path.rs:25-43, 62-68). evaluate_field_path turns that None into Err(MissingFieldPathValue) (compiled_expr/evaluate.rs:252-262). The `?` in Binary, FunctionCall and Unary evaluation carries it past OR, COALESCE and NOT (evaluate.rs:191-205, 427-465), and both filter wrappers map it to Ok(false) for the whole row (scalar.rs:385, 406). Nested-path filters always run in the expression lane when a residual remains (semantics/logical.rs:679-711). NESTED_STORAGE.md:128-136 says only that comparison predicates do not match a missing descendant, which is a per-leaf rule. It does not say a true sibling disjunct gets vetoed. So `name='bob' OR profile.rank=5` and `profile IS NULL OR profile.rank > 5` drop rows that should match. That is a wrong result under realistic use of optional records.

SortRequiresMaterialization can never fire: the admission summary always reports materialized_sort=false, so public reads admit materialized ORDER BY
crates/icydb-core/src/db/query/admission/plan_summary.rs:58

Failure scenario

An entity has a secondary index on `tenant` only. A public endpoint runs `db.query::<E>()?.filter(E::TENANT.eq(t)).order_by(asc("created_at")).execute_live_page(cur)`, where `created_at` is not indexed. The IndexPrefix route passes the index check, the page limit (at most 100) passes the row bound, and the materialization check is skipped, so the query is admitted. Each page runs `scan_materialized_order_direct_data_rows` (executor/terminal/page/scan.rs:666-707), which reads every row for tenant t into a top-K window. Non-primary-key orders also run without the page work envelope (executor/projection/facade.rs:307-318), so one page costs O(rows for tenant), bounded only by the hard budget (250k rows / 4.5B instruction units, executor/budget.rs:35-51). The endpoint works in development and then fails with budget exhaustion once a tenant grows. SQL EXPLAIN's admission block also reports materialized_sort=false.

Evidence

summary_from_plan sets `materialization: QueryMaterializationSummary::none()`. This is the only place the summary is built, and `none()` (admission.rs:325) is its only constructor, so `materialized_sort` is always false. `materialization_rejection` (policy.rs:330-343) rejects only when `summary.materialization().materialized_sort()` is true, so SortRequiresMaterialization is unreachable and `primary_key_materialized_sort_has_exact_candidate_bound` is dead code. PublicRead counts every secondary-index route as bounded, including the planner's unbounded whole-index fallback, so public pages can full-scan the table
crates/icydb-core/src/db/query/admission/plan_summary.rs:63

Failure scenario

The existing test at session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak.rs:950-969 asserts that `DynamicQuery::new("PlannerRow").filter(wide_branch = "y").limit(1)` is rejected with UnboundedFullScanRejected. Adding `.order_by(asc("wide_fixed"))`, the leading field of an accepted index (assuming that field is required), makes the planner choose a whole-index IndexRange instead, and PublicRead admits it. Page 1 walks the whole index, reading rows until one matches `wide_branch = "y"`. Every later page restarts at the first index entry and scans to the end. A public endpoint therefore does per-call full-table scans limited only by the hard execution budget. CURSOR.md:74 claims envelope exhaustion yields resumable empty pages; here it does not, and once the index passes about 250k entries every page fails with a budget error.

Evidence

`access_satisfies_index_requirement` returns true for any `kind.is_secondary_index()`, ignoring prefix length and bounds. `is_full_scan()` matches only FullScan. When predicate planning ends in a full scan, the planner swaps in `index_range_from_order_with_semantic_indexes` (query/plan/planner/mod.rs:180-201), which builds `whole_index_ordered_range_scan_from_contract` with an empty prefix and `Bound::Unbounded, Bound::Unbounded` (order_select.rs:56-69), and records no non-index reason. In the executor, non-primary-key orders get no page envelope (`page_entry_limit` is Some only when `scalar_page_physical_progress_eligible`, facade.rs:307-318). Resumed pages do not reposition the secondary stream: `access_scan_input` passes anchor None and uses the boundary only for primary-key orders (executor/planning/continuation/scalar.rs:114-135). They also have no keep cap (`continuation.has_progress() && !scalar_order_is_primary_key_only`, executor/terminal/page/plan.rs:109), so `scan_rows_with` reads to the end of the stream (scan.rs:483-506). Primary-key KeyRange routes, which do get the envelope and repositioning, are rejected with PublicQueryRequiresIndex.

Recommendation

Record the prefix length and bound shape (and whether the route came from the order-only fallback) in AdmissionAccessSummary. Under PublicRead, reject index ranges with an empty prefix and both bounds open, at least whenever a residual filter or resumption is involved. Alternatively, give secondary-index-ordered pages the page envelope and physical repositioning before admitting them. Add public-lane tests for order-only index routes with a non-indexed filter.

Verifier (confirmed): `access_satisfies_index_requirement` (plan_summary.rs:63-75) accepts any secondary-index kind, and `index_range` (plan_summary.rs:173-183) discards the prefix and bounds. When predicate planning yields a single full scan, planner/mod.rs:180-201 falls back to `index_range_from_order_with_semantic_indexes`. That fallback emits `whole_index_ordered_range_scan_from_contract` with an empty prefix and Unbounded/Unbounded bounds (order_select.rs:39-70), and records no non-index reason. The only gates are that every index key field is non-omittable or implied non-null (index_select.rs:54-79) and that the order contract is satisfied. With a LIMIT or page limit, the admission row bound passes. Executor side: the page envelope applies only to PK-only orders (facade.rs:307-317, 556-566). `access_scan_input` passes anchor None and supplies the boundary only for PK orders (continuation/scalar.rs:114-135). Resumed non-PK pages get no keep cap (terminal/page/plan.rs:109), and the comment at plan.rs:90-94 says outright that the cursor 'does not reposition its physical secondary-index stream'. `scan_rows_with` without a cap loops to the end of the stream (scan.rs:483-506). That index is (wide_fixed, wide_branch), and classify_index_match_by (order_contract.rs:259-287) requires the non-PK order terms to match all index key items. Also, no filter is needed at all: with no predicate, the planner goes straight to the order-only fallback (planner/mod.rs:139-150). Public admission (dynamic.rs:546-554) therefore admits it. Execution: - `page_entry_limit` is Some only for primary-key-only orders (facade.rs:307-318, 556-566). Secondary-ordered pages never enter `with_production_scalar_page_work` (facade.rs:444). - On resume, `access_scan_input` passes anchor None and drops the boundary for non-PK orders (continuation/scalar.rs:114-135). - The keep cap is None when the continuation has progress and the order is not PK-only (terminal/page/plan.rs:92-110). Still, the documented bounded-list pattern stops working at realistic table sizes (every resumed page fails past about 250k rows, or 128 MiB of stored bytes). highreproducedr2-covering-projection-1 · correctness · high confidence
Hybrid covering fails valid SELECTs with an invariant error whenever a projected index component is anything other than Bool/Int/Nat(<=64)/Text/Ulid/Unit
crates/icydb-core/src/db/executor/projection/covering/shared.rs:655

Failure scenario

Entity Item { id: Ulid (pk), category: Nat64, price: Decimal(scale 2), name: Text } with index(fields = ["category", "price"]). SQL `SELECT price, name FROM Item WHERE category = 3` (or the same with `ORDER BY price`) plans IndexPrefix(category=3). The pure plan is None because name is not covered, and the hybrid plan is fields [IndexComponent{1} (price), RowField(name)] with PrimaryKeyOrder(Asc), or IndexOrder when ORDER BY price is present. At execution the hybrid lane scans the prefix, reads the first row, calls decode_hybrid_covering_components on the Decimal-tagged component, gets Ok(None), and returns query_executor_invariant. The whole SELECT fails although the scalar path would have answered it. The same happens for any composite index with a Timestamp, Date, Principal, U256, Float or unit-Enum trailing component, e.g. `SELECT created_at, note FROM Order WHERE tenant_id = 7` with index (tenant_id, created_at), or `SELECT amount, label FROM U256AuditEntity WHERE bucket = 1` against the repo's own fixture (schema/audit/one_simple/src/one_simple.rs:55). It also happens for an IN list on a single-field Enum/Decimal index plus an extra column (multi-lookup has no prefix constants). EXPLAIN meanwhile reports the query as hybrid_covering.

Evidence

decode_covering_projection_component decodes only the Bool, Int64, Nat64, Text, Ulid and Unit tags and returns Ok(None) for every other tag (covering.rs:1036-1065). The index encoder writes distinct tags for Decimal, Timestamp, Date, Duration, Float32/64, Int128, Nat128, IntBig, NatBig, U256, Principal, Subaccount and Account (index/key/ordered/mod.rs:217-266 via value.canonical_tag()), and a catalog Enum key for unit enums (index/key/build.rs:205-212, enum_catalog/equality_key.rs:68-72). The hybrid decoder maps Ok(None) to Err(InternalError::query_executor_invariant()) (shared.rs:655-659). It is called on the first projected row in both the proven and the checked hybrid lanes (hybrid.rs:148, 198). The planner admits a field as IndexComponent purely by name match, with no kind check (query/plan/covering/mod.rs:965-976). The hybrid plan is built whenever at least one projected column is not in the index (covering/mod.rs:769-775, 314-337). The only exclusion is a finite IndexRange window in IndexOrder (covering/mod.rs:341-358); IndexPrefix, multi-lookup, branch-set and PK-order shapes are never excluded. The facade propagates the error with `?` and never falls back (facade.rs:269-280; projection/covering/mod.rs:97-100). Tests do not cover this: the generated reference schemas behind the hybrid coverage axis use only Blob/Bool/Int64/Text/Ulid kinds (session/tests/tier_c_reference.rs:979-987), so no hybrid test exercises an unsupported component kind.

Recommendation

Make hybrid fail closed the way pure covering does: have decode_hybrid_covering_components return Ok(None), and have try_execute_hybrid_covering_projection_rows_with_plan_for_canister decline (Ok(None)) on an unsupported tag. Better still, gate IndexComponent/IndexExpressionComponent admission in covering_projection_field_source on the accepted component kind being decodable (Bool, Int8-64, Nat8-64, Text, Ulid, Unit, Relation over those), or extend decode_covering_projection_component to every canonical encoding (Enum needs the accepted catalog). Add hybrid tests for Decimal, Timestamp and Enum trailing components.

highreproducedr2-identity-allocation-1 · correctness · high confidence
Dense field-ID renumbering orphans the Identity allocator: removing a field that sorts before the PK restarts Identity::next at 1 (reuse on empty entities; permanent insert failure and integrity corruption after a physical migration)
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/identity_state.rs:620

Failure scenario

Physical migration (populated entity). Entity Order v1 has fields id: Nat64 with generated(insert="Identity::next") as the PK, plus amount: Int64. Sorted by name, amount gets FieldId 1 and id gets FieldId 2, so the Identity owner is (tag, 2). Inserting 1,000 orders gives ids 1..1000 and high-water 1000. v2 uses a migration with CheckedCast{from: amount, to: amount_cents: Nat64} and SchemaRemoval::Field{amount}. rebuild_fields adds amount_cents as FieldId 3. The dense removal of FieldId 1 then maps id 2->1 and amount_cents 3->2. At publication, (tag, 2) is retired with high-water 1000, and a fresh Active (tag, 1) is created at high-water 0. From then on, every INSERT INTO Order allocates id 1, finds the existing row 1, and fails with an Identity Corruption error, forever, because no value is consumed. CHECK INTEGRITY DEEP reports all 1,000 rows as above high-water, and schema description shows the full lifetime capacity again. SQL cannot reseed Identity, and the FieldId cannot be restored, so the only ways out are deleting rows or recreating the database. Online path. An operator deletes every row of a log entity (ids 1..H), then calls apply_schema with SchemaRemoval::Field for an obsolete field named e.g. "archived", which sorts before "id". The next insert returns id 1. Committed values are reissued, which contradicts docs/contracts/IDENTITY_CONTRACT.md:180-183 ("A committed value is never reused after deletion"; capacity is lifetime) and silently aliases any numeric or external references to the old IDs. Each such removal also leaves an extra retired record counting against the 65,536 cap.

Evidence

1. Identity owners are keyed only by (entity_tag, field_id). identity_declarations collects (entity_tag, field.id()) from each bundle (identity_state.rs:671-690). prepare_identity_state_transition retires any current key that is missing from the candidate (identity_state.rs:609-616). It creates a brand-new Active owner at high-water 0 via IdentityState::new_active for any candidate key that is missing from current (identity_state.rs:620-633). It never consults field lineage. Every publication path uses this key-only transition (crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/store.rs:1426-1447, 2795-2799, 3034-3038, 3052-3056; crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/live_schema_checkpoint.rs:235).

2. The Identity PK's FieldId is not stable. EntityFragment::try_new sorts fields by source key, which is the field name (crates/icydb-schema/src/fragment.rs:799). lower_initial_entity_fields assigns FieldId = position + 1 in that order (application_lowering.rs:2721-2728). So a PK named "id" gets a FieldId above 1 whenever any field name sorts before it ("amount", "created_at", "email", ...). derive_dense_field_removal_candidate renumbers every retained field to 1..N and explicitly remaps primary_key_field_ids (crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/mutation/field_removal.rs:76-99, 116-122). apply_existing_field_removals remaps only snapshots and source bindings (application_lowering.rs:1322-1356; source_binding.rs:382-399). Nothing remaps the identity-state record. The planner test itself notes that dense removal reuses ordinals across revisions (crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/migration_planner.rs:3204-3207).

3. Reachability. Online explicit generated-field removal requires an exactly empty entity (crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application.rs:2588-2618). Physical migrations skip that proof on purpose, so they can remove a field from a populated entity (application.rs:1062-1072). The documented pattern is a CheckedCast/Copy into a new field plus SchemaRemoval::Field of the old one (migration_planner.rs:1847-1908, 3127-3219).

4. After publication the cursor opens on (entity_tag, new field_id) (crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/write.rs:1360-1368) at high-water 0. A generated key that hits an existing row returns insert_key_exists_after_generation(true), which is identity_state_corruption (write.rs:328-331, 1461-1466). Rejection consumes no value, so every retry generates the same key again. Deep integrity classifies rows above the committed high-water as HighWaterExceeded (crates/icydb-core/src/db/integrity/row.rs:856-860).

Recommendation

Make the Identity owner survive dense renumbering. Options: (1) In prepare_identity_state_transition, when an entity's sole Identity declaration keeps its tag and kind but its FieldId changes, move the record: write the same materialized_high_water and last_applied_advance under the new key, and delete or retire the old key only as an implementation detail, never resetting to 0. The removal candidate already has the exact old-to-new lineage (DenseFieldRemovalCandidate::retained_field_id), so it can be carried to the transition. (2) Alternatively, key identity state by an immutable owner that does not depend on dense ordinals, such as entity_tag alone, since integrity already guarantees at most one Identity field per entity. (3) At minimum, reject any field removal whose lineage changes an Identity PK's FieldId, in both lower_existing_schema_proposal and the migration planner. Add tests covering online removal and physical-migration removal of a field that sorts before an Identity PK, asserting the high-water is preserved and the next insert succeeds.

ILIKE/LOWER text predicates mean different things in the expression and predicate lanes; resumable UPDATE uses the expression lane and silently updates the wrong set
crates/icydb-core/src/db/sql/lowering/expr.rs:204

Failure scenario

Rows with name in {'alice', 'Alan', 'bob'}. `execute_trusted_sql_exact_update("UPDATE users SET flagged = true WHERE name ILIKE 'Al%'", 10)` flags alice and Alan through the casefold predicate. `start_trusted_sql_mutation_job` with the same SQL, then repeated advances: the Forward scan finds no candidate, because a LOWER()'d string never starts with 'A'. Verify finds no residual row, and the job reports `Completed` with rows_updated = 0. The same split happens for `LOWER(email) = 'Admin@x'` and `STARTS_WITH(LOWER(name), 'Al')`. A plain SELECT is also inconsistent: `WHERE name ILIKE 'Al%'` returns alice, but adding an OR branch that falls outside the runtime predicate subset forces the expression lane, and alice disappears from the results.

Evidence

Lowering `name ILIKE 'Al%'` produces `STARTS_WITH(LOWER(name), 'Al')` and leaves the prefix literal unfolded (expr.rs:196-209). The same `LOWER(field)` shape compiles to a predicate with `CoercionId::TextCasefold` (query/plan/expr/predicate/compile.rs:414-428, 848-856). At runtime that predicate casefolds both sides (`TextMode::Ci => casefold_text(actual).starts_with(&casefold_text(prefix))`, predicate/runtime/compare/scalar/text.rs:106; `compare_casefold` folds both operands, predicate/semantics.rs:174-178). The compiled expression evaluator has no casefold rewrite: `LOWER` is plain `lower_text`. The planner runs the predicate program whenever a residual predicate exists (compile_effective_runtime_filter_program, semantics/logical.rs). The UPDATE selector attaches an independently lowered predicate and claims Full coverage (`from_update_where_expr`, select/mod.rs:129-139). Resumable UPDATE compiles the persisted scope expression (`compile_scalar_projection_expr_with_schema(scope)`, resumable_update.rs:1482) and uses only that for Forward and Verify (`eval_compiled_filter_expr_with_required_slot_reader(compiled_scope, row)`, resumable_update.rs:1327).

Recommendation

Give ILIKE and LOWER-casefold comparisons one meaning in both lanes. For ILIKE (and the documented `LOWER(field) LIKE` / `STARTS_WITH(LOWER(field), ...)` casefold forms), fold the literal with `casefold_text` at lowering time. Alternatively, stop compiling mixed-case literals into TextCasefold predicates. Add differential tests (expression lane vs predicate lane, and resumable vs exact UPDATE) with mixed-case patterns.

Verifier (confirmed): I traced this end to end. The parser keeps the ILIKE pattern as written (parser/projection/postfix.rs:119-141). lower_sql_like_expr then builds STARTS_WITH(LOWER(expr), '<prefix as written>') without folding the literal (sql/lowering/expr.rs:196-209, 222-236), and no later normalization or canonicalization pass folds it either (lowering/predicate/normalize.rs only folds literal-only subtrees; canonicalize/mod.rs:91-119 has no text rewrites). The predicate lane maps LOWER(field) to CoercionId::TextCasefold with the raw literal (predicate/compile.rs:414-428, 845-856), and at runtime it casefolds both sides (predicate/runtime/compare/scalar/text.rs:103-107). The expression lane evaluates LOWER as plain lower_text (function_semantics/evaluation.rs:30) and STARTS_WITH as a plain text.starts_with(needle) (function_semantics/types.rs:168-173, projection_eval.rs:314-330). So lower('alice').starts_with('Al') is false in the expression lane and true in the predicate lane. compile_effective_runtime_filter_program picks the predicate whenever a residual predicate exists and falls back to the expression otherwise (semantics/logical.rs:606-630). from_update_where_expr attaches a strict predicate subset (sql/lowering/select/mod.rs:129-139), so exact UPDATE runs in the casefold lane. Resumable UPDATE stores selector.scalar_filter_expr() as its scope (resumable_update.rs:892) and compiles it with compile_scalar_projection_expr_with_schema (1482). Forward and Verify both call resumable_row_needs_patch, which uses only the compiled expression (1318-1329). A mixed-case ILIKE prefix therefore matches no rows in the resumable job, which completes having updated nothing, while exact UPDATE updates the matching rows. The contract (SQL_SUBSET.md:873-883) presents these forms as casefolded. Existing tests and docs only use lowercase prefixes such as 'al%', so nothing catches this. High is fair: silent wrong write results under realistic use.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could not refute the claim. Every step from the public facade to the wrong result checks out, and I found no guard that normalizes or rejects a mixed-case literal under LOWER/ILIKE. 1. Lowering. `name ILIKE 'Al%'` parses to SqlExpr::Like{casefold:true}. The parser keeps the pattern as written (sql/parser/projection/postfix.rs:119-141), and supported_like_prefix only strips the trailing '%' (predicate/mod.rs:80-91). lower_sql_like_expr then builds STARTS_WITH(LOWER(name), Text("Al")) and leaves the literal as written (sql/lowering/expr.rs:196-209, 229-235). Nothing later touches the case of that literal: - SQL WHERE normalization (sql/lowering/predicate/mod.rs:74-95) does not. - SQL schema canonicalization (select/binding.rs:62-77, 124-139, 160-190) does not: it only rewrites Field/Literal compares and IN lists. - Planner canonicalize/rewrite modules have no Lower handling at all. 2. The two lanes disagree. - Predicate lane: compile_bool_text_target maps LOWER(field) to CoercionId::TextCasefold (query/plan/expr/predicate/compile.rs:847-859, used at 568-586). compile_bool_compare_leaf does the same for `LOWER(f) = lit` (compile.rs:414-428). At runtime TextCasefold becomes TextMode::Ci (predicate/runtime/compare/scalar/text.rs:19), which casefolds both sides (text.rs:88, 106). So 'alice' starts with 'Al' and matches. - Expression lane: LOWER is plain lower_text (function_semantics/evaluation.rs:30), and STARTS_WITH is a raw str::starts_with (function_semantics/types.rs:172, called from projection_eval.rs:328). So 'alice' does not start with 'Al' and does not match. - I found no validation that rejects a non-lowercase casefold literal (query/predicate/validate.rs:290, 431 only enforce text-only). 3. Exact UPDATE uses the predicate lane. The path is `icydb::db::session::sql::execute_trusted_sql_exact_update` (crates/icydb/src/db/session/sql.rs:87) → update.rs:454 → execute_sql_update_statement_with_contract (update.rs:248-263) → sql_update_selector_query (update.rs:204). from_update_where_expr attaches both the visible expr and an independently lowered predicate subset (select/mod.rs:129-139). The planner's compile_effective_runtime_filter_program prefers any residual predicate (semantics/logical.rs:616-620). planner_predicate_requires_expression_runtime only forces the expression lane for FieldPath filters (logical.rs:705-711). So on a full scan, alice and Alan are flagged. A repo test confirms that casefold semantics are what SELECT is meant to give: `LOWER(common) = 'EVERYONE'` must return the rows of `common = 'everyone'` (session/tests/cardinality_tiebreak.rs:1005-1030). 4. Resumable UPDATE uses the expression lane only. The path is `start_trusted_sql_mutation_job` (crates/icydb/src/db/session/mod.rs:181 → session/mutation_job.rs:46) → prepare_resumable_update_start. The policy classifier does not reject ILIKE (update_policy/planning.rs:92-118). The persisted scope is selector.scalar_filter_expr(), the visible expression (resumable_update.rs:892). The intent codec supports Lower and StartsWith (mutation_job/intent.rs:695, 708). On advance, the scope is decoded (resumable_update.rs:575) and compiled only as a CompiledExpr (1482-1489). The Forward scanner (1036) and the Verify scan (1299) both call resumable_row_needs_patch → eval_compiled_filter_expr_with_required_slot_reader (1327). No predicate program is consulted anywhere on this path. Forward yields no candidates, Verify finds no residual row, and the job finishes having updated none of the rows the exact path updates. 5. SELECT side-claim. derive_normalized_bool_expr_predicate_subset returns None unless the whole expression compiles (compile.rs:76-84). So `WHERE name ILIKE 'Al%' OR TRIM(name) = 'x'` gets no predicate, apply_to_query falls back to filter_expr (select/mod.rs:175-182), and the expression lane drops 'alice'. Results therefore depend on unrelated OR branches. Contract: SQL_SUBSET.md:873-882 lists ILIKE and `STARTS_WITH(LOWER(field), 'prefix')` as supported "casefolded predicate forms", and QUERY_PRACTICE.md:175 says TextCasefold casefolds both operands. The expression lane is the side that violates this. Severity: high. A trusted, realistic API silently updates the wrong row set, and the lane mismatch also makes query results inconsistent. It does not corrupt durable state, so it is not critical. Confidence: high, traced end to end statically. Not executed, per the ground rules.
Reproduction (reproduced): Journaled store with a custom schema: id, name Text, flagged Bool. Rows: alice, Alan, bob. `name ILIKE 'Al%'` returns [1,2] through the casefold predicate lane. Adding an OR branch that forces the expression lane returns []. Exact UPDATE flags rows [1,2]. After resetting, start_trusted_sql_mutation_job with the same UPDATE reaches Completed after a Forward and a Verify pass that each scanned 3 keys, with rows_updated_total=0 and no rows flagged. The job reports success after updating none of the rows the exact UPDATE matched.

Decimal::checked_div panics on i128::MIN / -1 (integer division overflow), which callers can trigger through SQL arithmetic
crates/icydb-schema/src/decimal/arithmetic.rs:355

Failure scenario

A caller runs SQL such as `SELECT amount / -1 FROM T` over a row whose Decimal amount has mantissa i128::MIN at scale 18. That row can be inserted by the same caller, since Candid Decimal text parses to that value. A literal expression like `-170141183460469231731.687303715884105728 / -1` does the same. Expression evaluation reaches Decimal::checked_div → `i128::MIN / -1` → panic → canister trap. Every repetition is a caller-triggerable trap, against the rule that production code must not panic. If the same evaluation runs in a timer-driven or background job (e.g. mutation-job SET expressions), it could fail on every advance. A lhs of scale 28 with rhs mantissa -1 at scale 10 hits the same path.

Evidence

checked_div_impl normalizes both operands, then division_operands at target_scale 18 yields factor 10^0 when lhs.scale == 18 + rhs.scale, so numerator = lhs.mantissa unchanged. div_round_half_away_from_zero then runs `let quotient = numerator / denominator; let remainder = numerator % denominator;`. For i128 these panic on overflow in release builds too. Core calls it from db/numeric/mod.rs:82 (`left.checked_div(right)`) for SQL Div. SQL literal parsing turns `-170141183460469231731.687303715884105728` into Decimal{mantissa: i128::MIN, scale: 18} (sql_shared/cursor.rs:27-38, types.rs:504-509; Decimal::from_str deliberately admits i128::MIN), and `-1` becomes Int64(-1) → Decimal(-1, 0).

Recommendation

Use checked_div/checked_rem in div_round_half_away_from_zero and treat None as 'retry at lower scale' or Overflow. Do not propagate it straight out of the loop with `?`: the retry-at-lower-precision loop is currently skipped whenever the rounding step fails. Add a regression test for (i128::MIN @ s, -1 @ s-18) and for the scale-28 variant.

Verifier (confirmed): div_round_half_away_from_zero (decimal/arithmetic.rs:350-356) uses plain `/` and `%`. For i128::MIN / -1 these panic in every build profile, because Rust always checks signed division overflow. checked_div_impl (arithmetic.rs:57-82) normalizes, then tries target scales 18 down to 0. division_operands (335-347) returns (lhs.mantissa, rhs.mantissa) unchanged when exponent == 0. Any target scale that overflowed earlier just retries lower, so it always reaches exponent 0 when 0 <= lhs.scale - rhs.scale <= 18. The mantissa i128::MIN has no trailing zero, so normalize leaves it alone. There is an even simpler trigger than the one reported: an Int128 field holding i128::MIN. Value::Int128 goes through Decimal::from_i128 (numeric_value.rs:20-27, decimal/mod.rs:203) to Decimal(i128::MIN, 0). `SELECT x / -1` reaches evaluate_numeric_binary_expr, then apply_value_arithmetic_checked (db/numeric/mod.rs:295-307), apply_numeric_arithmetic_checked, and finally checked_div (mod.rs:77-82). Nothing on that path special-cases -1. At target scale 0 this panics, which is a canister trap. The trap is reachable from caller-controlled data and query text, and it violates the no-panic rule. checked_rem uses checked_rem and is safe.
Skeptic · reachability (upheld, high): I could not refute the claim. I traced it end to end and found no guard. `Decimal::checked_div_impl` (crates/icydb-schema/src/decimal/arithmetic.rs:57-82) retries at lower target scales until `division_operands` succeeds. For a mantissa of i128::MIN at any scale s, with a divisor of -1 at scale r where 0 <= s-r <= 18, it eventually reaches exponent 0. There it returns `(i128::MIN, -1)` unchanged, because `checked_pow10(0)` is 1 and `checked_mul(1)` succeeds. `div_round_half_away_from_zero` then runs `numerator / denominator` at line 355 with no MIN/-1 check. Rust always emits the signed-division overflow check, even in release builds, so this panics and the canister traps. Nothing in the chain filters these operands out: - `normalize()` has no effect, since i128::MIN ends in 8 and has no trailing zeros. - `apply_decimal_arithmetic_checked` (crates/icydb-core/src/db/numeric/mod.rs:77-82) only rejects a zero divisor. - `Decimal::from_str` (text.rs:106-121) deliberately accepts i128::MIN. - `Decimal::from_i128` (mod.rs:203) maps Int128(i128::MIN) to mantissa MIN, so an Int128 column holding i128::MIN hits the same path. The simplest trigger needs no stored data at all: a literal-only constant fold in WHERE, which panics during planning. The saturating `impl Div for Decimal` (arithmetic.rs:434-446) calls the same checked_div_impl, so it panics too. That impl also saturates to mantissa i128::MIN at scale 18, which is exactly the value that then panics when divided by -1. Why high rather than critical: - The trap only affects the message that caused it. Query and update messages roll back. - I found no timer, startup or recovery path that evaluates SQL arithmetic. Mutation-job advances are called by the application, not by a timer. So there is no permanent wedge and no state corruption. - The generated `icydb_query` endpoint is controller-only by default. The guard variant, or an app exposing the facade SQL API, opens it to other callers. The cross-user case is narrower. Another user's `col / other_col` query traps only if a stored Int128 or Decimal row holds a mantissa of i128::MIN and the divisor is -1. It still breaks the project rule against panics in production executor code, and it is a trap reachable from caller-controlled SQL with a single literal, which the rubric grades high. If the reviewer weighs it by practical impact (the trap stays within the message, and the default endpoint is controller-only), medium is also defensible. Confidence is high. Fix: in `div_round_half_away_from_zero`, use `numerator.checked_div(denominator)?` and `checked_rem`, or explicitly return None for (i128::MIN, -1). The test profile is [optimized], and i128 division overflow panics regardless of overflow-checks. The bug is wider than the finding says. The retry loop lowers target_scale from 18 toward 0; when lhs.scale - rhs.scale is between 0 and 18 it reaches exponent 0, where numerator=i128::MIN and denominator=-1. So plain Decimal::from(i128::MIN) / Decimal::from(-1), both at scale 0, also traps. That value is the text "-170141183460469231731687303715884105728". Failure scenario

Two fields price and qty are declared Decimal(scale = 18), a very common token-amount shape ('e18 compatibility' is called out in decimal/mod.rs). With price = 20 and qty = 20, each mantissa is 2e19; the product 4e38 exceeds i128::MAX (≈1.7e38), so `SELECT price * qty` fails with 'numeric overflow' even though the result is 400. Any two scale-18 values above about 13.04 fail. A scale-18 value of 1e20 times a literal like 1.5 fails the same way.

checked_mul_impl does `let scale = self.scale.checked_add(rhs.scale)?; let mantissa = self.mantissa.checked_mul(rhs.mantissa)?;` and strips trailing zeros only afterwards (checked_from_mantissa_scale). Accepted admission pads every Decimal{scale} field value up to the declared scale (db/schema/enum_catalog/admission.rs:1014-1025, `scale_to_integer(scale)`), and the persisted decode keeps that mantissa/scale (data/structural_field/typed.rs:215). SQL Mul calls left.checked_mul(right) and maps None to NumericEvalError::Overflow (db/numeric/mod.rs:76). checked_div normalizes first; checked_mul does not.

Normalize both operands (strip trailing zeros) before the mantissa multiply. When the product still overflows, compute in 256-bit and reduce or round to scale ≤ 28 rather than failing. Consider normalizing before alignment in checked_add too. Add tests multiplying padded fixed-scale values.

So for two scale-18 fields, `price * qty` with 20 and 20 computes 2e19 * 2e19 = 4e38. That exceeds i128::MAX (about 1.7e38), so the multiply returns None, which is mapped to NumericEvalError::Overflow (mod.rs:76). Every product of two scale-18 field values whose true result is at least about 170 fails. The mathematical results fit easily, and SQL_SUBSET.md:731-735 frames errors as out-of-domain inputs or running-sum overflow, not spurious intermediate overflow. decimal/mod.rs:17 explicitly advertises e18 workloads. The query fails closed rather than returning silent wrong data, but multiplication on e18 fields is effectively broken in realistic use.

AcceptedFixedUpdatePatch::is_satisfied_by: `if row.required_bytes(field.slot.index())? != field.payload.as_slice()`. required_bytes returns persisted_row_declared_field_missing, which is Corruption class (error/mod.rs:1522-1524), whenever get_bytes(slot) is None. That is the normal state for fields introduced after the row's layout stamp. The resumable forward scan calls it on raw stored rows: resumable_update.rs:1031-1036 -> resumable_row_needs_patch (1317-1330). The same pattern is in CanonicalSlotExprReader::read_field_path (executor/projection/eval/scalar.rs:266-269) and the grouped single-path decode (grouped.rs:443). Eligibility (update_policy/planning.rs:92-118) has no layout restriction. The same absent-bytes-as-corruption pattern appears in CanonicalSlotExprReader::read_field_path (eval/scalar.rs:266-269) and the grouped single-path decode (grouped.rs:443) for later-added record fields. A public live page with `ORDER BY created_at` over an indexed range of 300k rows and page size 100. Page k reads about 100k rows before its boundary, so total work grows quadratically. Its comment admits: 'the current scalar cursor does not reposition its physical secondary-index stream'. The page-work envelope and scan probe are attached only for PK-only orders (facade.rs page_entry_limit), and index-range limit pushdown is disabled on resume. Rows before the boundary are read, decoded and filtered, then dropped by the post-access cursor filter (post_access.rs:171-177). CURSOR.md says the token binds 'consumed physical progress', but for these orders the physical progress is never used.

Thread an index resume anchor derived from the validated boundary into IndexRange and IndexPrefix streams for secondary orders; the cursor anchor machinery and resume_bounds_for_continuation already exist. Page work and the envelope apply only to PK-only orders (facade.rs:305-316, 556). For IndexRange and IndexPrefix routes, apply_index_set_page_fetch_hint does not apply either. So scan_rows_with runs with row_keep_cap None (scan.rs:482-505) and reads until the stream is exhausted. Every resumed secondary-ordered page therefore scans the entire range, before and after the boundary, and materializes it before the cursor filter trims it (post_access.rs:75-82). That is O(N) per page, not just O(k·page). With the 250k RowsVisited/KeyIndexEntries hard budget (session/request.rs:24-25), any secondary-ordered range above about 250k rows fails at page 2. It keeps every matching row and only then applies the cursor filter and the page window. From page 2 on, every page costs O(range size). No guard blocks this path: - Public admission allows IndexRange/IndexPrefix access. - The cursor contract binds order terms but has no physical progress for secondary orders. - The PK-suffix anchor applies only when the order is PK-only. - Index-range LIMIT pushdown is turned off on resume by `requires_anchor`. - The load scan-budget hint is rejected when a continuation has progress. Why it stays high: live pages are the main UI browsing API ("keyset traversal for ordinary UI browsing"). ORDER BY on an indexed field over a large range can't be paged past page 1. Any caller can replay page-2 tokens to force near-maximum read budget per call, which is work amplification that the public admission "no full scan" policy is meant to prevent.
highverifiedquery-intent-3 · security · low confidence
The shared plan-cache key identifies literals only by an XXH3-128 digest with a public seed when a filter has no parameter template, so a forged collision would serve one caller another caller's plan
crates/icydb-core/src/db/query/intent/cache_key.rs:238

Failure scenario

A multi-tenant app exposes `filter(tenant.eq(my_tenant) AND deleted_at.is_null())` and lets users choose their own tenant slug, a Text value. An attacker who can find a slug x whose `hash_value(Text(x))` equals `hash_value(Text(victim_slug))` registers x. After a victim request has cached the plan (through an update call), the attacker's authorized query for `tenant = x` produces an equal cache key, the cached plan with `tenant = victim_slug` is executed, and the attacker receives the victim's rows. Conversely, the attacker can poison the cache so the victim sees the attacker's rows. Accidental collisions are negligible; the risk depends entirely on how feasible an adversarial XXH3-128 second preimage is, which this review did not demonstrate.

Evidence

When `parameter_contract` is None, the key's `filter_expr` is built with `ProjectionExprCacheKey::from_expr`, and literals become `Literal(ValueCacheKey::Canonical([u8;16]))` via `hash_value` (cache_key.rs:67, 363). `hash_value` is XXH3-128 with `VALUE_HASH_SEED: u64 = 0` (value/hash.rs:14-20, 115-121). Line 253 then drops the SHA-256 predicate fingerprint whenever `filter_expr` is Some. The parameter contract is None whenever the predicate contains IsNull, IsNotNull, Not, CompareFields, text-contains, or exceeds the slot/list/byte caps (query/plan/parameters.rs:91-93, 117-135, 154-160), which covers common filters such as `deleted_at IS NULL`. The cache is a canister-wide thread_local shared by all callers (session/query/cache.rs:114-121). A hit returns the stored SharedPreparedExecutionPlan with its own literals and does not compare them to the current query (cache.rs:596-609). XXH3 is not designed to resist collisions or second preimages, and its seed here is public. Continuation signatures likewise hash literals through the same digest (hash_sections/mod.rs:190-197, access.rs).

Recommendation

Key cached plans on the full canonical literal bytes, or on a SHA-256 digest of them. The SHA-256 predicate fingerprint is already computed, so keep it in the key even when filter_expr is present. Do the same for access-plan and filter literals in the continuation signature. Keep XXH3 only for internal bucketing.

Verifier (confirmed): When `parameter_contract` is None, cache_key.rs:238-247 puts literals into the key only as `ValueCacheKey::Canonical([u8;16])` via `hash_value` (cache_key.rs:297-302, 363). That is XXH3-128 with seed 0, i.e. the public default secret (value/hash.rs:14-20, 81-86, 383-393). Line 253 drops the SHA-256 predicate fingerprint whenever `filter_expr` is Some, and ExpressionBacked filters are the common case (intent/state.rs:92,112,133-137). The parameter contract is None for IsNull, IsNotNull, Not, CompareFields, TextContains and similar predicates, or when slot/byte caps are exceeded (plan/parameters.rs:91-93, 117-135, 159-169). On that path, cache.rs:597-610 returns the cached plan on key equality with no literal comparison. The cache is canister-wide and thread_local (cache.rs:114-121). On feasibility: xxhash-rust 0.8.18 `mix16_b`/`mix32_b` (xxh3.rs:164-183) confirm the structure is nearly linear. For a hashed length of 33-64 bytes, an attacker who controls the bytes can set chunk c1_lo equal to the secret word, which forces mix16B(c1)=0. The two remaining 64-bit targets can then be met by choosing c2's lane sum and solving for c1_hi, after inverting the bijective avalanche (solvable for about 1/4 of lengths). That gives an O(1) second preimage for Blob-typed literals. Text needs valid UTF-8 at the chosen positions (the default-secret words at offsets 32-48 are not valid UTF-8), so the Text case needs longer inputs or more search. It is plausible but I did not demonstrate it. Impact is a cross-caller plan and row disclosure under specific app shapes, so high is appropriate.

Every code step holds, and the one step the original reviewer left open, forging an XXH3-128 match for a literal, turns out to be practical. I built a standalone program in the scratchpad (rustc linked with rust-lld; no repo build). For the victim value Text("acmecorp"), it produced a 58-byte printable-ASCII string whose icydb hash_value is identical: 72a97b819cbeab800ba41f194660f8af. The run took about 10 minutes on 8 laptop cores with about 3 GB of RAM. **Code path (all confirmed):** - The typed facade, DynamicQuery and SQL filters all store an expression-backed filter: - crates/icydb/src/db/query/typed.rs:141,152 build a DynamicQuery. - session/query/dynamic.rs:155 calls filter_for_schema, then filter_expr, which produces ExpressionBacked. - SQL goes through sql/lowering/select/mod.rs:173-181. - A filter like `tenant = X AND deleted_at IS NULL` gets no parameter contract, because IsNull returns None at query/plan/parameters.rs:158. That sends the query down the literal-specific path at session/query/cache.rs:586-602. - On that path the cache key's filter_expr contains Literal(ValueCacheKey::Canonical(hash_value(v))) (intent/cache_key.rs:238-246, 297-302, 363). The SHA-256 predicate fingerprint is dropped whenever filter_expr is present (cache_key.rs:253-257). - hash_value is XXH3-128 with seed 0, so it uses the public default secret. Text is framed as [1, 18, len_be_u32, bytes] (value/hash.rs:14-20, 358-361, 413-423). - The cache is a canister-wide thread_local keyed by store registry (cache.rs:119). - On a hit, cache.rs:278-293 returns the stored SharedPreparedExecutionPlan and checks only the cardinality lifecycle stamp, never the literals. - Execution then runs that plan, including its access path and residual filter carrying the victim's literal (session/query/dynamic.rs:255, 272-318). - Canonical AND-child ordering sorts by rendered label, and the field name leads that label (canonicalize/ordering.rs:26-75). All constants are public. - Fixing the chunk sums (sigma = 0x9f repeated, which keeps printable ASCII closed under 0x9f - c) splits the problem into two independent 64-bit meet-in-the-middle problems. The low half pairs chunk C0 against A1; the high half pairs D0 against B0. - Each half costs about 2^37-2^38 evaluations with a memory-filtered birthday search. - About 25% of victim values can be reached at length 64; the other 75% fail a mod-4 condition. I checked 975 of 4000 sample names. The other 75% would need a length that is not a multiple of 4, where chunks overlap; I did not demonstrate that case. **Why high rather than critical:** exploitation depends on how the application is built. - The authorization-scoping literal must be a Text (or Blob) value the attacker can choose, at least about 58 bytes long. - The filter must fall off the parameter template, for example by using IS NULL, Ne, NotIn, StartsWith, text-contains, or more than 64 slots. - The victim's plan must have been cached by an update call and still be within the 1024-entry FIFO. - The attacker must know the victim's value. - Principal- or ULID-keyed tenancy is not practically forgeable, because the attacker cannot choose those bytes. SQL DELETE/UPDATE candidate selection goes through the same shared cache (write/delete.rs:62-73, then write/mod.rs:174, then select_plan.rs:150). Either reject non-uniform directions in the canonical grouped lane with a typed GroupPlanError, or route mixed-direction group-key ordering to the per-term ranking lane (the Top-K comparator) and bind per-term directions into the grouped cursor. Finalization then sorts groups by the canonical group key only (bundle.rs:768-780) and ranks candidates with Canonical{direction: route.direction()} (page_finalize.rs:363-367, 536-543, 717-727). highverifiedr2-cross-message-concurrency-2 · robustness · medium confidence
Each migration Validating or abort page rewrites and heap-snapshots the whole index store, so large stores make both Advance and Abort trap while the database is gated
crates/icydb-core/src/db/index/store.rs:831

Failure scenario

Take a production store with about 1M index entries (schema-migration-9 used 10M) and a physical migration that adds or rebuilds one index generation. The first Validating page stages up to 256 keys and then reinserts all N entries into stable memory and clones them into heap. With 133 KiB B-tree nodes (index-access-6), each insert costs tens of thousands of instructions, so the call exceeds the per-message instruction limit and traps. Every retry traps the same way. Abort calls the same materialization on its first page and also traps. The migration stays in Validating with the gate BLOCKED, so all ordinary reads and writes fail. Redeploying the same successor changes nothing, and only a code change can recover the canister. Smaller stores succeed but pay O(N) stable writes for every 256-row or 512-entry page.

Evidence

fold_journaled_materialized_view copies every canonical entry of the store's shared index store (all entities, all indexes) into a HeapBTreeMap (index/store.rs:946-958). It then calls canonical.clear_new(), reinserts every entry into the stable BTreeMap, and runs rebuild_prefix_cardinality_from_entries over all entries (831-843). The per-page limits bound only the rows scanned and the bytes staged. The rewrite runs once per store per Validating page with staged entries (migration_validation.rs:575-582, MAX_MIGRATION_VALIDATION_ROWS_PER_PAGE = 256 at :38). It also runs per store on every abort page, even when that page removes nothing (migration_execution.rs:1073-1078, MAX_MIGRATION_ABORT_INDEX_ENTRIES_PER_PAGE = 512 at :101). Total cost is O(N) per call and O(N^2/512) for a full abort. Validating, ReadyToRewrite and Rejected block ordinary operations (migration_record.rs:55-66), and the only exit from them is the same cleanup path (abortable() at migration_record.rs:74-80). Round 1's schema-migration-9 counted the number of abort calls but assumed each call succeeds.

Recommendation

Apply staged entries and cleanup removals incrementally, as ordinary positioned or journaled index puts and deletes such as SchemaMigrationIndexPut, instead of rewriting the whole canonical tree. If direct canonical writes are kept, insert or remove only the staged keys in canonical, maintain prefix cardinality incrementally, and prove the overlay is empty first. Add an instruction-budget test that runs Validating and Abort on a store with more than 100k index entries.

Verifier (confirmed): The cost claim holds. fold_journaled_materialized_view copies every canonical entry of the whole shared index store into a HeapBTreeMap (index/store.rs:946-958). It then clear_new()s the stable BTreeMap and reinserts all N entries (index/store.rs:831-834). rebuild_prefix_cardinality_from_entries then takes a second full snapshot through entries_snapshot_for_cardinality and applies apply_insert for each entry (index/store.rs:886-908). The only bounds are per page: rows scanned and bytes staged (migration_validation.rs:38-40) and abort entries/bytes (migration_execution.rs:101-102). No bound exists on store size; I checked every MAX_ constant in the migration modules. staging runs this per store on every page that has staged entries (migration_validation.rs:575-582). cleanup runs it on every abort page even with zero removals (migration_execution.rs:1073-1078). Validating, ReadyToRewrite and Rejected block ordinary operations (migration_record.rs:55-66), and Abort is their only exit (migration_record.rs:74-80), so if one call exceeds the per-message instruction limit, Advance and Abort both trap on every retry. Deploying code without the migration feature does not clear the gate either: schema_migration_record_blocks_ordinary_operations blocks any nonterminal record when the capability is not compiled (live_schema_checkpoint.rs:672-678). Reinserting about 1M entries into a stable BTreeMap, plus two heap snapshots and the cardinality rebuild, plausibly costs well over 40B instructions. Smaller stores succeed but pay O(N) stable writes on every page. The design docs do not describe this as intended; an archived audit (docs/design/archive/0.189-mega-audit-2/audit-results.md:750-758) flagged the same O(index size) materialization in an older recovery path. Severity stays high: a controller-reachable trap that leaves the database gated, dependent on store size.

It then calls `canonical.clear_new()` (store.rs:831), which resets root, length and allocator (ic-stable-structures 0.7.2 btreemap.rs:712-716). It reinserts every entry into the stable BTreeMap (store.rs:832-834). Finally `rebuild_prefix_cardinality_from_entries` (store.rs:886-896) takes a second full snapshot through `entries_snapshot_for_cardinality` (store.rs:899-907). - The cost is O(N), where N is every index entry in the store: all entities and all indexes that share the store path. None of it goes through `MaintenanceConstructionBudget` (only the scan/validation closures do) or any instruction check. That covers any migration that adds or rebuilds a unique index generation or a relation. - The page limit of 256 rows (migration_validation.rs:38) bounds only the scan, not the fold. Abort: - `cleanup_migration_staging_page` (migration_execution.rs:994-1086) runs `store.with_index_mut(|index| { remove...; index.fold_journaled_materialized_view() })` unconditionally for each store it visits (migration_execution.rs:1073-1078), even when `removals` is empty. - `by_store` is non-empty whenever the migration has any new or rebuilt index or relation generation (migration_execution.rs:879-905). - The abort cursor walks every raw entry in the store, 512 per page (migration_execution.rs:101), so a full abort costs about N/512 × O(N). A store of around 1M entries, and plausibly a few hundred thousand, then exceeds the 40B-instruction update limit. - A trap rolls the message back, so the cursor and record stay unchanged. The handoff finds Order assigned to S', which has no accepted bundle, so store_unsupported writes a terminal SchemaReconciliation receipt, and v2 is StartupFailure. The operator redeploys v1. Registry state is S Retired with a v1 proposal, which is rejected on every tick, so the canister stays Recovering forever. The only fix-forward is a v3 that drops Order, plus every entity whose relation targets it, from the model entirely, which orphans those rows. Otherwise the operator must reinstall. Other triggers: moving Order into A and deleting S (Order is unbound in A); switching S from journaled to heap; removing S in the same release as any other change that generated reconciliation rejects. A failed release that adds a store likewise retires the new quartet on revert. ensure_database_format_admitted runs first in every timer-driven recovery page (commit/recovery.rs:218). reconcile_current_registry retires an omitted Active quartet after checking only its journal tail (convergence.rs:152-155, 331-341), adds new quartets (164-177) and persists the change immediately (196-206). Generated schema reconciliation runs only after recovery completes (startup/driver.rs:56-67,107-116). For an existing database, generated lowering only considers stores that already have an accepted bundle (schema/application.rs:2191-2207). Every proposal entity must already be bound in exactly that store: existing_proposal_entities_by_store does `store_by_identity.get(..).ok_or_else(store_unsupported)` (schema/application_lowering.rs:641-644), and verify_unique_entity_binding follows (1387-1400). Relation counts must match exactly (2094-2096). The resulting RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED is terminal for SchemaReconciliation (startup/mod.rs:131). Do not mutate the registry until the release's generated schema has reconciled. Options: record retire/add intent and apply it after Ready; or preflight generated lowering against the post-change topology before persisting the registry. Allow un-retiring a quartet whose four memories are untouched since retirement. Refuse to retire a store whose schema memory holds an accepted root with entities unless the release explicitly acknowledges data abandonment. Document that store-key changes cannot succeed on multi-store databases.

The retired S is no longer a registered store, so it takes no part in reconciliation (application.rs:2191-2207, application_lowering.rs:636-653). v3 gets a NoOp or Applied receipt and the canister becomes Ready. The old v2 receipt does not match v3's submission key (startup/observe.rs:218-235), so it does not block. The existing omitted-store test shows the same removal path reaching Ready. (3) The other triggers are weaker. If a release removes S and also makes some other rejected change, fixing forward means v2 minus the bad change, which loses nothing beyond the intended removal. Switching journaled to heap already gives up durability by contract (DURABILITY.md:62-68). Reverting a failed store-add burns one key and one of the 16 registry slots, and the operator can pick a new key. None of this is a permanent wedge. The upgrade itself still succeeds and the canister stays upgradable. What remains is a genuine gap at an edge condition. The design's rule for rejected registry changes is "no database retirement/publication", and the original actor recovers (0.258-design.md:208; logical_memory.rs:112-124). That rule is enforced only for journal debt and pending markers, not for rejections at the reconciliation stage. So a failed release that includes a store removal or addition can only be fixed forward, never rolled back. That is medium, not high.

crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/application.rs:2902

Migration-enabled canister has migrated User 1 to 2. Later a release removes an unused heap cache store (or retires a journaled store). Removal succeeds and the database is Ready, but every lineage entry is now keyed under the old store identities. The next release carries `entity_migration(entity="Order", from=1)`. The startup preflight returns SCHEMA_MIGRATION_UNADOPTED, which is non-terminal, so the handoff loops as described in xc-security-2, and `icydb schema migration advance` fails the same way. Adoption is rejected with VersionGap because User is at version 2. The canister can never run another migration. If all entities happened to be at version 1, adoption succeeds but leaves the stale entries. current_proposal_lineage_is_applied then stays false (application.rs:2054, see schema-migration-4), and the successor never reaches Ready after Applied. This is distinct from schema-migration-2: restamping heads would not fix the key change.

Lineage entries are keyed by (TargetStoreIdentity, EntityTag) (schema/migration_lineage.rs:108-110). Removing, adding or re-pathing any store changes every store identity and the accepted head. A no-change application after the topology change is NoOp with prior_head == accepted_head, so attach_ordinary_lineage_publication returns without a lineage op (application.rs:1539-1541). Old keys and old heads stay. Later planning looks up lineage by the new identity: resolve_transitions and validate_unchanged_lineage return `.ok_or(Unadopted)` (migration_planner.rs:428-430, 492-494). Adoption requires every entity at version 1 (migration_planner.rs:215-218).

Key lineage (and schema-application records) by a topology-independent store identity, such as the durable store key or quartet. Alternatively, re-key lineage atomically inside the publication that first observes a new topology. Add a test: migrate, remove a store, then migrate again.

Lineage entries are keyed by (TargetStoreIdentity, EntityTag) (migration_lineage.rs:108-110). After a topology change, a NoOp generated application has prior_head == accepted_head, and attach_ordinary_lineage_publication returns without a lineage op (application.rs:1539-1541). Later planning looks lineage up under the new identity and returns Unadopted (migration_planner.rs:428-430, 492-494). Adoption rejects any entity past version 1 with VersionGap (215-218). SCHEMA_MIGRATION_UNADOPTED is code 229, not RUNTIME_UNSUPPORTED (icydb-diagnostic-code/src/registry.rs:602), so it is non-terminal and the handoff keeps retrying.
