validate_delete_relations_structural loops over each relation and each deleted target key (validate.rs:136-215). For every reverse entry it reads the source from the final overlay and calls source_row_references_relation_target_primary_key_value (validate.rs:198-205). That call re-decodes the whole source relation value and charges the shared batch RelationCommitBudget: relation_target_keys_for_source_slots -> charge_nested_references / charge_raw_references (reverse_index.rs:1561-1581, 1775, 1878). Nothing is memoized across deleted targets. The batch raw-reference limit is 5,460 (reverse_index.rs:62). Sources deleted in the same batch are exempt (override -> Ok(false)), but sources that are updated away are not.

Recommendation

Memoize, per batch, each surviving source row's projected target-key set (keyed by source raw key and relation id) and charge it once. Alternatively, invert the check: collect surviving sources from the reverse ranges, project each once, and intersect with the deleted-target set.

That call re-projects the whole relation field and charges commit_budget.charge_raw_references(keys.len()) (reverse_index.rs:1775) against MAX_RELATION_BATCH_RAW_REFERENCES = 5,460 (:62). That is well inside MAX_STRUCTURAL_MUTATION_BATCH_OPERATIONS = 4,096 (session/write.rs:173). REF_INTEGRITY.md:141-146 explicitly allows pairing a target delete with an update-away in one batch. The write fails closed, and splitting it into two messages works, so there is no corruption. Medium is appropriate.

Charge the before image against a separate allowance, or skip re-projection when the old and new relation field bytes are identical (no delta is possible). crates/icydb-core/src/db/integrity/derived.rs:135

Failure scenario

Stable-memory corruption enlarges an indexed row to over about 4.06 MiB (RawRow's Storable is Unbounded). The row phase records OversizedRow. When the job reaches that row's index entry, every DeepContinue returns an InProgress page with zero findings and the same checkpoint. The job never terminates or reaches FinalProof, and it holds its progress slot until the client gives up, after which it lingers as TerminalPending.

can_start_entry reserves MAX_ROW_BYTES of headroom (derived.rs:116-129), but consume_source_row (:135-149) stops the page with no progress when the source row is larger than the remaining budget. That happens even for the first entry of a page, because the limit is MAX_ROW_BYTES + 64 KiB. inspect_index_witness and inspect_reverse_witness return Ok(None) when it fails (:453-455, :644-646), leaving the checkpoint unchanged, and exhausted = !stopped = false. deep.rs:522-529 and :548-556 persist the same checkpoint as a new InProgress page. MAX_INTEGRITY_IN_PROGRESS_PAGES is u64::MAX - 1 (job.rs:25), and persist_candidate refreshes the lease on every page (deep.rs:813). The row phase avoids this with a first-row exemption (row.rs:209-216), and it already reports such rows as OversizedRow, so they are known to exist.

Recommendation

Exempt the first entry of a page from the decoded-byte budget, as the row phase does. Or, when a source row exceeds MAX_ROW_BYTES, record a DivergentIndexEntry or DivergentReverseRelationEntry finding ('oversized_source_row') and advance the checkpoint.

Verifier (confirmed): I traced this myself. MAX_DERIVED_DECODED_BYTES_PER_PAGE = MAX_ROW_BYTES + 64 KiB (derived.rs:28-29). can_start_entry reserves MAX_ROW_BYTES (:116-129) but has no first-entry exemption. consume_source_row (:135-149) sets stopped and returns false when key + value + row_len exceeds the limit, which for the first entry means a row over about 4.06 MiB. inspect_index_witness (:453-455) and inspect_reverse_witness (~:644-646) then return Ok(None). inspect_index_entry returns early on page.stopped without advancing page.checkpoint, and exhausted = !stopped = false. execute_index_candidate and execute_reverse_candidate (deep.rs:504-557) then persist the same checkpoint as a new InProgress page. checkpoint_after_rows (:697-705) does not skip index or reverse phases after an OversizedRow row finding. RawRow is Storable Unbounded with an unchecked from_bytes (data/row.rs:107-122), so an oversized persisted row is returned by get. The row phase has the first-row exemption (row.rs:209-216) and classifies OversizedRow (row.rs:481-489). 0.212-design.md's 'Risk: A Malformed Or Oversized Unit Wedges Its Phase' promises this cannot happen, so the derived phases break that design commitment. The trigger needs physical corruption, since writes enforce RawRow::try_new. There is no durable harm, and the owner can still abort. But the job never reaches later index, reverse or journal phases, so it hides further findings in exactly the corrupted scenario it exists for. Medium stands.

crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/sql/resumable_update.rs:497

Failure scenario

An application timer calls advance_trusted_mutation_job for an Active job while an operator's offline schema migration has the database gated (MIGRATION_GATE_BLOCKED). The session is created normally, because db() only checks startup Ready. The catalog lookup returns MigrationInProgress, which is recorded as a terminal RestartRequired(AcceptedSchemaChanged). If the migration is later aborted, the schema never changed, but the job is dead, its progress is lost, and the reported reason is wrong. Any transient or internal error from root compilation has the same effect. See the next finding for how this becomes a stuck recovery.

Evidence

prepare_mutation_job_authority:
  let catalog = self.accepted_schema_catalog_context_for_entity_source_key(intent.target_entity_path())
      .map_err(|error| mutation_job_execution_budget_restart_reason(&error).map_or(
          MutationJobExecutionPreparationError::Restart(MutationJobRestartReason::AcceptedSchemaChanged),
          MutationJobExecutionPreparationError::Restart))?;
The lookup runs accepted_schema_runtime_root(), which first calls self.db.ensure_recovered_state() (session/accepted_schema.rs:429-431). That call includes ensure_schema_migration_ready_for_ordinary_operations() (MigrationInProgress) and ensure_recovery_admitted() (recovery_pending). advance_mutation_job_forward/verify (resumable_update.rs:636-641, 718-726) then call persist_terminal_mutation_job_restart, which writes RestartRequired(AcceptedSchemaChanged) straight into the progress store. By contrast, a recovered_store() failure a few lines later (515-520) is mapped to the non-terminal Failure(TargetQueryFailed).

Recommendation

Only persist AcceptedSchemaChanged when the lookup succeeds and proves the entity is missing or its fingerprint or revision differs (for example, handle Ok(None) or a mismatch explicitly). Map admission, migration-gate and internal errors to a non-terminal MutationJobExecutionPreparationError::Failure, as the recovered_store() branch already does. Better still, run ensure_recovered_state() before loading or transitioning the record at all.

Verifier (confirmed): I traced this end to end. resumable_update.rs:496-506 maps every Err from accepted_schema_catalog_context_for_entity_source_key to Restart(AcceptedSchemaChanged), except ExecutionBudgetExceeded (1433-1443). That lookup goes find_...(518-529) -> accepted_schema_runtime_root(), which first calls db.ensure_recovered_state() (accepted_schema.rs:429-431). ensure_recovered_state runs ensure_recovery_admitted, which returns recovery_pending when a marker is present, and ensure_schema_migration_ready_for_ordinary_operations, which returns MigrationInProgress while the gate is BLOCKED (db/mod.rs:264-267, live_schema_checkpoint.rs:626-650). advance_mutation_job_forward/verify (resumable_update.rs:633-640, 717-725) then call persist_terminal_mutation_job_restart (1566-1584), which writes RestartRequired straight to the progress store. Nothing earlier rejects the gated state. advance_trusted_mutation_job (session/mutation_job.rs:87-117) only loads the record and charges budget. The generated db() only checks startup Ready (icydb-model build/actor/db/store.rs:121-130), and observe() (startup/observe.rs) never looks at the migration gate. So an advance during a blocking migration phase, or after an in-message retained-marker error, or after any internal root-compile error, ends the job for good with a false reason. SQL_SUBSET.md:605-608 says a terminal RestartRequired is only for actual authority/policy drift, so the code contradicts the contract. In contrast, the recovered_store() failure at 515-520 maps to a non-terminal Failure. No test covers the gate case. The consequence is lost progress and a misleading reason, not corruption: committed fixed-patch pages stay committed, and a fresh job can redo the work idempotently. Medium stands.
mediumconfirmedjournal-jobs-2 · durability · medium confidence
Direct progress-store writes skip recovery admission and can invalidate a pending marker's MutationProgress `before`, making recovery fail permanently
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/mutation_job.rs:142

Failure scenario

In one message: the first Forward page of job J (sequence 0) builds a marker carrying rows plus MutationProgress(before=seq0 bytes, after=seq1). append_marker_encoded_batch returns an unexpected Err, so the marker is kept and the record is still seq0. The application, reusing the same DbSession, either (a) calls cancel_unadvanced_mutation_job(J, 0), which deletes the record, or (b) retries advance_trusted_mutation_job, whose catalog lookup now returns recovery_pending, which the previous finding persists as RestartRequired. The message returns without trapping, so the state is committed. The startup driver's replay then finds the record missing or different from both before and after, fails deterministically with commit_corruption on every attempt, and guarded reads and writes stay blocked for good.

Evidence

cancel_unadvanced_mutation_job (and acknowledge/state/inventory) call with_mutation_progress_store directly with no ensure_recovered_state(). persist_terminal_mutation_job_restart -> replace_mutation_progress_record_op (integrity/progress_store.rs:1074-1078) also writes without admission. The commit window can return an error normally after the marker is persisted: index_store_guard.verify()? and append_prepared_journal_batches(guard, &effects)? (executor/mutation/commit_window.rs:624-632) are not wrapped in enforce_preflighted_apply, and finish_commit keeps the marker on Err (commit/guard.rs:313-324). Recovery then requires an exact match: apply_mutation_progress returns CorruptProgressStore unless current == after or current == before (progress_store.rs:516-530), and recovery.rs:392-398 turns that into a StartupRecoveryFailure.

Recommendation

Call self.db.ensure_recovered_state() (or at least ensure_recovery_admitted) at the start of every progress-store mutation (cancel, acknowledge, the terminal/verify restart persistence paths, resumable start/advance/acknowledge). Alternatively, reject direct progress replacement for a job whose record is named by a live marker's MutationProgress op. Consider trap-guarding the post-marker append/verify errors in commit_window, as the rest of the apply phase already is.

Verifier (confirmed): The code does what the finding says. After begin_commit publishes the marker, apply_prepared_row_ops (commit_window.rs:614-630) calls index_store_guard.verify()? and append_prepared_journal_batches(guard,&effects)? outside enforce_preflighted_apply. append_batch_bytes (journal/store.rs:743-795) has several fallible corruption returns. finish_commit (commit/guard.rs:313-327) deliberately keeps the marker and returns Err normally, arming only a wake-up timer. The same message can then write the progress store with no admission check: cancel_unadvanced_mutation_job, acknowledge and state go through with_mutation_progress_store (session/mutation_job.rs:127-156; progress_store.rs:1041-1047), and replace_mutation_progress_record_op (1074-1078) does the same. Nothing blocks this within the message; admit_ordinary_database_work only runs when a new db() session is created. Case (a): cancel at sequence 0 passes ensure_cancelable_at_sequence and deletes the record (progress_store.rs:573-587). Case (b): a retry hits ensure_recovery_admitted -> recovery_pending (recovery.rs:144-148, with the hint set in store/mod.rs:365). Finding 1 maps that to a terminal replace, and apply_mutation_progress accepts it because current == before. On replay, apply_mutation_progress (progress_store.rs:512-530) needs current == after or current == before. Otherwise it returns CorruptProgressStore, which recovery.rs:391-397 turns into StartupRecoveryFailure::database_control. That failure repeats on every attempt, so the canister stays wedged. The trigger is narrow: an internal error after preflight but after the marker (normally only a bug or corruption), followed by the application touching the same job in the same message. The outcome, though, is permanent. Medium is fair, and I confirmed the reasoning, but likelihood is low.

Durable access-state revision rises by 2 on every startup, so no resumable job or exhaustive cursor over journaled stores survives an upgrade
crates/icydb-core/src/db/commit/recovery.rs:686

Failure scenario

An application starts a long export/validation job with start_resumable_job over journaled stores, as DURABILITY.md:346 advises ('Journaled source stores are required for cross-upgrade jobs'). A routine code upgrade with no schema change runs empty-tail recovery, and access_state_revision goes N -> N+2. The next compare_proof_and_advance returns receipt Invalidated and the job must restart from scratch. The same happens to every exhaustive page cursor across any upgrade. The recovered index is logically identical, so the change is spurious and cross-upgrade jobs can never complete across an upgrade.

Evidence

IndexStore::init_journaled starts in IndexState::Ready (index/store.rs:186). Every startup path runs reset_journaled_live_projections, which calls handle.mark_index_building() (recovery.rs:686): Ready->Building. It then runs db.mark_all_registered_index_stores_ready() (recovery.rs:285 / 431): Building->Ready. StoreHandle::set_index_state (registry/handle.rs:1092-1106) calls JournalTailStore::advance_access_state_revision (journal/store.rs:878-888) on each real change, and that value is persisted. verify_read_set_revision_proof compares it (session/read_set.rs:99-104) and reports StoreAccessChanged, which is_source_change() treats as grounds to invalidate the job.

Recommendation

Do not advance the durable access-state revision for startup projection resets, which leave identical post-recovery traversal. For example, bump it only for genuine readiness or generation changes (schema publication, candidate-generation promotion), or compare the persisted logical index state rather than counting volatile transitions. If the conservative behavior is intended, narrow DURABILITY.md:345-347 and CURSOR.md to say that upgrades invalidate proofs.

Verifier (confirmed): IndexStore::init_journaled always starts at state Ready with a heap revision of 1 (index/store.rs:170-191). RECOVERED_KEYS is heap state (recovery.rs:2370-2377), so recovery runs on every init or upgrade. Both the empty-tail path (recovery.rs:277-285) and the full path (404 then finish_recovery 431) call reset_journaled_live_projections, whose mark_index_building (686) takes Ready to Building. mark_all_registered_index_stores_ready (db/mod.rs:312-322) then takes Building back to Ready. set_index_state (registry/handle.rs:1092-1106) advances the durable JournalTailStore access_state_revision on each change (journal/store.rs:878-888), so the revision rises by 2 durably on each startup. The accepted runtime root identity hashes only schema-root revision and fingerprint (schema/runtime_root.rs:77-105), so a same-schema upgrade leaves it unchanged. The access-revision mismatch alone therefore trips StoreAccessChanged (session/read_set.rs:99-104). compare_proof_and_advance (session/resumable_job.rs:126-135, 164) treats that as is_source_change (read_set.rs:284-293) and persists Invalidated. This contradicts DURABILITY.md:345-347 ('Journaled source stores are required for cross-upgrade jobs') and 0.221-design.md:624-626, which say journaled stores can back cross-upgrade jobs. The only upgrade test (durable_mutation_job_scale.rs) covers mutation jobs, which use entity journal revisions rather than access_state_revision, so it misses this. Invalidation fails closed, so medium, not high.
mediumconfirmedjournal-jobs-4 · correctness · high confidence
Heap-store read-set revisions reset on upgrade (ABA), so a pre-upgrade exhaustive proof and cursor can be accepted against different data
crates/icydb-core/src/db/session/read_set.rs:143

Failure scenario

A heap cache store is refilled with N rows in post_upgrade, so its generation is N after every upgrade. A client paging with execute_public_exhaustive_page holds proof (data_revision=N+1, access=1) and a continuation cursor across an upgrade. After the upgrade the cache holds different rows, but its revision is again (N+1, 1), the root is unchanged and the cursor still authenticates. The page resumes into the new dataset and finally reports a null continuation, i.e. a revision-strict 'complete' traversal made of two unrelated snapshots. This contradicts the design's 'incarnation-bound' heap revision (0.221-design.md) and DURABILITY's rule that heap sources support only one-call exhaustive traversal.

Evidence

capture_store_revision for a store with no journal uses DataStore::generation + 1. The generation is initialized to 0 on every init (data/store.rs:127,153) and only goes up with saturating_add (841). The heap access revision starts at 1 (index/store.rs:158-160) and is not bumped by recovery, because reset_journaled_live_projections only visits journaled stores. The proof's database_incarnation and the cursor HMAC key (commit/store/mod.rs:253-257) live in stable memory and persist. execute_public_exhaustive_page / execute_trusted_exhaustive_page accept a caller-supplied proof and check it with the non-durable verify_read_set_revision_proof (session/query/dynamic.rs:431-441), and heap stores are allowed.

Recommendation

Tie heap revisions to a per-process nonce (for example, mix a random boot identifier into ReadSetStoreIdentity or the heap revision), or reject resume proofs and continuations that include a non-journaled store. compare_proof_and_advance should also re-check with verify_durable_read_set_revision_proof, so a store whose storage mode changed after an upgrade cannot pass by coincidence.

Verifier (confirmed): For a heap store, capture_store_revision (session/read_set.rs:137-156) uses DataStore::generation+1. The generation is const-initialized to 0 (data/store.rs:123-129) and rises by one per write (bump_generation, called at 187/217/...). The heap access revision starts at 1 (index/store.rs:155-162). Recovery never bumps it: reset_journaled_live_projections covers journaled stores only, and mark_index_ready does nothing when the store is already Ready (handle.rs:1093-1095). The proof's incarnation and the cursor MAC key are durable (commit/store/mod.rs:246-257). The token authority binds only incarnation, root and entity (cursor/token/scalar.rs:58-65), with no per-process nonce. Exhaustive pages accept caller-supplied proofs and check them only with the non-durable verify (session/query/dynamic.rs:429-441, 686-688). Heap stores are never rejected there (DurableStoreRequired appears only in verify_durable). If a heap store takes the same number of writes after an upgrade, the whole proof matches again and the cursor authenticates. The traversal then resumes over different rows and can report a null continuation as 'complete', which breaks CURSOR.md:89-94 ('Completion is only a null continuation under one unchanged proof'). Allowing multi-call heap traversal at all already conflicts with DURABILITY.md:346-347 ('heap sources may only support one-call exhaustive traversal'). I did not fully trace whether the heap store's re-reconciled schema root always gets the same revision after restart. Deterministic startup makes that likely. The trigger needs an exact revision coincidence, so medium (edge condition) is right.
Also reported as: xc-contracts-1

crates/icydb-model-macros/src/imp/normalize.rs:83

Case 1: `#[list(item(prim = "Text", unbounded, normalizer(path = "base::normalizer::text::Trim")))] pub struct Tags {}`. The app calls `icydb_model::normalize(&mut tags)` on caller input before insert. Nothing is trimmed and whitespace-padded tags are persisted. Case 2: `#[record(ty(validator(path = "crate::StartBeforeEnd")), fields(...))]`. `icydb_model::validate(&rec)` reports no issues for start > end. Case 3: `#[tuple(value(item(prim = "Nat32", validator(path = "base::validator::num::Gt", args(10)))), ...)]` accepts 0. In each case caller-controlled data skips checks the schema author declared, with no warning.

`Item` and `Type` accept `normalizer(...)` and `validator(...)` everywhere (node/item.rs:38-42, node/type.rs:17-21), but generation reads them only in a few places. rg over `.normalizers|.validators` shows: List/Set/Map normalize use only `container_self_tokens(&node.ty.normalizers)` (normalize.rs:83-99), so `node.item.normalizers` and `node.value.item.normalizers` are never emitted. `impl NormalizeAutoFn for Enum {}` (normalize.rs:63) and `impl ValidateAutoFn for Enum {}` (validate.rs:61) are empty, so enum `ty` rules and variant-payload item rules are dropped. Tuple::map_trait (tuple.rs:77-84) sends NormalizeAuto/ValidateAuto to `default_strategy`, which emits empty marker impls (traits.rs:219-226), so tuple value item validators/normalizers and tuple `ty` are dropped. Entity/Record ValidateAuto/NormalizeAuto call `field_list(def, fields)` only (validate.rs:155-248, normalize.rs:176-246) and never read `node.ty`. The icydb-model side does not reject these either (`impl ValidateNode for Type {}`). Related: field-level normalizers are applied to the whole `&mut node.field` (normalize.rs:189-195), not per element as validators are via `cardinality_wrapper`, so a normalizer on an `opt`/`many` field needs `Normalizer<Option<T>>` and fails to compile.

Set items and map keys cannot be mutated in place, so their normalizers should be rejected. Add fixtures covering each position.

Severity stays medium: the contracts (WRITE_ADMISSION.md:237-246, ATOMICITY.md:195-197) say these are app-level pre-write operations the database never runs, so this is silent loss of declared app validation, not database-invariant corruption.

`IS TRUE` / `IS FALSE` in generated CHECK predicates are lowered to `= TRUE` / `= FALSE`, which lets NULL through under the three-valued check evaluator
crates/icydb-model-macros/src/predicate.rs:422

Failure scenario

Entity with `field(name = "terms_accepted", value(opt, item(prim = "Bool")))` and `constraint(name = "must_accept", check = "terms_accepted IS TRUE")`. In SQL, `NULL IS TRUE` is FALSE, so a row with terms_accepted = NULL should be rejected. The generated check is `terms_accepted = TRUE`, which evaluates to UNKNOWN, and the write is admitted. The declared invariant is silently weakened. `IS FALSE` has the same problem. For filtered-index predicates, `x IS NOT TRUE` becomes `NOT(x = TRUE)`, which is UNKNOWN for NULL, so NULL rows are left out of the index if membership uses the same three-valued evaluator (runtime path not verified).

Evidence

parse_field_predicate: `Some(Token::Is) => ... Some(Token::Literal(Literal::Bool(value))) => { let compare = Predicate::Compare { field, op: CompareOp::Eq, operand: Literal(Bool(value)) }; Ok(if negated { Predicate::Not(Box::new(compare)) } else { compare }) }`. index.rs:611-621 lowers this to `[Field, Literal(Bool), Equal (, Not)]`. SourceCheckInstruction documents Equal/Not as SQL three-valued (icydb-schema/src/expression.rs:118-135). The runtime `compare_values` returns `AcceptedCheckTruth::Unknown` when either side is Null, and a check violation is raised only for `== AcceptedCheckTruth::False` (icydb-core/src/db/schema/check/compile.rs:452-457, 544-549, 1067-1073).

Recommendation

Lower `x IS TRUE` to `x IS NOT NULL AND x = TRUE`, `x IS FALSE` to `x IS NOT NULL AND x = FALSE`, and the negated forms to `x IS NULL OR x <> TRUE/FALSE`, or add dedicated IsTrue/IsFalse instructions. Add a regression test that inserts NULL into an opt Bool field under `check = "f IS TRUE"`.

Verifier (confirmed): predicate.rs:421-431 lowers `f IS TRUE/FALSE` to `Compare{Eq, Bool}` and the negated form to `Not(Compare)`. index.rs:611-620 emits Field, Literal, Equal, and source_instruction_tokens is used for generated checks (node/constraint.rs:39-47 via predicate_source_expression_tokens, index.rs:571-579). bind.rs:123-136 and :298 turn Equal into AcceptedCheckCompareOpV1::Eq. compare_values returns Unknown when either side is Null (compile.rs:1067-1073), and both enforcement sites raise a violation only on `== AcceptedCheckTruth::False` (compile.rs:452-457, 544-549). validate_predicate_fields (index.rs:421-440) rejects only Many cardinality, so an opt Bool field is allowed. A NULL row under `check = "f IS TRUE"` therefore evaluates to Unknown and is admitted, whereas SQL `NULL IS TRUE` is FALSE and would be rejected. It is also misleading: CheckConstraint::new keeps the original `IS TRUE` text (constraint.rs:43-47) while the semantics are `= TRUE` under 3VL. The IS NOT TRUE-with-NULL case comes out the same in both (admitted). One nuance: the SQL frontend lowers IS TRUE the same way (icydb-core/src/db/sql/parser/projection/postfix.rs:47-66), so SQL DDL CHECK shares the bug. The macro is consistent with SQL DDL; both diverge from SQL semantics, and the fix belongs in the shared lowering. In query WHERE the two-valued predicate runtime makes `= TRUE` equal to IS TRUE (changelog 0.79), which likely explains why the shortcut was never questioned. No contract defines IS TRUE for checks. Medium stands: it silently weakens a declared integrity constraint, but only on nullable Bool fields.
mediumconfirmedmodel-schema-crates-2 · correctness · high confidence
Account treats `subaccount: None` and `Some([0;32])` as different accounts; core stores and indexes both, and text parsing collapses them
crates/icydb-schema/src/account.rs:15

Failure scenario

One ICRC client sends `{owner=alice; subaccount=null}` and another sends `{owner=alice; subaccount=opt vec{0 x32}}`; both are valid ICRC-1 encodings of the same account. Inserting both into an entity with a UNIQUE index on the Account field succeeds, giving duplicate rows for one logical account. A row stored with Some(zero) is displayed as `alice-principal`, but `WHERE acct = '<that text>'` parses to None and matches nothing; no text literal can ever select that row. A relation whose target PK is (alice, None) rejects a source that references (alice, Some(zero)).

Evidence

`#[derive(CandidType, Clone, Copy, Debug, Deserialize, Eq, Hash, PartialEq, Serialize)] pub struct Account { owner, subaccount: Option<Subaccount> }` compares structurally, and ordering_tag (l.63-70) sets TAG_SUBACCOUNT whenever the subaccount is Some. Upstream icrc_ledger_types::Account (the type this wraps) implements Eq/Ord/Hash via effective_subaccount(), so None and the default all-zero subaccount are the same account, as ICRC-1 specifies. Display (l.71-75) prints Some([0;32]) as the bare principal, and FromStr (l.101-109) parses the bare principal as None; upstream FromStr rejects an explicit default subaccount (DefaultSubaccountShouldBeOmitted). Core writes the tag bit into stored bytes (icydb-core types/account.rs ~l.95-101) and index keys (index/key/ordered/segments.rs l.30-41), admission does not canonicalize (enum_catalog/admission.rs l.414-416), and SQL filter literals go through Account::from_str (schema/types.rs l.397-405).

Recommendation

Canonicalize Some(Subaccount::MIN) to None at every construction point (from_owner_and_subaccount, new, From<LedgerAccount>, Deserialize), so the atom has one representation per ICRC account, and add tests. Because this changes which bytes are produced, classify it under PERSISTED_FORMAT_POLICY as a pre-1.0 hard cut, or at least canonicalize in core admission.

Severity adjusted from high to medium during verification.
Verifier (confirmed): The code does what the finding says. Account derives structural Eq/Hash (crates/icydb-schema/src/account.rs:15), and ordering_tag sets 0x80 whenever the subaccount is Some (l.63-70). Core storage (icydb-core types/account.rs:95-101) and the index encoding (index/key/ordered/segments.rs:30-41) keep the flag, and admission passes the value through unchanged (enum_catalog/admission.rs:414-416). Upstream icrc-ledger-types 0.2.0 compares by effective_subaccount (account.rs:40-68). Its Display prints Some([0;32]) as the bare principal (l.83), and its FromStr parses a bare principal as None and rejects an explicit default subaccount (l.159-160, 174-176). So a stored Some(zero) displays as text that parses back to a different value, and a SQL text literal, which goes through Account::from_str (core schema/types.rs:397-405), can never select that row. ICRC-equivalent accounts can also coexist under a UNIQUE index. I lowered severity because the structural distinction is a deliberate, tested design choice: core types/account/tests.rs:108 asserts "None and zero subaccount must serialize differently". Eq, Ord, Hash and the byte encodings are internally consistent, and no contract defines ICRC equivalence. What remains is a real semantic mismatch with ICRC-1 plus the broken text round trip. Both are reachable, but only when clients send an explicit zero subaccount.
mediumconfirmedmodel-schema-crates-5 · correctness · high confidence
Nested relation lowering silently drops relation leaves that are reachable only through a recursive type, contradicting the authoring guide
crates/icydb-model/src/fragment.rs:359

Failure scenario

`record TreeNode { owner: rel User, children: many(indirect) TreeNode }` and `entity Doc { tree: TreeNode }`. Lowering emits only the relation `tree.owner` (depth 0). The owner of every child node is never existence-checked on insert and never restricts deletion of the User. A write with `tree.children[0].owner = <missing user>` succeeds, and deleting a user referenced only by a child leaves dangling references, even though the author declared a strong `rel` and the guide promised such a schema would be rejected.

Evidence

In collect_nested_relation_candidates: `if !visiting.insert((*path).to_string()) { // ... Stop at a recursive edge ... return Ok(()); }`. The only test (recursive_structural_type_without_a_finite_relation_path_is_ignored, l.~1737) covers a recursive type with no relation. docs/guides/schema-authoring.md (~l.170-172) says "Map keys, tuple positions, opaque payloads, recursive cycles ... are rejected"; map keys are rejected by the macro and tuples by UnsupportedCardinality, but recursion is silently accepted. Model node validation has no cycle check, and core builds relation sources only from the emitted steps (application_lowering.rs ~l.3076-3101).

Recommendation

When the recursive target still reaches a relation (item_reaches_relation on the cycle target), return a FragmentLoweringError (or a macro/validation error) instead of Ok(()). Align REF_INTEGRITY.md ('not relation sources') with the guide ('rejected'), and add a test with a relation inside a recursive type.

Verifier (confirmed): collect_nested_relation_candidates (crates/icydb-model/src/fragment.rs:359-365) returns Ok(()) when it reaches an already-visited named type. With TreeNode{owner: rel User, children: many TreeNode}, it records only `tree.owner`, and children[*].owner is never a relation source. visiting.remove (l.499) runs correctly, so only true cycles are skipped, not repeated sibling uses of a type. Nothing in the model/macros layer detects cycles, and the only test (l.1737) covers a recursive type with no relation. On whether this is intended: the code comment and the normative contract (docs/contracts/REF_INTEGRITY.md:169, "recursive value cycles ... are not relation sources"; §8 lists recursive existence validation as a non-goal) are consistent with silently not enforcing these leaves. The authoring guide, however, says such shapes "are rejected" (docs/guides/schema-authoring.md:170-172), while map keys and tuples really are rejected (l.486-489). The result is that a declared strong `rel` goes silently unenforced and can dangle. That is a real integrity footgun, even though the code matches the contract's literal wording, so medium stands.

crates/icydb-model/src/build/actor/mod.rs:39

A developer bumps `Account` to version 3 but declares `entity_migration(entity = "Account", from = 1, ...)`. Codegen and cargo build succeed. generate_with_crate_path lowers `schema_fragment_for_canister` and calls `canister.migration_plan()` separately; ActorBuilder::new (l.80-96) only encodes each one. The build path and schema_validate never call them. mediumconfirmedmodel-schema-crates-7 · correctness · high confidence
Numeric validator/normalizer constructors silently replace unrepresentable bounds with 0 (Clamp can rewrite every value to 0)
crates/icydb-model/src/base/normalizer/num.rs:24

Failure scenario

`Clamp::new(0u128, u128::MAX)` on a Nat128 field sets max to 0, so Clamp(0,0) rewrites every incoming value to 0 before the write, silently destroying data. `Gte::new(u128::MAX)` or `Gte::new(1e40_f64)` sets the target to 0, so every non-negative value passes (fail-open). `MaxDecimalPlaces::new(-1)` becomes 0 and rejects every fractional value.

Clamp::new: `let min = try_cast_decimal(&min).unwrap_or_default(); let max = try_cast_decimal(&max).unwrap_or_default();`. validator/num.rs l.11-13 `cast_decimal_cfg` does the same for Lt/Gt/Lte/Gte/Equal/NotEqual/Range/MultipleOf. MaxDecimalPlaces::new (validator/decimal.rs l.25) and RoundDecimalPlaces::new (normalizer/num.rs l.79) use `try_into().unwrap_or_default()`. Validator args admit Nat128 and Float32/Float64 (node/arg.rs l.49-62), and Decimal::from_u128/from_f64_lossy return None above i128::MAX or for |x| > ~1.7e38.

Recommendation

Make these constructors fallible, or keep an 'invalid configuration' state that reports a ctx.issue on every validate/normalize call. Better still, reject unrepresentable validator/normalizer arguments during schema validation at build time.

Verifier (confirmed): Clamp::new (crates/icydb-model/src/base/normalizer/num.rs:23-28) and cast_decimal_cfg (validator/num.rs:11-13), which feeds Lt/Gt/Lte/Gte/Equal/NotEqual/Range/MultipleOf, both use `unwrap_or_default()`. Decimal derives Default, which is ZERO (decimal/mod.rs:114). Decimal::from_u128 returns None above i128::MAX (mod.rs:212-217), and from_f64_lossy returns None for out-of-range values. The macro arg parser accepts u128 and f64 literals (icydb-model-macros arg/number.rs:104, 118-121, 135-142). So Clamp::new(0u128, u128::MAX) becomes Clamp(0,0): min<=max holds, so no error is raised, and every value is rewritten to 0. Gte::new(u128::MAX) or Gte::new(1e40) becomes target 0 and passes everything non-negative. MaxDecimalPlaces::new and RoundDecimalPlaces::new also swallow try_into failures as 0 (validator/decimal.rs:23-27, normalizer/num.rs:76-81); that case fails closed but is still wrong. These application normalizers and validators run only when the app invokes them (WRITE_ADMISSION.md:279), and the trigger needs out-of-range configuration values. Medium fits: missing validation at configuration time, with a silent data-destroying normalizer outcome.
mediumconfirmedquery-expr-9 · robustness · high confidence
REPLACE with an empty search string inserts the replacement between every character, and text functions can amplify output without being charged to the execution budget (including during plan-time folding)
crates/icydb-core/src/db/query/plan/expr/function_semantics/evaluation.rs:208

Failure scenario

`SELECT REPLACE(name, '', '-')` returns '-b-o-b-' where other engines return 'bob'. `WHERE name = REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(... REPLACE('aaaaaaaaaa','a','aaaaaaaaaa') ...)))`, nested about 10 levels, is folded during SQL lowering and tries to allocate around 10^11 bytes. The message traps on wasm OOM or the instruction limit instead of failing with a typed budget error. `REPLACE(bio, '', bio)` does the same per row, driven by stored data.

Evidence

`Value::Text(text.replace(from, to))`. Rust's str::replace("", to) inserts `to` before and after every char, whereas PostgreSQL, SQLite and MySQL return the input unchanged when the search string is empty. The output grows as |text|*|to|. Neither the runtime (projection_eval.rs:348-363, evaluate.rs:427-466) nor literal-only folding at plan time (preview.rs:397-413, called from sql/lowering/predicate/normalize.rs:43-51) charges TemporaryBytes or any other budget resource for text function results. Nesting is allowed up to depth 128, and a single literal may be up to 2 MiB (admission/input.rs:18-20).

Recommendation

Return the input unchanged when `from` is empty, matching mainstream SQL. Compute the result length (saturating) before allocating in REPLACE and in other size-changing text functions, and charge it against the request budget, or cap output size with a typed error. Apply the same check inside literal folding.

Verifier (confirmed): Two parts are confirmed. First, eval_replace_text calls str::replace (function_semantics/evaluation.rs:208), so an empty search string inserts `to` around every char, unlike mainstream SQL engines. Second, nothing in projection_eval.rs, compiled_expr/evaluate.rs or evaluation.rs charges any budget for output size. A caller can therefore amplify per row with `REPLACE(field, '' or 'e', '<~2 MiB literal>')`, since MAX_QUERY_INPUT_BYTES is 2 MiB (query/admission/input.rs:20). That traps on OOM or the instruction limit instead of returning a typed budget error. The plan-time folding scenario is wrong, though. REPLACE's first argument must be a field identifier (parse_replace_scalar_function_call uses expect_identifier, then parse_literal for the other two, functions.rs:148-156; the WHERE shape routes to the same parser; the builder is replace(field, from, to)). So nested literal-only REPLACE cannot be expressed or folded, and `REPLACE(bio, '', bio)` does not parse. What survives is unbudgeted amplification on the caller's own message plus the semantic mismatch, so medium holds.
Also reported as: xc-robustness-3
mediumconfirmedquery-intent-4 · performance · medium confidence
The AND-constraint simplifier restarts at index 0 after every operator replacement, doing caller-driven O(R*N^2) work with no metering before admission
crates/icydb-core/src/db/predicate/simplify.rs:74

Failure scenario

A caller sends about 1,200 cheap filler terms on one field (`a != 1 AND a != 2 ...`, about 3.6k input nodes, under the 4,096 cap), which the label-based canonical order places first. They add pairs `f_k >= v AND f_k <= v` on R other orderable fields, which sort after the fillers. Each pair becomes `f_k = v` through a replacement that restarts the scan over all fillers, about N^2/2 ≈ 720k pair checks per restart. With R around 30 that is about 21M unmetered pair evaluations per call, roughly 1-2B instructions by estimate, spent before the query is admitted or rejected. Entities with many orderable fields push this toward per-message instruction limits.

Evidence

The ReplaceFirst and ReplaceSecond arms set `i = 0; continue 'left;` (lines 68-86), rescanning every earlier child against every later one. `simplify_and_compare_constraints` runs inside `normalize()`, which charges nothing to PreparationWork. `normalize_query_predicate` (query/plan/access_planner.rs:73-83), called from `prepare_query_model_scalar_planning_state_with_schema_info` (query/plan/pipeline.rs:630), runs on every filtered public or trusted request, including cache hits, and before admission. RESOURCE_MODEL.md itself lists boolean normalization as not yet bounded.

Recommendation

After a replacement, re-check only the modified predicate against the others (or rerun a single linear pass) instead of restarting from 0, and charge simplification pairs to the PreparationWork budget.

Verifier (confirmed): simplify.rs:67-84 sets `i = 0; continue 'left;` on every ReplaceFirst/ReplaceSecond, which rescans all earlier Compare children against their suffix. ReplaceFirst(Eq) comes only from equal inclusive lower/upper bounds (simplify.rs:246-270), so each restart consumes one (field, coercion) domain, and R is bounded by the entity's orderable domains. normalize()/normalize_and (normalize.rs:48-68, 582-605) is pure and uncharged. It runs from normalize_query_predicate (access_planner.rs:73-85) inside prepare_query_model_scalar_planning_state_with_schema_info (pipeline.rs:616-639), before admission, on public, trusted and filtered-cache-hit paths. One correction: simplification runs on the flattened authored order before `canonicalize_predicate_children_for_eval` (normalize.rs:593-598), not after a label sort, so the caller controls child order directly and the attack is easier than described. The input cap (3 nodes per compare, 4,096 nodes, input.rs:18-19, 62-80) allows about 1,300 same-field Ne fillers, giving about 0.85M cheap pair checks per restart. Real cost depends on R: roughly 0.4B instructions for about 8 orderable domains and 1-2B for about 30, which is under IC message limits for typical schemas. RESOURCE_MODEL.md already lists boolean normalization as not yet bounded, so this is a known but real unmetered super-linear path. Medium is appropriate.

crates/icydb-core/src/db/query/plan/planner/index_select.rs:492

Secondary index on text field `name`; row name='Alice'. `WHERE name = 'Alice' AND LOWER(name) <> 'alice'` plans IndexPrefix(name='Alice'). The strict Eq clause is stripped. The casefold Ne clause is stripped because 'Alice' != 'alice' byte-wise. The residual becomes None and the 'Alice' row is returned, although casefold('Alice') == 'alice', so the correct result is empty. With IndexMultiLookup/IndexBranchSet: `WHERE status IN ('A','B') AND LOWER(status) NOT IN ('a')` keeps the 'A' rows. equality_bound_implies_required checks coercion only for the ordered/Eq family (`compare_clause_supported`). For the others: `CompareOp::Ne => !values_equal(bound.value, cmp.value(), budget)?` (line 492) and `CompareOp::NotIn => !list_contains_value(cmp.value(), bound.value, budget)?` (line 494). values_equal uses compare_numeric_or_strict_order, which is byte-strict for Text. branch_in_clause_implies_required has the same flaw (lines 530-531). A TextCasefold `Ne`/`NotIn` is valid for text fields (query/predicate/validate.rs ensure_coercion). SQL `LOWER(name) <> 'x'` compiles to `Compare(name, Ne, 'x', TextCasefold)` (plan/expr/predicate/compile.rs:414-426). The same unsound strip feeds the exact-COUNT metadata proof (pipeline.rs:401-410).

In equality_bound_implies_required and branch_in_clause_implies_required, only discharge Ne/NotIn (and In) when the clause's coercion equals the bound's equality domain (Strict or NumericWiden with numeric operands). Otherwise return false. Add residual-stripping tests covering every CompareOp x CoercionId combination, including casefold negations.

Both go through compare_numeric_or_strict_order (lines 940-953), which is byte-strict for Text. branch_in_clause_implies_required repeats this (lines 526-532). A casefold Ne on a text field passes validation (query/predicate/validate.rs:431). The generated handler at crates/icydb-model/src/build/actor/db/schema.rs:42-47 builds one Vec holding a full EntitySchemaDescription for every entity. The only reply-size guard is `into_deliverable_query_reply` (crates/icydb/src/db/sql/types.rs:27,116-131), and only the icydb_query handler calls it (crates/icydb-model/src/build/actor/db/sql.rs:159-164). rg finds no schema-endpoint equivalent. docs/changelog/0.224.md:26-40 limits the 0.224.1 fix to icydb_query, and nothing in docs/contracts/READ_ADMISSION.md:148-160 or the guides accepts or bounds the size of the icydb_schema reply, so I found no documented intent that refutes this. On reachability: the repo's own fixture (describe.rs:2794-2854) is a valid accepted snapshot of 310,865 B, under the 512 KiB limit. Its compact DESCRIBE encodes to 3,693,116 B, over 3 MiB (describe.rs:2709-2733). The verbose rows that icydb_schema returns are smaller per nested leaf: the name is the short tree marker '├─ aa' (describe.rs:1791-1823), not the 131-byte canonical path the compact form uses. It still comes to roughly 0.8-0.9 MB of nested rows plus 95 fully expanded composite kind strings of about 2.5-5 KB each (describe.rs:2188-2200, 1887-1904), about 1.1-1.4 MB per entity. Three or four entities that share the record type go over 3 MiB. MAX_SCHEMA_PROPOSAL_BYTES = 2 MiB and MAX_FRAGMENT_ENTITIES = 1024 (crates/icydb-schema/src/bounds.rs:7,31) also allow a large ordinary schema to get there. The CLI's load_schema_report (crates/icydb-cli/src/observability/schema.rs:48-63) then gets a replica reject instead of a typed error. One small correction: the trap comes from msg_reply_data_append going over the reply limit, not from msg_reply itself. I kept the severity at medium. The endpoint is query-only, so nothing changes state and the canister is not wedged; icydb_query and the typed/dynamic endpoints keep working. The trap depends on how big the accepted schema is, not on caller input. It is a missing bound that permanently disables one diagnostic endpoint for a large valid schema.

Derived-cardinality inconsistency aborts the authoritative journal fold (STORE_CORRUPTION, terminal), although the 0.230 contract says it only makes evidence unavailable
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/store.rs:1365

Failure scenario

Any drift between durable counts and the canonical index turns optional metadata into a permanent wedge of the authoritative row fold. The concrete trigger is the migration materialized fold above, followed by an ordinary delete. Likewise, if the IndexPrefixCardinalityDelta is ever invalidated (a decode failure in counted_prefixes, or IndexStore::clear), every later fold of that store fails preflight with STORE_CORRUPTION. Recovery then stops even though rows and indexes are intact.

Evidence

prepare_cardinality_maintenance maps count underflow to store_corruption (schema/store.rs:1358-1365). A generation-identity mismatch also becomes store_corruption (1310-1313). In fold_selected_journal_head the maintenance preflight and the prefix-delta watermark preflight (index/store.rs:545-552, which fails whenever the delta was invalidated) are both hard `?` failures of the fold (commit/recovery.rs:998-1008). A failed maintenance apply traps (commit/recovery.rs:1042-1047). Fold failures become persisted terminal startup receipts (startup/driver.rs:66, 210-236; startup/mod.rs:116-124). The design says the opposite: '...impossible removals, unknown index identity, or count underflow make the current candidate unavailable and produce owner-local integrity evidence' and 'underflow ... returns no cardinality evidence to the planner' (docs/design/archive/0.230-durable-exact-cardinality-generations/0.230-design.md:158-161, 197-203). The driver's own comment says malformed derived evidence must not change readiness (startup/driver.rs:72-74).

Recommendation

Treat maintenance preflight failures (underflow, identity mismatch, invalid or unbound prefix delta) as 'evidence unavailable'. Skip maintenance so the header's watermark goes stale, or restart the generation in the same message, and record integrity evidence. Keep hard failures only for row/index authority. Add a test that corrupts one count record and asserts the fold still completes and counts become None.

Verifier (confirmed): The code does what the finding says. prepare_cardinality_maintenance maps count underflow to store_corruption (schema/store.rs:1358-1365), and a record-identity mismatch as well (1310-1313). In fold_selected_journal_head both the maintenance preflight and preflight_prefix_cardinality_delta_watermark are hard `?` failures (commit/recovery.rs:998-1008). The watermark preflight requires an exact delta watermark (index/store.rs:545-552), and it runs even when no Ready header exists. A failed maintenance apply traps (1042-1047). Fold errors become terminal JournalRecovery receipts (startup/driver.rs:66, 210-236; startup/mod.rs:116-124). The design says the opposite. 0.230-design.md:158-161 and 197-203 say underflow makes evidence unavailable, and 0.230-status.md:612-614 says impossible volatile evidence 'becomes unavailable'. Caveats: the driver.rs:72-74 comment covers optional construction pages, not fold maintenance. Without finding 1, the only triggers are genuine corruption. Delta invalidation needs a malformed index key/value in counted_prefixes (index/cardinality.rs:862-884) or i64 overflow. IndexStore::clear has no production callers I could find. The closeout audit also accepted this preflight shape (0.230-closeout-audit.md:233). So this is an amplifier rather than an independent trigger: it turns derived-metadata drift into a permanent wedge of authoritative recovery. Medium fits.

crates/icydb-core/src/db/executor/projection/covering/pure.rs:196

Failure scenario

Entity Order { id (pk), tenant_id: Nat64, created_at: Timestamp } with index (tenant_id, created_at). `SELECT id, created_at FROM Order WHERE tenant_id = 7` (a tenant with, say, 20k orders) plans a pure covering read: id is PrimaryKey and created_at is IndexComponent{1}. Execution walks all 20k index entries, allocates a DecodedDataStoreKey plus a component Vec for each, then fails to decode the Timestamp tag on row 1 and discards everything. The scalar path then walks the same 20k entries and loads the 20k rows. The index work and its budget charges roughly double on every execution, so on IC a query that fits the hard execution budget or instruction limit when run once can fail or run twice as slowly. Operators reading EXPLAIN are told it is a covering read.

Evidence

The planner admits pure covering plans whose components cannot be decoded (no kind gate at covering/mod.rs:965-976). At execution, resolve_index_backed_covering_scan collects every matching index entry into raw_pairs. The scan limit is usize::MAX unless the page window is allowed, which requires ProvenByPlanner and an IndexOrder or PK-safe order (shared.rs:159-165, 177-203, 349-365). Only afterwards do decode_single_covering_projection_pairs and decode_covering_projection_pairs decode the first row; Ok(None) aborts with return Ok(None) (pure.rs:196-205, 264-273; covering.rs:1067-1081). The facade then runs the full scalar path (facade.rs:293-453). Both attempts run inside one with_read_execution_budget scope (facade.rs:181), so the index traversal, decoded-bytes charges and buffered memory of the discarded attempt all count against the hard budget. Only the streaming bounded-range path (pure.rs:325-381) stops at the first row. EXPLAIN also reports these shapes as pure_covering/covering_read (explain/descriptor/load.rs:233-235, 772-783) although the covering route can never produce their output.

Recommendation

Decide decodability at plan time: reject IndexComponent sources whose accepted kind is not one of the tags decode supports, so these queries go straight to the scalar path and EXPLAIN tells the truth. Alternatively, decode lazily per chunk (streaming, as the bounded-range path already does) so an unsupported tag aborts before the range is materialized, or add decoders for the remaining canonical encodings.

Verifier (confirmed): Reproduced from code. The pure plan has no kind gate (query/plan/covering/mod.rs:965-976). pure.rs:84-105 calls resolve_index_backed_covering_scan, which collects rows eagerly through resolve_covering_projection_components_from_lowered_specs (shared.rs:176-203; covering.rs:98-150). The scan limit is usize::MAX unless page_window_allowed_for_route holds, and that requires ProvenByPlanner (shared.rs:163-169, 349-365). Each entry charges DecodedBytes and allocates a component Vec plus a DecodedDataStoreKey (stream/access/scan.rs:1051-1087). Decoding only happens afterwards, in decode_single_covering_projection_pairs / decode_covering_projection_pairs (pure.rs:196-205, 264-273). The first unsupported tag returns Ok(None) and the buffered rows are thrown away. Hybrid does not apply when every projected field is PK or a component (mod.rs:769-775), so the facade drops to the scalar path (facade.rs:293+), still inside the same with_read_execution_budget scope (facade.rs:181; budget.rs:636-651). The scalar path scans the index again. EXPLAIN still labels the query pure_covering (explain/descriptor/load.rs:232-235, 772-782). The bounded-range streaming path (pure.rs:325-381) stops at row one, as the finding says. The impact is overstated in one place: only the index-traversal part doubles, and the scalar path's row loads dominate, so 'twice as slowly' is too strong. Results are correct. The only failure is budget or instruction exhaustion near the limit. That makes it a latent cost hazard with the same root cause as finding 1, and medium is justified.
mediumconfirmedr2-cross-message-concurrency-3 · robustness · medium confidence
A Building cardinality generation restarts on every journal fold, so it never finishes on large, busy stores; the watchdog runs forever and later stores never get a build
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/cardinality_build.rs:353

Failure scenario

Take a store with 1M rows and two 2-component indexes: about 245 row pages plus about 245 index pages plus clearing pages, all needing consecutive ticks with no fold in between. After any DDL, activation start or promotion, or schema application in that store, the Ready generation becomes stale. If the app writes more often than roughly once per build duration (minutes), every write's fold changes the watermark, and the next page restarts from a cleared slot. The build never reaches Ready. The watchdog never becomes quiescent and spends a scan page every tick for as long as the canister runs. Stores whose path sorts after the busy store never get a cardinality page at all. Planner cardinality evidence (cardinality_tiebreak) is lost permanently. The window in round 1's schema-application-1 (missing cardinality treated as corruption during a later upgrade) becomes unbounded instead of lasting minutes.

Evidence

The build's source identity includes the store-level fold watermark (cardinality_generation.rs:353-355). drive_cardinality_generation_page restarts on the other slot whenever the source differs, and restart_cardinality_generation deletes the build cursor, so all progress is lost (cardinality_build.rs:353-358, 374-382; schema/store.rs:1084-1098). Folds keep only Ready generations up to date (commit/recovery.rs:1076-1080), not Building ones. The watchdog builds cardinality only when the tail is empty, one page per tick. Page limits are 4,096 source entries, 16 MiB, or 16,384 prefix updates (cardinality_build.rs:36-39). drive_cardinality_page returns Recovering at the first store that is not Quiescent (startup/driver.rs:80-103), and the generated callback maps Recovering to ContinueImmediately (crates/icydb-model/src/build/actor/db/store.rs:276-283). Any accepted-schema publication in the store invalidates a Ready generation (recovery.rs:1103-1110), which forces a rebuild.

Recommendation

Maintain a Building generation across folds as fold maintenance already does for Ready ones: apply each folded batch's count deltas to entries behind the build checkpoint, and move the recorded watermark instead of restarting. Alternatively, restart only on root, index-set, allocation or incarnation changes. Also iterate stores round-robin so one busy store cannot starve the rest, and back off the watchdog after repeated restarts.

Verifier (confirmed): The code matches the finding. The source identity includes fold_watermark (cardinality_generation.rs:353-355). drive_cardinality_generation_page restarts on any source mismatch (cardinality_build.rs:354-358, 378-382, 393-398). restart_cardinality_generation switches to the alternate slot and removes the build cursor, so all progress is lost and the new slot must be cleared again (schema/store.rs:1073-1099). Folds maintain only Ready generations: prepare_folded_cardinality_maintenance returns None unless the header is Ready and its source validates (recovery.rs:1077-1080). A Building header is never carried forward, so every fold makes the next page restart. The watchdog runs a cardinality page only after the tail is empty (startup/driver.rs:52-61) and stops at the first non-Quiescent store in sorted order (driver.rs:80-103). Recovering maps to ContinueImmediately (icydb-model build/actor/db/store.rs:276-283). Schema publication batches skip maintenance (recovery.rs:1059-1063, 1103-1110), so any DDL or schema application forces a rebuild. Restarting on watermark drift is itself intended: the 0.230 design says a Building candidate restarts on source or watermark drift, that writes may continue, and that the evidence is optional for correctness (docs/design/archive/0.230-durable-exact-cardinality-generations/0.230-design.md:167-178, 0.230-status.md:204). The design does not address liveness, though. Under steady writes (more often than one every few hundred ticks) on a large store, the build never publishes and the watchdog runs a page every round indefinitely. Later-sorted stores are starved permanently, and planner tiebreak evidence stays unavailable. The impact is performance and cycles, plus starvation of optional evidence; correctness falls back to the planner. The link to round 1's schema-application-1 depends on that finding and I did not re-verify it. Medium is appropriate.

crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/snapshot.rs:1261

Failure scenario

The model declares `index(fields=["customer_id"], predicate = "billing_country = shipping_country")`, persisted as `billing_country = shipping_country`. An operator runs `ALTER TABLE Order ADD COLUMN note text ...` and later `ALTER TABLE Order RENAME COLUMN note TO memo`. The rename also rewrites the unrelated generated index predicate to `shipping_country = billing_country`, and it passes acceptance. The next deploy that changes the generated schema fragment anywhere runs lower_existing_indexes. It re-renders `billing_country = shipping_country`, finds it unequal to the accepted text, returns store_unsupported, and records a startup failure, so the database never becomes Ready on the new release. SQL cannot repair it: renaming back re-renders in canonical order again, and DROP INDEX rejects generated indexes. The only options are rolling back the wasm or rewriting the model predicate in descending operand order. The same divergence makes the migration planner reject any metadata-only field rename on that entity, even an unrelated one, as UnexplainedSchemaDifference: relabel_index_for_fields re-renders every predicate (migration_planner.rs:1285-1310) and compares text at :1212-1216 and :1323. This is a different trigger from the chained/swapped renames in xc-architecture-2.

Generated index predicates are persisted as render_accepted_check_expr_sql output (application_lowering.rs:2888-2902, 2055-2068). That renderer emits a Compare in authored operand order: check/render.rs:46-52 renders `{left} {op} {right}`, bind_compare keeps field/field order (check/bind.rs:686-694), and the macro emits Field(left), Field(right), Equal (icydb-model-macros/src/node/index.rs:612-622). The predicate parser instead canonicalizes symmetric field compares so that the lexicographically greater name is on the left: CompareFieldsPredicate::with_coercion calls canonicalize_symmetric_fields for Eq/Ne (predicate/model.rs:433-443, 460). The parser path goes through predicate_compare_fields (parser/lowering.rs:119-134, plain/compare.rs:21), rewrite_field_identifiers re-canonicalizes (predicate/rewrite.rs:84-97), and render.rs:77-82 emits the canonical order. clone_with_renamed_field_path_root re-renders every predicate unconditionally (snapshot.rs:1261-1268), including predicates that do not reference the renamed field. derive_sql_ddl_field_rename_persisted_after applies it to ALL indexes, generated ones included (mutation/field.rs:832-843). The rename publication check only compares the result against the same derivation (sql_ddl/field_metadata.rs:383-405). Generated application re-lowers every generated index of every entity in the proposal (application_lowering.rs:824-846, 1882-1936) and requires `before == *accepted` with exact predicate_sql, otherwise store_unsupported (application_lowering.rs:1922-1923). The submission key hashes the fragment (icydb-model/src/build/actor/mod.rs:88-99), so any schema change bypasses the receipt short-circuit (application.rs:665). A failure is recorded as a generated schema startup failure and ordinary database work stays refused (icydb-model/src/build/actor/db/store.rs:341-352, 117-126).

Recommendation

Stop rewriting predicates that do not reference the renamed field, and never re-render generated-index text in the DDL path. Generated indexes cannot reference DDL-owned fields, so skip them in derive_sql_ddl_field_rename_persisted_after. Make reconciliation and the planner compare normalized predicate semantics (normalized_accepted_index_predicate) instead of strings, or have both renderers share one canonical operand order. The structural fix is still the field-ID-bound predicate tree recommended in xc-architecture-1. Add a test: a generated filtered index with `a = b`, then DDL ADD and RENAME of an extension column, then re-apply a changed generated fragment.

mediumconfirmedr2-query-call-caches-2 · performance · medium confidence
Folding a schema batch after C1 was rebuilt leaves the store bundle cache empty; C1 hits never refill it, so admitted-root cardinality evidence is silently unavailable and query calls re-decode the bundle
crates/icydb-core/src/db/schema/cardinality_build.rs:145

Failure scenario

A journaled store has a Ready cardinality generation. A controller runs SQL DDL, for example CREATE INDEX, in an update call. Before the watchdog folds that schema batch, some update-mode database call happens: a write, a mutation-job advance, an application timer, or an update-mode read. That call compiles C1 for the new root, which refills C2. The watchdog then folds the schema batch, which drops C2. Folding any later batches completes convergence, and the Ready-branch warm hits C1, so C2 stays empty. Once the cardinality generation rebuild publishes Ready, reads on that store in both query and update calls see no admitted-root evidence. Tie-breaks keep the policy index choice, which can mean a low-selectivity scan and ExecutionBudgetExceeded where the cardinality choice would have succeeded. Exact intersections fall back. Single-prefix covering and liveness proofs decode and verify the full bundle in every query call. This lasts until a write, or an update-mode Current-source read, on that store reloads the bundle. For read-mostly canisters that can be a long time.

Evidence

derive_for_admitted_consumer_root uses only schema.cached_cardinality_domain_for_root. If C2 is empty it returns Ok(None) (cardinality_build.rs:138-147, schema/store.rs:4032-4043), and ready_cardinality_counts_for_source then reports no counts (registry/handle.rs:1015-1031). C2 is refilled only by accepted_schema_authority_ref_for_selection (store.rs:3940-3976). A C1 hit returns before touching any schema-store bundle (session/accepted_schema.rs:436-445), and the watchdog's Ready branch only performs that C1 lookup plus canonical-only cardinality derives (driver.rs:56, 85-96; cardinality_build.rs:92-99). The online fold of a schema-publication batch drops C2: apply_online_batch_retirement leads to apply_prepared_journal_batch_retirement, which calls invalidate_accepted_bundle_cache_for_key on the root key (recovery.rs:1016, 1335-1336; store.rs:2092-2100, 3510-3513). The effective root bytes do not change, so C1 keeps hitting. The consumers that degrade: cardinality tie-break returns Unavailable (session/query/cardinality_tiebreak.rs:184-195), exact index intersection takes ConservativeFallback (executor/stream/access/traversal.rs:421-428), and the multi-prefix covering synchronized_generation check becomes false (executor/projection/covering/shared.rs:236-252). Current-source consumers instead go through derive_for_current_consumer and accepted_cardinality_domain_for_selection, which re-decode and verify the whole effective bundle on each miss (cardinality_build.rs:111-121, store.rs:3995-4018). That work is discarded in every query call.

Recommendation

Have AcceptedSchemaRuntimeRoot retain each store's CardinalityAcceptedDomain (derived once during compile) and serve admitted-root consumers from the captured root rather than from C2. Alternatively, have the watchdog's Ready branch refill C2 for every store (for example via accepted_cardinality_domain_for_selection on the current root) whenever it runs. Add a regression test for the sequence DDL, update-mode read, schema-batch fold, then tie-break.

(2) C2 is filled only by accepted_schema_authority_ref_for_selection (store.rs:3922-3976), reached through current_accepted_catalog_selection, borrow_accepted_schema_bundle_for_authority, current_accepted_schema_bundle and accepted_cardinality_domain_for_selection. (3) A C1 hit returns before any schema-store bundle access (session/accepted_schema.rs:426-445). The C1 key is the effective store roots (accepted_schema.rs:408-424), and those are unchanged when a schema batch folds, so C1 keeps hitting. (4) Folding a root key drops C2 through insert_canonical_raw_value (store.rs:3474-3479) and through Exact overlay retirement (store.rs:2092-2100). invalidate_accepted_bundle_cache_for_key clears the cache on any accepted-root key write, whether or not the value changed (store.rs:3510-3513). (5) The watchdog Ready branch does only the C1 lookup (driver.rs:56) and canonical-only CardinalityBuildAuthority::derive (driver.rs:85-96; cardinality_build.rs:99), so it never refills C2. (6) The precondition is realistic. SQL DDL invalidates C1 (session/sql/ddl.rs:248 etc.), and any update-mode C1 compile before the fold refills C2 through AcceptedSchemaEntityRuntime::compile, which calls current_accepted_catalog_selection (accepted_schema.rs:44-60). The fold then drops C2 while C1 stays valid. Planning-time tie-break consults the Admitted source before any Current consumer could refill C2 in the same call, so tie-break evidence is reliably missing in query calls. Execution-time Admitted consumers (index_prefix_cardinality.rs:155-210) are affected only when no Current consumer ran earlier in the same call. The effect ends at the next write (session/write.rs:753) or update-mode Current-source read on that store. All consequences are conservative fallbacks or repeated bundle decodes in query calls, not wrong results, so medium (edge-condition cache-coherence bug that loses the warm cache the driver comment at driver.rs:54-55 intends) is appropriate.

crates/icydb-core/src/db/data/structural_field/value_storage/walk.rs:26

record Node { label: Text, children: List<Node> }; entity Doc { id: Nat64, tree: Node }. Insert a Doc whose tree is a 17-node single-child chain. Admission and canonical encode accept it: the deepest member sits at absolute depth 33 < 64, and `SELECT tree FROM Doc` decodes it. `SELECT tree.children FROM Doc` resolves the children list with ValueStorageView and then calls decode_structural_value_storage_bytes on it. The list/map walkers increment it again (walk.rs:26, walk.rs:58), then call decode_value_storage_binary_value_at for each item, which increments once more (decode/cursor.rs:50). A value at relative level k is therefore checked at 2k against MAX_VALUE_STORAGE_DECODE_DEPTH=64 (value_storage/mod.rs:15-23), which caps materialization at 32 levels. The canonical encoder and admission allow 64 (canonical.rs:57, admission.rs:412). Type inference admits Collection/Structured member paths (query/plan/expr/type_inference/source.rs:33-58, :111-112). No test covers this decoder's depth.

Better, route field-path leaf materialization through decode_canonical_value_storage_bytes plus admission so one codec owns the depth rule. Add a boundary test: depth 63 accepted, depth 64 rejected, for every decoder that reads canonical bytes.

The grouped single-path consumer (grouped.rs:453) is labelled scalar-path, so the projection path is the stronger case.
